rows.label: PPI-over-UPI MDR implementation
rows.why: Management expects payments revenue to follow GMV once PPI-over-UPI MDR is implemented, but it has not yet been implemented and payments revenue has been flat for 4-5 quarters.

rows.label: Debt-free status and working capital lines
rows.why: Long-term debt fully repaid; remaining INR 261 crore working capital lines against INR 434 crore net owned unencumbered cash, with part of cash still IPO proceeds to be drawn down.

rows.label: Merchant breakeven by FY28
rows.why: Offline and Zaakpay merchant businesses guided to EBITDA breakeven by FY28, with merchant investment of about INR 55 crore per year continuing for at least 18 months.

tone.note: Management was confident on the profitability turnaround and growth-engine narrative but evasive on payments revenue growth, merchant-breakeven timing and NBFC scale; analysts pressed on the UPI GMV vs flat revenue gap, merchant breakeven timing and NBFC rollout.

544305|2026-06.headline: MobiKwik posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR76 million, its third straight profitable quarter, with payments GMV up 50% YoY to INR587 billion.
544305|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as its most profitable quarter yet, with PAT of INR76 million and EBITDA of INR158 million, up INR470 million YoY. Payments gross profit rose 31% YoY to INR777 million and financial services gross profit grew 5.6x to INR433 million. Lending disbursements dipped in Q1, while payments revenue fell as card-linked categories were paused under regulatory pressure and UPI (near-zero take rate) grew. Management targets full-year PAT of about INR400 million and EBITDA of about INR750 million including other income, and is scaling a merchant acquiring business that is still loss-making.

financial_highlights.change: Swing of INR495 million vs Q1 FY26; up from INR45 million in Q4 per management
+50% YoY; 14th straight quarter of payments GMV growth

segments.name: Payments
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR777 million (+31% YoY) on revenue of about INR208 crore versus INR59 crore a year ago on similar revenue; net payments take rate 13-15 bps in recent quarters, guided at 12-14 bps long term. Zaakpay (payment gateway) GMV INR25.6 billion; revenue not disclosed.

segments.name: Financial services (lending)
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR433 million (5.6x YoY). Net financial services margin 4.1% in Q3, 5.4% in Q4 and 5.9% in Q1; management guides 4.5-5.5% long term. About 18% of gross lending revenue came from write-backs on past books (about INR16 crore).

segments.name: Merchant (Zaakpay online + offline acquiring)
segments.commentary: Merchant GMV INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ. Business is loss-making with an expected full-year burn of INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted for FY28. Management expects 10x ramp over two years.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 PAT target of about INR40 crore (INR400 million) and EBITDA of about INR75 crore (INR750 million) including other income; management said it is 'fairly confident'.
Lending disbursements to rise from about INR700 crore per quarter to INR1,000 crore per quarter; management says Q2 is already running at that rate.
Consumer payments revenue expected to grow 5-6% QoQ; merchant revenue expected to grow about 25% QoQ.
Merchant business burn for FY27 capped at INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted in FY28.
Long-term net payments take rate guided at 12-14 bps; net financial services margin guided at 4.5-5.5%.
Paused card-linked payment categories expected to be relaunched in Q2 FY27.
Digital lending business transfer to wholly-owned subsidiary expected to close in August 2026; own NBFC launch still 'some time away'.
capex_capacity: About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains available for buying more merchant devices (soundboxes, EDC, QR); management does not expect more than this needed for FY27.
Merchant ramp: 10x over two years targeted; merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue not disclosed yet.
Employee benefit expense rose from INR46 crore in Q4 to INR53 crore in Q1, mostly merchant business manpower; expected to rise 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.
Lending partner base: nine major NBFC partners in Q1 (10-15 total); top-three lender concentration cut from about 91% (Q2-Q3 FY26) to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1.
demand_pricing: Payments revenue dipped because high-take-rate card-linked categories (credit and debit) were paused, while low or zero take-rate UPI and merchant volumes grew; management attributes the pause to regulatory guardrail changes on categories such as rent and education.
Wallet transactions up 68% YoY but GMV up only 24%, as users shift to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments on which no PPI MDR is earned.

UPI: MobiKwik's transactions grew 5x faster than the industry; ranked 13th in NPCI UPI stack rankings and described as second fastest-growing TPAP. No MDR on UPI; PPI-on-UPI MDR mandated by RBI but not rolled out by NPCI.

Lending: Q1 disbursements dipped; 60% of loans went to repeat customers and credit quality improved 25%. Cross-sell from about 96 million engaged non-lending users targeted at INR150-250 crore extra disbursement per quarter; AI funnel engine targeted at about INR100 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why has quarterly revenue growth been muted over the last seven to eight quarters, and what levers will accelerate it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was spent re-stabilising businesses and Q1 is the baseline. Lending disbursements are to rise from about INR700 crore to INR1,000 crore per quarter via new lending partners, pre-approved offers to about 96 million engaged users, and an AI funnel engine. Card-linked categories were paused in Q4 and Q1 and are to be relaunched, while merchant revenue is to scale.

qa_highlights.question: Non-UPI GMV trend and whether take rate is falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-UPI GMV rose to INR317 billion from INR300 billion in Q4 (about 6%). Management said card-linked categories with higher take rates de-grew under regulatory pressure. Net payments take rate guidance remains 12-14 bps long term, at gross profit level, versus 13-15 bps in recent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant roll-out: what numbers and how should it be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant GMV was INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ from INR107 billion. Management targets a 10x ramp over two years, expects merchant revenue to grow about 25% QoQ and consumer payments revenue 5-6% QoQ. Merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue were withheld as too early. About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains for devices, and no more is expected to be needed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Own NBFC timing and FLDG share of lending?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital lending transfer to a wholly-owned subsidiary is expected to close in August 2026 after shareholder approval on 2 July, then CoR will be sought; own NBFC lending is 'still some time away'. As of Q1, 32% of lending was pure distribution and 68% FLDG, with a possible 40/60 mix by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of INR750 million EBITDA and INR400 million PAT still valid after Q1 operating EBITDA ex other income of about INR80 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident in the baseline and expects about INR400 million PAT for FY27 with some growth, plus about INR750 million EBITDA including other income. Q1 PAT of INR76 million annualises to about INR302 million, and improving by INR20-30 million per quarter would reach about INR400 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lending disbursements fall in Q1, and what is the top-three lender concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-three lender concentration was cut from about 91% in Q2-Q3 FY26 to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1, with two new partners added in Q1. Management said the digital lending transfer to the subsidiary consumed focus in Q1, and it is already at the INR1,000 crore run rate in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wallet transactions grow 68% but GMV only 24%, and is PPI-on-UPI monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Users shifted to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments and card-linked pauses removed high-ticket transactions. No MDR is earned on PPI-on-UPI although RBI mandated it; NPCI has not rolled it out in about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant business burn, breakeven timing and employee cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant burn for FY27 is capped at INR50-60 crore (about INR15-16 crore in Q1); breakeven targeted for FY28. Employee benefit expense rose to INR53 crore from INR46 crore in Q4, and merchant-related manpower cost may grow 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.

risks_watch: Payments revenue dip from paused card-linked categories (credit and debit, rent, education); relaunch targeted for Q2 FY27 and not yet proven.
Lending disbursements fell in Q1; Q2 INR1,000 crore run rate depends on the digital lending transfer closing in August 2026 without disruption.
Gross take-rate compression as UPI (near-zero take rate) and merchant volumes grow; net payments take rate guided at 12-14 bps long term versus 13-15 bps recently.
Net financial services margin of 5.9% in Q1 includes write-backs (about 18% of gross lending revenue); management guides 4.5-5.5% long term.
Merchant business still loss-making (FY27 burn INR50-60 crore); merchant revenue, device and merchant counts not disclosed; breakeven FY28.
Regulatory dependence: PPI-on-UPI MDR mandated by RBI but not rolled out by NPCI; no timeline given.
Own NBFC launch still 'some time away'; CoR pending until digital lending transfer completes.
Q1 PAT of INR76 million rests on one quarter; full-year PAT of about INR400 million requires sustained sequential improvement of about INR20-30 million per quarter.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 has been our most successful and profitable quarter yet.
We are targeting full-year PAT profitability for this financial year, and Q1 is of course the baseline.
So yes, INR75 crores EBITDA and INR40 crores PAT is the kind of numbers that we are fairly confident of achieving.
It's too early. Apart from the GMV for merchant, we are not revealing any other numbers yet.
544305|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability and guidance, with a repeated 'fairly confident' stance on FY27 PAT and EBITDA targets. Cautious and evasive on merchant metrics (no merchant counts, devices or revenue, calling it 'too early'), on regulatory issues around UPI MDR (expressed frustration), and on the timing of its own NBFC.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 PAT INR76m vs INR45m in Q4 and management targets FY27 PAT ~INR400m, needing ~INR20-30m sequential improvement per quarter; but the Q1 net financial services margin of 5.9% includes write-backs (~18% of gross lending revenue) and guidance is 4.5-5.5% long term, so the margin lift is not clean.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Merchant device capacity is funded by ~INR25 crore of remaining IPO proceeds, and management does not expect more than this to be needed in FY27; no new plants or lines are discussed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Platform GMV up 50% YoY to INR587bn, merchant GMV up 17% QoQ, and lending disbursements guided from ~INR700 crore to INR1,000 crore per quarter with Q2 already at that rate; payments volume is strong but card-linked categories are paused and relaunch is not yet proven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond the ~INR25 crore of residual IPO-funded merchant devices; utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is 'fairly confident' of FY27 PAT ~INR400m and EBITDA ~INR750m but Q1 annualises to only ~INR302m PAT, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 PAT of INR76m annualises to ~INR302m versus the INR400m target; the target needs INR20-30m of quarterly improvement, and the lending transfer must close in August 2026 without disruption to hit the INR1,000 crore disbursement run rate.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Paused card-linked payment categories are expected to be relaunched in Q2 FY27, and the AI funnel engine is targeted at ~INR100 crore per quarter of disbursement; relaunch not yet proven.

rows.label: Digital lending transfer to wholly-owned subsidiary
rows.why: Shareholder approval was given on 2 July and closing is expected in August 2026, after which CoR will be sought; own NBFC lending is still 'some time away'.

rows.label: Cross-sell to ~96m engaged non-lending users
rows.why: Management targets INR150-250 crore extra disbursement per quarter from cross-sell, with 60% of Q1 loans going to repeat customers, but no conversion data has been disclosed yet.

rows.label: PPI-on-UPI MDR rollout by NPCI
rows.why: RBI mandated the PPI-on-UPI MDR but NPCI has not rolled it out in about 2.5 years and gave no timeline, so there is no visible monetisation in the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 PAT of ~INR400m and EBITDA of ~INR750m and the INR1,000 crore lending run rate, but cautious and evasive on merchant counts, devices and revenue, UPI MDR, and NBFC timing; analysts pushed on the sustainability of the Q1 profit and the falling lending disbursements.

544306|2026-06.headline: Sai Life Sciences Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR553 crore, with CRO up 26% and CDMO up 6%; management guides to a stronger H2.
544306|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR553 crore against INR496 crore a year earlier, up about 12% YoY. CRO (about 40% of revenue) grew about 26% YoY, while CDMO (about 60%) grew about 6%. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations and reiterated a stronger H2 as new capacity comes online, with the Discovery facility already commissioned and sold out and Bidar production block 1 due in H2/Q3. Management reaffirmed the mid-term revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA margin of 28-30%, and FY27 capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore.

financial_highlights.change: about +12% YoY vs INR496 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: CRO / Discovery
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 26% YoY. About 65% of customers now use integrated discovery services, mainly biotech; a pilot with a large pharma converted to a long-term high-volume discovery chemistry partnership. Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 and is already sold out.

segments.name: CDMO / CMC
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 6% YoY, described as lumpy. Portfolio is 33 active commercial molecules and 14 late-phase molecules. Three of the four commercial contracts expected this year were added in Q1; management said three are commercial supplies, primary supplier in about two of three (anecdotal).

guidance_outlook: Mid-term (3-5 year) revenue growth guidance of 15-20% reiterated; management said guidance should be viewed over a longer horizon, not quarterly.
EBITDA margin range of 28-30% reiterated.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with capacity coming on stream by end-Q2 or early Q3; management referenced a 40/60 historical H1/H2 split, with FY26 at about 48/52.
FY27 capex guidance INR1,100-1,300 crore unchanged; no FY28 capex guidance yet.
Target of about 1,150 KL capacity by FY27 reconfirmed.
Expects to convert at least two large pharma customers to integrated models in FY27.
Formulation (oral solids up to Phase 2) expected to be operational in about six months, within the current fiscal year.
capex_capacity: Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 FY27 and is sold out, ahead of the one-to-1.5-year fill timeline management had assumed.
Bidar: two production blocks of 225 KL each (450 KL total); first block due for completion and operation in H2/Q3 FY27, on track.
First dedicated peptide development lab coming online shortly for a top-tier pharma company; GMP pilot-scale peptide facility coming online soon for clinical supply.
Commercial peptide manufacturing at a new greenfield site near Hyderabad expected to be operational in 2028; groundbreaking planned. Peptide spend to end-2028 likely below INR300 crore.
XDC Center of Excellence close to opening; ADC pilot-scale space under build.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian outsourcing demand is strengthened by geopolitical concerns and IP worries, with customers using India for diversification.

FTE (dedicated team) model: one top-tier pharma FTE relationship expanded from small scale to a sizable dedicated contract running end-to-end from discovery to commercial; another large pharma process development FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2, with work from Q3.

Pipeline sourced via three routes: biotech molecules acquired by pharma partners, molecules transferred from acquirers, and FTE-led progression. Five of six late-phase molecules added in 15 months came via large pharma FTE relationships.
Phase 3 pipeline: one customer approved in FY26, two more with regulatory milestones in FY27, one expected Q2 FY28.
Modalities: about 4-5% of revenue from new modalities, all in development and discovery, none in commercial. Peptide work is mainly early-stage discovery.
Sai works with 19 of the top 25 pharma companies. Five FDA-approved molecules in calendar 2025 involved Sai in discovery, development or commercial manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Has the shift to integrated CRDMO and big pharma FTE engagements accelerated this calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still early, with relationships growing from one service at a time; FTE model started about 15 months ago and acceleration is seen mainly in scale and scope.

qa_highlights.question: Is the H2-weighted FY27 guidance due to capacity, given the historical split?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said FY26 was about 48/52 H1/H2 versus a historical 40/60, and capacity additions are behind the stronger H2 call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex threshold and what would cause a slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal hurdle rates are set above the company's ROCE/ROE targets. Capacity-addition capex can be slowed if demand slows; capability-building capex is harder to defer absent severe circumstances.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 15-20% when the pipeline is large and recent quarters slowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is framed over 3-5 years given lumpiness; management said it is not constraining growth and FY26 grew close to 30%, with quarterly revenue driven by delivery timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI initiative the same as the high-throughput experimentation platform?
qa_highlights.answer: No. HTE generates more data points per experiment; the AI initiative targets non-value-added chemist and operator work, with an update expected before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial profile of the four new commercial contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Three of four are commercial supplies, described as decently sized by value; one is a lower-volume product. Primary supplier in about two of three, anecdotally.

risks_watch: CDMO growth of about 6% YoY and quarterly lumpiness; H2 recovery depends on Bidar block 1 and formulation start-up timelines.
Capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore is heavy; FY28 capex guidance not yet given.
Formulation entry (oral solids to Phase 2, China+1 driven) is new; management says it is not yet commercial and profitability was questioned.
Management did not disclose revenue at the individual molecule or customer level, and declined to discuss mAb strategy or fermentation capex.
Commercial peptide capacity not due until 2028.

544307|2026-03.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22.2% to INR 3,114 crore with same-store sales growth of 13.2%, while management flagged input inflation from May.
544307|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 3,114 crore (+22.2% YoY), with same-store sales growth (SSSG) accelerating to 13.2% from 11% for FY26. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened to 8.8% from 8.2% and PAT rose 45.9% to INR 168 crore. Management attributed the strength to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus heavier promotions ahead of the spring/summer season. Management said input inflation, mainly petroleum-linked materials and fabric, began in late April and May, and it committed to keep private-brand discounts to third-party brands at least at current levels (about 40% on apparel).

segments.name: Apparel (fast fashion, biggest category)
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG by price point: entry 11.1%, mid-price 13.6%, fashionable (top 2-3 price points) 14.7%. Management said fashion was the fastest-growing segment in Q4 and FY26.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: 74.1% of FY26 revenue; two brands above INR 1,000 crore and six more above INR 500 crore revenue.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Expanded to 745 stores across 505 cities; registered users reached 1.3 crore.

segments.name: Small format stores
segments.commentary: 13 stores in total, 3 opened in Q4 FY26; management said store EBITDA and revenue per sq ft match large-format stores.

Fabric prices rising about 10-11%, per management's current range for suppliers.

Pricing is set by price point: no uniform price increases; opening and low price points are protected, higher fashion price points get more room, and management aims for price increases to be volume-neutral.
Suppliers facing gas and labour shortages earlier in the period; management said vendor supply is improving but labour has not fully returned.
Competition: management believes it is gaining share, citing 7 of the 11 SSSG points coming from new customers; it did not name V2 or V-Mart directly.
Management expects down-trading benefits if demand weakens, given private brands are 30-50% cheaper than third-party brands in food and grocery.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 SSSG acceleration, and was there pre-buying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a general consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus higher growth investment in the quarter. It did not frame it as pre-buying.

qa_highlights.question: How will private-label pricing respond to rising leader-brand prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to keep the discount to leader brands at least at 40% for apparel, and to try to widen it if possible.

qa_highlights.question: How did the company handle the cotton inflation of 2021-22?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it took a margin hit then, absorbed much of the increase, and used cost initiatives such as removing poly bags, using gunny bags, shipping shoes without outer cartons, and CAD cutting to reduce waste.

qa_highlights.question: Are price increases neutral, incremental or negative to apparel sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for neutral, since high-fashion price points show lower elasticity, and it avoids raising opening price points.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend policy given strong free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred to the Board and gave no dividend commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new small-format and newer-state stores performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kerala is above average, Gujarat and Maharashtra (6 stores each) are in line with the network, and small-format stores match large-format stores on sales per sq ft and store EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin compress, and why did working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cleared old spring/summer stock ahead of the April-June season and increased promotions to capture a consumption uptick. The CFO said working capital days are about the same as last year and that is the intended operating level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for rent and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said rent rises about 5% a year under lease terms, so double-digit SSSG should keep producing operating leverage. He said Q4 rent looked low because of lease renewals in Q4 FY25.

Geopolitical and crude-price shocks, currency depreciation and possible weak rural demand from a poor monsoon.
Vendor labour and gas availability constraints, which the company says are easing.
Rising competition in apparel from e-commerce and value-fashion players moving into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
Dividend policy remains undecided despite strong cash generation.

544307|2026-06.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.7% to INR 3,727 crore on 10% same-store sales growth; operating EBITDA margin 10.4%.
544307|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR 3,727 crore, up 18.7% YoY, driven by 10% same-store sales growth. Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crore (up 19.3%, margin 10.4% vs 10.3%) and PAT was INR 259 crore (up 25.6%, margin 6.9% vs 6.6%). Gross margin improved to 28.7% from 28.4%, mainly from lower promotional spend rather than price hikes. The company added 27 stores to reach 819 across 559 cities, with management flagging elevated inflation as a demand headwind expected to ease in later quarters.

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 819 stores in 559 cities at June 2026 end after 27 openings in the quarter, including 10 in South India; total trading area 13.8 million sq ft.

segments.name: Small format
segments.commentary: 3 small stores opened in the quarter (16 in total cited); currently run only in UP and Haryana, with a stated opportunity of about 3,000 small-format stores nationally.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: Contributed 75.2% of revenue; 100% of apparel, about 75% of general merchandise, about 60% by volume of FMCG, and about 50% of kitchen appliances (Tandem brand).

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: 767 stores across 520 cities and over 1.4 crore registered consumers; contributes 2-9% of store revenue, at least 5% in most locations; average bill about INR 800; 20% of customers are new to Vishal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects inflation-driven demand impact to taper in subsequent quarters.
Small-format stores to accelerate; current guidance cited as 80 to 100 small-format store additions.
RFID rollout: Delhi NCR stores live; full network rollout expected to slightly exceed one year.
No further price increases planned beyond those already taken, assuming current conditions persist.
Gross margin sustainability depends on current cost structure; management says no significant issue if circumstances hold, but declined to forecast West Asia-linked developments.
Foreign ownership to be capped at 49.99% to keep the company Indian owned and controlled; foreign holding is close to 20% today.
capex_capacity: Store additions: 27 in Q1 FY27 (819 total); small-format openings were slow at 3 in the quarter, with some large-format stores opened alongside.
New format: first pilot store said to be very close to launch, followed by one or two more pilots before a roll-out decision.
RFID: pilot in 2 stores in Delhi NCR, now extended to all Delhi NCR stores; stock counts possible in 4-5 hours, enabling weekly counts.
Minimum wage increases in Haryana, UP, Telangana, Karnataka and others lifted employee cost per sq ft about 13% YoY.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth of 10%: new customer acquisition up 8%, existing customer spend up 3%.

Price increases were limited to higher price points and selected categories; opening and mid price points were not raised, and price-sensitive categories such as children's clothing and staple foods were left unchanged.
Highest-priced apparel fashion grew 13.9% same-store sales growth.
Gross margin gain came mainly from lower promotional intensity, with little contribution from price hikes.
Management says no new competitors entered apparel and expansion pace from existing players did not rise sharply this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is small-format expansion slow when small towns may suit it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small-format stores were a test phase; they now match larger formats on revenue per sq ft and ROCE, and expansion will accelerate, with UP and Haryana as the only states so far. Large-format stores are still being opened alongside.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin improve despite cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin rose from 28.4% to 28.7%, mainly because promotional spend was lower YoY; prices were held to protect same-store sales, with little price-hike effect.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organisational change and the foreign ownership cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Sashi Gumma replaces Manoj, who is leaving after more than 10 years, in the same role, with no change to the org structure. The 49.99% foreign cap is to stay Indian owned and controlled; it applies because subsidiary Airplaza runs multi-brand retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is quick commerce's contribution and profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce contributes 2-9% of store revenue, with most locations at 5% or more; average bill is about INR 800, slightly above offline, and 20% of quick commerce customers are new to Vishal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in employee cost per sq ft structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the increase came from significant minimum wage hikes across several states, which is a structural change; management will try to optimise but cannot fully offset it.

qa_highlights.question: What is closing inventory and status of the new format?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing inventory was INR 1,900 crore. The new format is near its first pilot store launch, with one or two more pilots planned before a roll-out decision.

risks_watch: Elevated inflation weighing on demand; management expects easing but gave no firm timeline.
Gross margin sustainability: the gain depends on lower promotions and holding prices; West Asia developments are an open risk.
Structural rise in employee costs from minimum wage increases across several states.
Competitive pressure in apparel from value retailers; management says the competitor set is unchanged, but pace is a watch item.
Leadership change: COO Manoj departs and Sashi Gumma replaces him; further org changes not discussed.
Small-format and RFID roll-outs are gradual; timing and benefits remain to be proven at scale.

But I'm not saying that I can see the future any better than any of us on the West Asia crisis and so on.
Under no circumstances, would we allow a price discount to the market leader become lesser than before.

544307|2026-09.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% to INR3,399 crore, but same-store sales growth slowed to 5.4% as festivals shifted into Q3.
544307|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 14% YoY to INR3,399 crore in Q2 FY27, with same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 5.4%, which management says would have been about 9% without the festival shift. Operating EBITDA rose 3.7% to INR262 crore, but margin fell to 7.7% from 8.5% on operating deleverage from low fixed-cost absorption. Adjusted PAT grew 6.4% to INR172 crore, with margin at 5.1% versus 5.4%. Store network reached 844 with 26 gross additions in the quarter, and management said it sees no demand moderation despite inflation.

financial_highlights.change: About 9% adjusted for festival shift (3-4pt impact)

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (Q2 FY27, after ESOP charges)

financial_highlights.change: About 9.5% adjusted for festival shift (1.5-2pt impact)

segments.commentary: Core format; management sees room for about 2,000 large-format stores against roughly 850 today, and is prioritising these in all states. 24 of 26 Q2 openings were in Tier 2/3 towns.

segments.name: Small format stores (UP and Haryana pilot)
segments.commentary: 18 small-format stores now, with 2 added in Q2. Management sees potential for upwards of 3,000 stores nationally, but will open them only where large-format opportunity diminishes.

segments.name: Belong & Co. (apparel format)
segments.commentary: First pilot store launched in Q2 targeting young affluent urban shoppers. Management reports footfall-to-purchase conversion above 50% but says it is still learning and has not set a rollout plan.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Expanded to 781 stores across 532 cities, with over 1.5 crore registered users. Management is increasing advertising and digital spend, starting in Delhi.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for double-digit SSSG for full FY27; Q3 SSSG must be above 10% for the nine months to look double-digit, per the analyst's arithmetic that management accepted.

Gross margin expected to hold YoY in Q3 and Q4 with no material impact from vendor price increases, supported by cost re-engineering; Q2 gross margin was down 30 bps, of which 20 bps came from apparel shift to Q3.
More than 100 new stores targeted for FY27, with the aim of beating the prior year's count every year.
EBITDA margin expected to improve about 30 bps a year over time, assuming double-digit growth against 6-7% store-level cost inflation.
No further price increases planned at the current inflation level, including after the festive season.
Employee cost pressure to ease: management says 8-10% SSSG is enough to offset the higher employee cost from minimum wage increases and new stores.
capex_capacity: Store additions: 26 gross in Q2 and 53 in H1 FY27; total 844 stores. Q2 split: 15 South (6 in Kerala, which now has 35 stores), 5 North, 4 East, 2 Western.
Management said the Kerala store plan was roughly doubled from the original estimate, with smaller stores, because the state is contiguous with no gaps between cities.
Large pilot in Gujarat and Maharashtra with smaller-format stores based on a hypothesis that higher affluence supports higher revenue per sq ft; management called it too early to conclude.
A fully automated large warehouse has been commissioned in North India, with plans for East, then South, then West warehouses.
Retail trading area is 1.41 crore sq ft. Area growth has trailed store growth; management said store size is set by catchment and that it solves for stores first.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is steady with no moderation; Q2 growth came mainly from market-share gain rather than existing customers buying more.
Price increases were taken mainly at higher price points. Opening price points had no increase and mid price points had very few changes.
Revenue mix: about 18-20% from opening price points, about 50% from mid, and about 24-25% from highest price points.
Rentals grew slowly versus area addition, which management attributed to Tier 2/3 expansion, not renegotiation. It expects this gap to continue.

Inventory days were around 65 in the base period versus 59-60 in H1 FY27 per an analyst's calculation; management attributed the gap to the festival shift, with the stock build happening three weeks later this year.
Weather and rainfall were uneven, causing one- to two-day revenue disruptions in some regions, but no regional demand weakness was reported.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 3-4% festive shift carry into Q3, and what Q3 SSSG is needed for a 9% first-half-equivalent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed Q3 SSSG must be above 10% for the nine months to look double-digit, since festivals (Durga Puja, Dussehra, Navratri) moved from September to October.

qa_highlights.question: Will vendor price hikes hurt gross margin in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost re-engineering has protected gross margin and vendors are already charging higher prices, so no material impact is expected in Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about INR10 crore QoQ, and what SSSG offsets the wage pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the rise reflects incremental ESOP cost and new stores, with minimum wage increases already in Q1. He said 8-10% SSSG is enough to offset the higher employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: How are price increases split across price points, and will there be more?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further price increases are planned at the current inflation level, including after the festive season, and that opening price points were protected.

qa_highlights.question: How are new store openings split by region, and will Tier 1 entry follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 24 of 26 Q2 openings were in Tier 2/3 towns and 15 were in South. It is piloting in Maharashtra and Gujarat, with stores in Ahmedabad, Surat, Pune and Baroda.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash on the balance sheet be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to more stores each year, Belong & Co. and small-format capacity, warehouses in East, South and West India, and quick commerce advertising. It said the board is still evaluating options.

Capital allocation of a large cash balance is under board review, with no decision yet.

544309|2026-03.headline: IKS agreed to acquire TruBridge for ~$557M enterprise value (~3x EBITDA), funded by $565M debt; management guides to ~INR3,000 crore revenue ambition by FY30.
544309|2026-03.overview: IKS signed a definitive merger agreement to acquire TruBridge, a US listed EHR and RCM provider, on April 23, 2026, with closing expected in 90 to 120 days subject to HSR/FTC clearance. TruBridge's trailing CY2025 revenue was $347M ($126M EHR, $221M RCM) and adjusted EBITDA was $69M, versus $186M-plus on a reported-to-adjusted basis cited by management. Management framed the deal as adding an EHR installed base of about 700 clients as a distribution and data moat for IKS's AI-led RCM and clinical workflow platform. The call focused on strategic rationale and TAM, with limited detail on synergy quantum or timing beyond G&A-first sequencing and a four-year timeline.

Reported EBITDA $159M; management-adjusted figure cited as $186M on $698M revenue basis, after removing ESOP ($43M), public-company and one-time costs ($9.5M and others)
5-year term loan at SOFR+275 bps, stepping down to SOFR+175 bps as leverage falls; starting leverage ~3x EBITDA
Management said instantly EPS and PAT accretive; analyst noted a $12M amortisation item not included in the calculation

Acute RCM offering to be launched; Scribble ambient scribing product to be upgraded into a live encounter co-pilot.
Management described the EHR modernisation as costly for TruBridge, previously a drain on financials, and said IKS would bring agile, cost-optimised development.
demand_pricing: RCM is fragmented: top players hold under 20% share, with 400-plus players and a long tail; US healthcare RCM spend about $1.75-1.8 trillion, of which management's modelled addressable base is around 2% take rate.
Management modelled 2% take rate for RCM outsourcing (versus about 3% today) to conservatively allow for price compression from AI.

Competitors named: Med-Metrix and CorroHealth (RCM BPO); 3M and Optum (encoders); Epic, Athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen (EHR); Oracle Cerner challenger; MEDITECH; Phreesia, Augmedix, Abridge, Ambience and Microsoft DAX in ambient AI.
Management argues outcome-based pricing will replace per-user SaaS pricing as AI orchestrates tasks; TruBridge's 700-client base is outpatient-heavy (60-70% of volume).
Management said the parent's own attempts at globalising RCM and building a captive in India had not succeeded, and that IKS brings an offshore-enabled model.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition in EHR and RCM, and do IKS's learnings help win the segment? Any overlap between RCM and EHR clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EHR is a two-player market with Epic and Oracle Cerner dominant and MEDITECH a challenger; RCM is largely unmanaged, and about 230-240 of TruBridge's ~700 EHR clients already buy RCM, leaving a large white space. The 500-odd clients without RCM and 1,500 non-TruBridge EHR clients are targets.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the initial synergies or the financial outcome of the merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify synergies beyond saying the INR1,000 crore to INR3,000 crore north star is a definition of success, and said the target contains uncertainty for learnings and mistakes; drivers are RCM transformation, globalisation and G&A, with 2,000-plus RCM FTEs in India versus about 1,000 in US.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the deal structured with a 4-year timeline and why is the organic path hard?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said synergy timing is not being given in detail; G&A synergies come first and operational synergies later; organic growth to 700 clients would take about a decade and IKS's global RCM model is a differentiator given earlier failed attempts.

qa_highlights.question: What are the steps post-close and how will IKS retain customers and talent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management outlined Q1 learning, Q2 actioning new structure, Q3 operational synergies; customer retention was called the gold mine of the transaction, along with identifying and retaining key talent in the first quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How does TruBridge's headcount and RCM proposition compare with IKS's model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EHR has low marginal cost and RCM is tech-led and AI-first; RCM spend at large systems runs about 4-5% of revenue and about 7-10% at hospitals, strengthening the outsourcing proposition.

qa_highlights.question: Does IKS plan to compete with the large EHR vendors at scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is not to take EHR to larger hospitals; EHR is for the 0-50 bed segment, with the 50-200 bed range a later addition, and EHR is to be a sticky source of data for RCM.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth guidance change after closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not changing aspirations of growing faster than the ~12% industry rate, and is less certain on growth than margins over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT accretion of about $5M excluding a $12M amortisation item?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intangible amortisation schedule is being separately evaluated for EHR and RCM relationships, with new asset lives under valuation by experts; the $5M accretion was presented as the highest-possible level, with minor changes possible.

544309|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY (12% constant currency) to INR893 crores, with reported EBITDA of INR294 crores at 33% margin.
544309|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached about INR893 crores, up 21% YoY and 12% in constant currency, with forex gains neutral versus Q4. Reported EBITDA was INR294 crores (33%); management says it was about 35% after adding back roughly INR20 crores of one-time TruBridge acquisition costs. PAT was INR193-194 crores, up about 28% YoY. TruBridge closed on July 10, 2026, so Q1 figures are legacy IKS only; management reset TruBridge's steady-state revenue to about $300 million a year (from $340 million pre-close) while keeping its roughly $68 million EBITDA, and reaffirmed a FY30 EBITDA True North of at least INR3,000 crores without further dilution beyond ESOPs.

qa_highlights.question: What organic constant-currency growth is healthy over the medium term, and is margin expansion coming from currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin growth is not from currency: revenue grew 12% CC on 4.2% headcount growth; adjusted EBITDA is 35% with neutral forex. Aspiration is 12%+ CC on legacy IKS, not guidance; TruBridge growth to be set in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How does SLM fit with LLMs, and where does glass-box/explainable AI sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Three SLM approaches: standalone SLMs, LLM-distilled SLMs, and hierarchical SLM-plus-LLM. Explainability comes from knowledge graphs acquired via ARAI. Management would not commit to a 60% token-usage reduction, saying it will emerge over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire TruBridge and what criteria govern acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Chosen because the rural market is large, TruBridge holds 30%+ share as one of two dominant rural EHRs, and its service mix resembles ambulatory. Criteria: strategic thesis first, leverage tolerable relative to EBITDA, and accretive price; $68 million EBITDA bought for ~$550 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge's margin of 22-23% fixable, and does the INR3,000 crore target rule out M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers include existing and in-build technology plus offshore human-in-the-loop to restore early-to-mid 30s margins. INR3,000 crores is achievable without another acquisition, but M&A is not ruled out; white space seen as large.

qa_highlights.question: Does Abridge's platform move threaten IKS, and is pricing under pressure in renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management respects Abridge but sees ~30 vendors aspiring to platforms and rising competition. Recent five-year deal signed at healthy price; pricing pressure expected but margin leverage maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge still EPS accretive for FY27 after revenue reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; EBITDA is unchanged, so management says EPS accretion is absolute and possibly a bit higher than previously expected.

544310|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 57% to INR235.1 crore with EBITDA margin of 25.7%; order book above INR400 crore and FY27 order-booking target of INR500+ crore.

H2 FY26 revenue was INR135.5 crore (up 46% YoY), with H2 EBITDA of INR37.2 crore and PAT of INR23.7 crore. Order book stood at over INR400 crore on 31 March 2026. Management said the Greenfield RIP facility is in final commissioning, with trial production by end Q2 FY27 and commercial production targeted around October 2026.

segments.commentary: Balance of volumes in FY26 (combined with OIP, about 15-18% of order book per management).

544311|2026-03.headline: IGI Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue and EBITDA each grew 21% YoY to INR 3,686 mn and INR 2,360 mn, with volumes up 16% to 3.64 mn reports.
544311|2026-03.overview: Q4 (Jan–Mar 2026) was the first quarter reported after the switch from calendar to financial year, so the 15-month period (Jan 2025–Mar 2026) is the main comparison basis. Growth was led by lab-grown diamonds (LGD +35%) and LGD jewelry (+29%), while natural diamond jewelry fell 19% on gold and silver price volatility. The AGL acquisition (closed 30 Jan 2026) contributed about 2 pts to revenue and 3 pts to EBITDA growth in the quarter. Management guided to 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth for FY27 and said margins would be held at last year's levels.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +35% YoY (India standalone +46%); 15-month growth +25%. Management attributed the jump to new customer acquisitions and capacity additions at primary growers.

Growth expected mainly from LGD capacity build-up and deeper penetration in natural diamonds, with AGL gemstone certification as a fifth segment.
Management said FY26 was ahead of the original guidance and that FY25 was over-delivered; the FY27 numbers are broad guidelines rather than firm targets.
Q4 is seasonally strong for LGD mix; management expects the LGD mix to taper through the year after Christmas and Diwali quarters.
capex_capacity: Lab-grown manufacturing capacity additions are happening mainly in Surat, India; management said the full impact of capacity additions has not yet shown in results and will ramp through FY27.

Management said 30–35% of natural and loose diamonds are uncertified, mainly small sizes with low commercial value, and that smaller studded stones are generally not certified at loose-stone level.
Retail demand for natural diamonds in bridal and high-value purchases was described as intact despite gold price volatility and macro uncertainty in some markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA growth achievable, and will INR depreciation help margins?

qa_highlights.question: Has LGD and ND pricing remained stable, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No structural pricing changes in Q4. Mix is an outcome rather than a driver, and the company focuses on the growth of each segment.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the decline in natural diamond jewelry, and what is the US leadership progress?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline is attributed to gold and silver price increases and volatility in India. A new US leader has been in place for 3–4 months and the sales team is being strengthened.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs not rise after the gemologist hiring plan, and how do exports square with the growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose 16% QoQ as costs built up. Management said export values in rupees or dollars understate volume, since LGD carats have roughly doubled while value per carat has fallen.

544311|2026-06.headline: IGI Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23% YoY to INR 3,708 million and EBITDA 29% to INR 2,238 million, with 60.4% margin.

India standalone growth was slower on EBITDA (15%) because of commission payouts to overseas subsidiaries, front-loaded IPL sponsorship and headcount additions. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA growth, with AGL adding a couple of percentage points on top.

AI-based work allocation and scheduling is now in use in labs, letting the same team grade more stones faster without changing grading standards.
AGL colour-stone methods are being rolled out in IGI's other labs, with dedicated setups planned for large customers. Global expansion of AGL services is planned but locations were not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Lab-grown wholesale prices have stabilised in the INR 118-120 range per management's Investor Day deck. Certification costs 2-3% of retail price.

Q2 ARP rose 4% YoY to INR 891: AGL added 2%, and the base business added 2% from a higher LGD mix (54% vs 52%). Sequentially, ARP fell about 12% on a lower LGD loose mix (down 4%) and a higher jewellery mix.
Natural diamond buyers are delaying purchases due to high and volatile gold prices.
Management said 4Cs grading remains the reporting standard and that it sees no demand shift to simplified classification. It said there are no printing rights for certificates granted to anyone.

qa_highlights.question: Is the LGD revenue surge a pre-festive stocking effect, and will Q3 taper?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LGD revenue has been steady at about INR 2,100 million in Q1 and Q2 and expects no slowdown, citing grower capacity additions. Natural growth is expected to pick up, with traction starting and momentum expected to continue for two more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Should guidance be raised given H1 overshoot?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 will outperform the 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA guidance, similar to H1. It did not give a new number, but confirmed when asked that H2 growth would be above the original guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How will the surplus cash be used: M&A or higher dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Priority is growth investment first (Italy, Saudi Arabia), then M&A, then dividends. The September interim dividend was INR 2.55 per share.

qa_highlights.question: Is there grading inconsistency at IGI, and are the top Surat manufacturers printing certificates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied giving printing rights to anyone. It said grading involves multiple checks, is ISO accredited for 18 years, and that there is no gap versus other labs.

qa_highlights.question: Does the AI push allow smaller labs to compete cheaply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IGI's image dataset from c.4.5 million certificates a quarter is hard to replicate and is used to build its AI and ML capability, improving turnaround times.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin in India fall and when will the investments pay off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the India margin drop of about 340 bps to leadership hiring, marketing and commission spend. It gave no timeline for payback, but said the group margin was 60.1% for FY26, 60.4% in Q1 and 61.4% in Q2.

risks_watch: Natural diamond certification growth of 8% lags LGD, and natural jewellery grew only 3%. Watch whether festive-season recovery materialises.
India standalone EBITDA margin fell to 69.5% from 72.8%. Watch whether the people and marketing spend yields a return.
Diwali timing shift means some Q2 festive demand was pulled from Q3 by September stocking. Watch Q3 for payback.
AGL integration: gemstone growth is driven by acquisition and the organic base is not disclosed. Watch the AGL contribution and the global rollout.
Grading consistency questions were raised by a市场 participant and a Surat source. Management denied them. Monitor for any disputes or customer complaints.

544314|2026-03.headline: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue rose 59.7% YoY to INR 1,169.2 crores as Punjab ramped up; management guides FY27 consolidated EBITDA north of INR 500 crores.
544314|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue grew 3% YoY to INR 752.8 crores with EBITDA up 16.9% to INR 82.5 crores and margin at 11%. Consolidated Q4 revenue of INR 1,169.2 crores and EBITDA of INR 94.4 crores (8.1% margin) reflect the first full quarters of Punjab Phase 1 ramp-up, which management says reached full capacity only at end-March 2026. Consolidated FY26 PAT was INR 77.3 crores, weighed down by higher depreciation and finance cost after Punjab capitalisation. Management guided FY27 consolidated revenue of INR 5,600-5,700 crores and EBITDA north of INR 500 crores, with Phase 2 at Punjab targeted for end-FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Silvassa ran at full capacity through the war-related disruption, and Punjab ramp-up finished only in March after a one-quarter delay. Product line-up realignment is expected to show margin benefits from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: why did inventory and payable days rise (payables from about 59 days in FY25 to about 104 days)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Punjab ramp-up raised material and FG inventory, and about INR 180 crores of raw material was in transit. Punjab stock is lower than Silvassa, and days should fall as full-quarter COGS builds.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gross debt of about INR 1,500 crores is the peak, with repayments of INR 100-125 crores a year. Average cost of debt is about 7.25% after including trade payables carrying LC interest beyond 68 days; finance cost stays above INR 125 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to the INR 7,000 crore-plus revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is INR 5,600-5,700 crores, and peak revenue of INR 7,500-7,700 crores is expected by end FY28 after Phase 2 and cotton yarn.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Punjab margin reach Silvassa levels and double-digit consolidated EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin, calls its guidance conservative given the global situation, and tracks performance on EBITDA per tonne rather than percentage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Punjab Phase 1 utilisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 80-85% utilisation in the current quarter, with the facility aiming to run flat out like Silvassa over time.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to currency, raw materials and PTA supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Euro-denominated ECB is hedged for the full tenure, imports are booked on arrival, and the import and export balance limits raw material risk. PTA supply depends on GAIL and Indian Oil start-up timing.

risks_watch: Crude and cotton volatility: pass-through lags, and management said inventory was held back in some quarters when crude was expected to rise.

544317|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR6,880 crores with record EBITDA; FY27 guidance trimmed to 20-22% growth and about 11% EBITDA margin.
544317|2026-03.overview: Transrail reported record FY26 revenue of INR6,880 crores (up 30% YoY, against 25% initial and 27% revised guidance), with full-year EBITDA of INR820 crores (11.92% margin, up 21%) and operational PAT of INR421 crores (up 28%). Q4 FY26 was softer: revenue INR1,863 crores, EBITDA INR207 crores (11.08% margin) and PAT INR96 crores, which management attributed to project-cycle timing and supply-chain delays in February and March. Management guided FY27 to 20-22% revenue growth and around 11% EBITDA margin, citing geopolitical and commodity cost pressure, and reported an unexecuted order book of about INR16,361 crores with FY26 order inflow of INR8,520 crores (below the earlier INR10,000 crore expectation). Working capital days fell to 81 from 91 and net debt reduced to INR274 crores.

International backlog cited by analyst as INR6,400 crore; management said it will be consumed over 18-24 months.

segments.name: Bangladesh project
segments.commentary: Management said the INR4,500 crore Bangladesh book is almost complete, with only INR300 crore left to finish in the next 3 months.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of about 20% YoY for FY27 reiterated; management expects Q2 and Q3 to be much better.
EBITDA margin guidance of 11% plus maintained for FY27; management said it hopes to do better than 11% plus.
Order intake target of INR10,000 crore plus for FY27; tenders worth over INR20,000 crore quoted, with declarations expected in Q2 and part of Q3, at an assumed 10-15% win rate.
Net debt to EBITDA expected to return to around 0.33 by year end (March 2027), per management's stated direction.
Working capital days targeted at or below 81 days.
Interim dividend of INR3 per share declared for FY27.
QIP of up to INR600 crore approved by board, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals; the enabling resolution is still under evaluation with no firm plan yet.
INR200 crore tools and plant capex: about 70% to be used in FY27, balance in FY28, staggered quarter on quarter.
capex_capacity: Eco-friendly tower manufacturing facility at Butibori, Nagpur commenced commercial production (started 24 April per management).
Conductor brownfield phase 1 is ready and equipment calibrated; start delayed from Q1 to Q2 FY27 pending approvals from authorities.
Tower capacity expanded; management said supply chain for projects should improve in Q1-Q2.
Acquired Gactel turnkey projects, adding IDCT tower solutions to NDCT cooling tower EPC offering.
INR200 crore capex for tools and plants, staggered use through FY27 and FY28.
demand_pricing: Order intake of about INR1,000 crore in Q1 versus the INR10,000 crore annual target; management attributed this to a 3-5 month lag between bid and award.
Quoted tenders worth over INR20,000 crore across domestic and international markets.
Won a 500 kV HVDC order from an Indian developer during the quarter.
Entered Australia with first monopole supply and seed marketing for monopoles and towers; management cited about 10,000 circuit km requirement there.
Strengthened position in MENA region; global footprint now 6 continents.
Exploring data center EPC, BESS, and drone-based mapping and survey, which management described as early stage; MoA amended to add these areas.
Management cited global electricity demand expected to nearly double by 2050 and India's plan to add 1,91,000 circuit km of transmission lines by 2032.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 order intake only about INR1,000 crore against a INR10,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 3-5 month bid-to-award lag and INR20,000 crore of bids in Q1, with a 10-15% win rate expected to convert in Q2 and Q3. Guidance of INR10,000 crore plus is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-line growth lag guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply chain disruptions in the factory (diesel, LDO, procurement delays) hurt output. It called the 5% growth the best first quarter in company history and expects Q2 to catch up.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company raising capital through a QIP when cash flows are strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the QIP is an enabling resolution for long-term working capital and to take advantage of opportunities, with no firm plan yet. It ruled out greenfield or acquisition plans for now.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to the conductor brownfield capex that was due in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said phase 1 is ready and equipment calibrated, but approvals are pending; start is now expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract assets rise and what do they consist of?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said contract assets include retention, TOC retention and unbilled revenue, all recoverable with provisions for doubtful amounts. Retention will rise with revenue. Management acknowledged some delays in collections.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt to EBITDA almost double this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to delayed collections and higher working capital deployment, expected to normalise in Q2 and return to about 0.33 by March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR80 crore related-party loan to Burberry and when will it be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the INR80 crore loan has been outstanding for about 3 years, INR30 crore was received last year, and principal plus interest is due by 30 September 2026. Management said all loans are recoverable.

risks_watch: Order intake of about INR1,000 crore in Q1 is well below the INR10,000 crore FY27 target; Q2 tender conversion must be tracked.
Revenue growth needs to accelerate from 5% in Q1 to about 20% for the year, implying a steep ramp in Q2-Q4.
Net debt rose sharply and collections are delayed; watch the Q2 normalisation and net debt to EBITDA trend.
Related-party INR80 crore Burberry loan due by 30 September 2026.

The conductor kilometre figures in the investor presentation were questioned by an analyst and management said it would check the data.

544318|2026-03.headline: Mamata Machinery FY26 revenue fell about 8% to Rs 233.1 crore and EBITDA margin dropped to 8.2%, which management attributes mainly to a 50% US decline and one-offs.
544318|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a consolidation year: revenue from operations fell about 8% to Rs 233.1 crore (FY25: Rs 254.6 crore) and Q4 revenue was Rs 73.9 crore versus Rs 111 crore a year earlier. The US business (including Canada and Mexico) fell close to 50%, hit by unresolved tariffs through Q2-Q3, then West Asia uncertainty and higher polymer prices in Q4. EBITDA fell to Rs 19.1 crore (8.2% margin) from Rs 54.6 crore (21.4%), and PAT to Rs 15.1 crore from Rs 40.8 crore. Management says the company remains debt-free with Rs 69.26 crore cash and guides FY27 revenue growth of about 15% with margin normalisation toward about 20%.

segments.name: Converting machinery
segments.commentary: US converting sales fell from Rs 31.63 crore to Rs 5.93 crore (-81%). Domestic converting grew over 6% and rest-of-world converting grew 23%, but the segment moderated overall because of the US share.

segments.name: Packaging machinery
segments.commentary: Packaging revenue was flat to down about 1%, at roughly Rs 48-49 crore. US packaging fell from Rs 36.8 crore to Rs 29.4 crore, while domestic packaging grew about 55%.

segments.name: Co-extrusion
segments.commentary: Marginal degrowth due to lumpy order timing. Three large nine-layer orders: two executed in FY26, one (about Rs 9 crore) due in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at conservatively about 15% over FY26, with management avoiding a truncated base.
EBITDA margin expected to normalise to historical average of about 20% as the top line recovers and one-offs roll off.
US business expected to recover in FY27, with residual headwinds from West Asia affecting capex sentiment.
Domestic packaging growth targeted at 30-40% in FY27 based on the current FMCG pipeline; domestic converting targeted at double-digit growth.
RecTech recyclable film expected to take 12-18 months before meaningful traction; treated as incremental, not part of the 30-40% packaging target.
Europe: incremental revenue of US$2-3 million over the next three to five years; South-East Asia initial business target close to US$1 million.
risks_watch: US recovery depends on tariff stability and West Asia-driven customer capex sentiment; the Rs 3.5 crore Saudi shipment is stalled.
Gross margin fell 6.2 percentage points on mix, lower exports and commodity inflation; watch H1 FY27 gross margin and pass-through.
RecTech adoption timeline of 12-18 months is long and depends on early-adopter FMCG trials and certifications (Europe and US pending).
Europe ramp is slow and depends on the Carpentier GmbH partnership, which is non-exclusive for initial years.
Lumpy co-extrusion and exhibition-linked spends can swing quarterly results.
Order book conversion: Rs 80 crore due in H1 FY27 must be executed on time to support the 15% growth guidance.
544318|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term direction and the packaging pipeline, but candid that FY26 was weak. Management attributes the decline to external events (US tariffs, West Asia) and one-offs. Answers on RecTech and Europe were measured and conservative, and some figures (such as the margin split) were deferred or not quantified.
key_quotes: This was a year of consolidation for the company.
We expect profitability to normalize to historical averages of around 20% as the top line recovers and these one-off costs roll off.
It is definitely not because we are cheaper. In fact, we are the most expensive in India today.
We have zero B2C in business. Our entire business is B2B.

qa_highlights.question: Does the FSA exemption and three-year carry-forward mean packaging users face minimal near-term compliance pressure, making FY27-28 the inflection point?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RecTech needs first two or three early adopters after 6-9 month trials, with 12-18 months before traction. RecTech is incremental growth; the 30-40% domestic packaging target is based on the current FMCG pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Are there other markets to diversify into if the US stays weak? What is the Russia revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Packaging is being taken to Africa and Europe in FY27; a Russia branch office was approved. Russia has no packaging revenue yet, only a couple of converting machines. Converting is already present in about 84 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Order book split and margin difference between exports and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book Rs 89.59 crore: 62% exports, 38% domestic. Gross margin about 60% on exports vs about 42-43% domestically. Rs 80 crore executes in H1 FY27 and Rs 9 crore in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Were any orders delayed due to West Asia, and what is the FY27 growth expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Three machines worth about Rs 3.5 crore for Saudi Arabia are ready but unshipped. Management said it will not use a truncated base and conservatively expects FY27 revenue about 15% above FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins normalise, and who bears the input cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins to normalise as top line recovers and one-offs (exhibition spend, wage code) roll off; costs are semi-variable. Majority of cost increase passed on to customers project-by-project; no numeric split given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the US decline is in the US entity versus Canada and Mexico, and how were packaging and converting US figures split?
qa_highlights.answer: The 50% drop includes the US, Canada and Mexico. US packaging fell from Rs 36.8 crore to Rs 29.4 crore; US converting fell from Rs 31.63 crore to Rs 5.93 crore (-81%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Europe market size and the Carpentier partnership's scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Addressable market about US$800 million for the product lines; target US$2-3 million incremental over 3-5 years. Partnership with Carpentier GmbH is non-exclusive for Western Europe in initial years; Eastern Europe to use additional channel partners.

capex_capacity: Q4 FY26 order flow: capex decisions by customers were put on hold in Q4 amid West Asia conflict and polymer price spike; a few US orders came in during Q4 and are expected to execute over the next two months.
Multi-machine VFFS order from a leading Indian snacks and namkeen brand: 4 machines delivered in FY26 (3 in India), orders for 18 more scheduled for delivery in H1 FY27.

demand_pricing: US business (incl. Canada and Mexico) fell close to 50%, or about Rs 31 crore gross; US converting fell from Rs 31.63 crore to Rs 5.93 crore (-81%), US packaging from Rs 36.8 crore to Rs 29.4 crore (about -20%).
Recovery in FY26 gap of Rs 31 crore: domestic converting +Rs 3 crore (about 6%), domestic packaging +Rs 6 crore, rest-of-world converting +Rs 11.5 crore; total Rs 20.65 crore recovered.
Domestic packaging grew about 55% in FY26; domestic converting grew over 6%; rest-of-world converting grew 23%.

Gross margin 54.6% vs 60.8%; management cited lower export share (exports higher margin, about 60% gross margin vs about 42-43% domestic on order book), adverse mix (lower co-extrusion), and H2 commodity inflation; 6.2 pp EBITDA margin impact.

Pricing: most of the polymer/input cost increase passed on to customers on project-by-project basis; management said it was the most expensive machine supplier in India and won on cost-to-output ratio, not price.
Competition: converting is highly fragmented (customers in about 84-86 countries per management); packaging customers are FMCG/organised-sector MNCs and marquee brands.

Europe: addressable market for product lines about US$800 million; initial target US$2-3 million incremental revenue over 3-5 years via Carpentier GmbH (non-exclusive for Western Europe in initial years).

RecTech: trials of 6-9 months with large FMCG companies; needs 2-3 early adopters; 12-18 months before traction; certifications (Indian Institute of Packaging, CPET) done, EU/US Class A testing pending.

rows.why: Orders for 18 more machines from a leading Indian snacks brand are scheduled for delivery in H1 FY27, after 4 machines were delivered in FY26.

544319|2026-03.headline: Senores FY26 consolidated revenue rose 62% to about INR664 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR122 crore; FY27 guided to 30-40% revenue growth.
544319|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose 66% YoY to about INR190 crore, with EBITDA of INR62 crore (32.7% margin, up about 1,151 bps) and PAT after minority interest of about INR32 crore (up 78%). Regulated markets drove the quarter at INR118 crore (up 83%), while emerging markets grew 26% and India branded generics roughly doubled to about INR9 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% and PAT growth of 50-60%, with blended EBITDA margin held at 29-31%. The Apnar Pharma acquisition (75% stake, 25% due by year-end) weighed on working capital and margin in Q4, with commercial shipments only starting in April 2026.

segments.name: Regulated markets (US and others)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR427 crore, up 75%; Q4 INR118 crore, up 83%, driven by portfolio expansion. Sourced/spot business is 10-12% of total revenue and is not expected to grow.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR145 crore, up 20%. Q4 was the highest-ever quarter with EBITDA margin of 18-19%; management expects this margin to hold, and the segment is now cash-flow positive. FY27 revenue projection is about INR180 crore.

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR40 crore, roughly 5x FY25. FY26 budget is INR60-70 crore; about 120-130 MRs in field, with a long-run plateau of about 200 MRs.

segments.name: CDMO-CMO and own products
segments.commentary: Management says own products are about 50-53% and CDMO-CMO about 47-48% of revenue. Apnar facility is expected to contribute INR80-100 crore in FY27 and INR180-200 crore in 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 30-40%, with PAT growth of about 50-60%; management called 30-35% the minimum achievable and will review after one or two quarters.
Blended EBITDA margin guided at 29-31% for FY27; ex-other-income, Q4 FY26 margin of 26.5% could be about 28-28.5%.
Apnar Pharma FY27 revenue budgeted at INR80-100 crore; Q1 FY27 revenue expected at INR10-20 crore; INR180-200 crore in 2-3 years.
Emerging markets FY27 revenue projected at about INR180 crore, with EBITDA margin of about 18-21%.
Amerisyn JV FY27 revenue budgeted at INR50-80 crore (management cited INR80-100 crore, then conservative INR50-70 crore), at EBITDA margin around 40%.
Capex FY27 about INR200 crore, including about INR100 crore for injectables and the balance for other plants and maintenance; management expects FCF generation in FY27.
Long-term aspiration of INR2,500-3,000 crore (up to INR4,000 crore) US revenue in 3-4 years across India and US facilities; ANDA rollout of 90-95% of the 51 approved ANDAs within 6-8 quarters.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR230 crore, including about INR65 crore for an ANDA acquisition.
FY27 capex expected at about INR200 crore, including about INR100 crore for injectables; about INR100 crore IPO proceeds earmarked for sterile manufacturing, to be started within this year.
Apnar Pharma (Baroda, USFDA-approved, also approved by UK MHRA and Health Canada): 75% acquired in Q4 FY26, remaining 25% by end of year; multiple pre-built clean rooms and expansion-ready.
Atlanta OSD facility: three lines commercialised; fourth line deferred due to Apnar acquisition; decision on fourth line or Apnar expansion expected within two quarters.
Emerging markets PIC/S approval for the facility expected around June-July 2026; more than 4,000 products under registration in emerging markets.
demand_pricing: Approved ANDAs rose from 22 (March 2025) to 51 (March 2026), covering more than 150 strengths; 20-21 launched, 30 to be launched over next few quarters; about 27 further molecules (60+ strengths) in development.
Management estimates the total accessible market for currently approved products plus pipeline at close to $1 billion.
Emerging market realisation per unit rose from about INR1.20 to about INR1.90 over 1-1.5 years (about 60-70%), with a shift to niche molecules.
Amerisyn JV (entered April 2026) targets US federal, VA and military procurement and FSS tenders; management says margins are not thin.
Management says branded generics do not need a large MR expansion to scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net working capital days rise from 114 to 187, and what is steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the jump is due to Apnar being consolidated with no sales yet; excluding Apnar, the cycle is about 104 days. Apnar is expected to align with group cycle from FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is other financial assets of INR172 crore (previously unbilled revenue)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is profit share on cost-plus B2B supplies, booked as income and parked as a financial asset until realised, typically 1-6 months. Balance should plateau then fall as launches mature. Not warranty or royalty.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance conservative given 60% growth history?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited external uncertainty (shipping, US inflation) and said 30-35% is the minimum achievable; guidance to be revisited after one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Emerging market margin improvement: forex versus operations?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said margin gain mainly came from product mix; forex contributed about INR3 crore of realised gains in the year.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate jump from about 17% in FY25 to about 23.6% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the rise to the Apnar tax provision, US tax at 20-21%, and India at 26%, and to FY25 benefit from US carry-forward losses. Long-term rate guided at about 23%.

risks_watch: Apnar revenue ramp: only about INR2.5-3 crore in the last three months; management guides INR10-20 crore in Q1 FY27 and INR80-100 crore for FY27.
Working capital and receivables: other financial assets (INR172 crore) and working capital days (187) need to normalise.
Guidance credibility: management said FY27 revenue guidance is conservative; a revision is possible after one or two quarters.
Execution on 30 pending ANDA launches over 6-8 quarters and the INR2,500-3,000 crore US target, which depends on launch timing.
Macro factors (shipping, US inflation, geopolitics) flagged by management as affecting margins.

544319|2026-06.headline: Senores Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to INR180 crores and EBITDA 87% to INR54 crores (~30% margin); FY27 guidance is 30-40% revenue and 50-60% PAT growth.
544319|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR180 crores, up 36% YoY, led by regulated markets (up 42%) and emerging markets (up 30%). EBITDA was INR54 crores (up 87%, margin ~30%, up 810 bps) and PAT was INR31 crores (up 56%). Sequentially, absolute EBITDA and PAT dipped versus Q4 FY26, which management attributed mainly to about INR14-15 crores of forex gains in Q4 that did not recur. Management reiterated FY27 guidance and a INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue ambition in three to four years, while the company shifted INR100 crores of IPO proceeds from sterile injectables to oral solids capacity.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 30% YoY; EBITDA margin was about 14% (mid-teens) against about 20% in Q4 FY26. Management guides 18-20% for the full year and says the business is cash flow positive, with INR18 crores operating cash in Q1.

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: Revenue was INR8 crores in Q1 FY27. Management shifted focus to profitability, targeting INR50-60 crores for FY27 at 35-40% EBITDA margin.

Chhatral facility PIC/S approval targeted around Q2-Q3 FY27, opening access to markets such as Vietnam, South Africa and Mexico.

Sterile injectable project has about INR100 crores of IPO proceeds left, now pushed to the second half of FY27 with a pilot approach.

Management said the Chhatral site in Ahmedabad is PIC/S inspected and makes oral solids, injectables and liquids.

qa_highlights.answer: H1 is seasonally weaker than H2, and Q1 is still the strongest first quarter in four years. Management reiterated the full-year 18-20% margin target and cited product mix and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did branded generics decline 2%, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus has moved from sales to profitability after the business rose from INR8 crores to INR40 crores in FY26. It targets INR50-60 crores at 35-40% EBITDA margin for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 'other income' restated for June 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said there is no restatement or policy change. Forex gains were moved from above the operating line into other income, so the presentation changed.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 included about INR14-15 crores of forex gains that were nil in Q1 FY27. Excluding this, margins are in line sequentially.

qa_highlights.question: Why was IPO proceeds use changed from sterile injectables to oral solids?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Apnar acquisition and oral solid pipeline growth needed capacity sooner, so it reallocated proceeds to oral solid lines in the US and India. A small sterile injectable pilot will follow, and shareholder approval is pending.
