544320|2026-03.headline: Carraro India FY26 revenue rose 25% to INR2,255 crore and EBITDA margin reached 10.8%; FY27 growth guided at 4-12%, with West Asia risk flagged.
544320|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 37% YoY to INR606 crore, with EBITDA up 45% and margin at 11.6%, driven by strong export and domestic agri demand. For FY26, revenue rose 25% to INR2,255 crore, EBITDA rose 33% to INR2,475 million, and PAT rose 48% to INR1,306 million. Management said FY27 growth could be 4-12% depending on how the West Asia situation evolves, and it declined to restate the 100bps-a-year margin improvement target. A final dividend of INR6.75 per share was recommended.

segments.name: Agricultural vehicles (domestic 4WD axles)
segments.commentary: FY26 agri revenue INR10,192 million (+19%). Management estimates the company's domestic 4WD axle revenue grew ~30%, in line with 4WD tractor growth above 40 HP. Management estimates ~24% of the >40 HP tractor market was 4WD in FY26, and expects 40-45% in 3-5 years.

segments.commentary: FY26 construction revenue INR9,837 million (+31%). Drivelines to Indian construction customers grew ~9% in FY26 against a ~2% domestic decline. Backhoe loader sales were positive against a ~10% BHL market decline.

segments.commentary: Turkey program SOP expected in FY27; Indian customer program expected to enter production by FY28. Turkey export tractor demand is described as stabilising or softening.

Domestic construction is uncertain given government fertiliser subsidies. Exports grew ~32% industry-wide in FY26.
Export mix (approx.): Europe including Turkey ~50% or less, China ~8-9%, Latin America ~10%, US ~9-10%. Management cautioned these are approximate because of contract-manufacturing invoicing.

Mix was the main reason for lower Q4 gross margin: the company prioritised dispatches to customers, with cost efficiency compromised. Commodity cost pass-through lag is ~3 months under most contracts.
Labour availability has tightened, with migrant workers having left, which has pushed up labour costs.

qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Rai said the TBH program is on track, with ~INR30 million of TBH revenue targeted by FY29. Backhoe export order book is 'good', but visibility is limited given geopolitical volatility.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 raw-material ratio increase was commodity inflation versus mix, and what is the pass-through lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Davide Grossi said the Q4 increase was mainly adverse product mix, not material or freight inflation. Most customer agreements pass through commodity changes over ~3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 revenue growth stay at 8-12% and how much margin expansion is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Balaji Gopalan said 8-12% is the target under normal conditions, but in the current environment it could be 4-8%. He declined to give a margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Why not repeat the 100bps-a-year margin expansion target?
qa_highlights.answer: Balaji Gopalan said guidance is hard amid disruption; margins will rise from 10.8% and will not fall, with the pace depending on how soon normalcy returns and on mix, energy and labour costs.

qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Rai estimated ~24% 4WD penetration above 40 HP in FY26 (from ~20-22%). About 60-65% of 4WD axles are outsourced and 30-35% are made in-house by OEMs; these are estimates with no formal data.

qa_highlights.answer: Davide Grossi confirmed FY27 capex of ~INR130-140 crore, more toward INR130 crore. Of ~INR285 million other income, ~INR83 million was a provision reversal and ~75% of the rest (~INR150 million) is export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Geographic split of exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is the largest (~50% including Turkey), with China ~8-9%, Latin America ~10% and the US ~9-10%. Management noted the split is approximate because OEMs assemble and distribute from multiple countries.

Labour cost inflation after migrant workers left, plus energy and freight costs.

544320|2026-06.headline: Carraro India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR5,447 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.4% on pass-through lag from commodity and freight inflation.
544320|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to INR5,447 million, driven by domestic growth of about 26% that offset a roughly 14% fall in exports. EBITDA rose 6% YoY to INR579 million, but margin was 10.4% as higher energy, raw material and freight costs, plus supplier-side labour shortages, were not yet recovered from customers. Total income included a one-time INR88 million provision write-back linked to a customs reassessment, which flatters other income and PAT. Management expects the price pass-through gap to close over about 12 months and targets full recovery of price increments for the full year.

Affected by energy, raw material costs and labour constraints

qa_highlights.question: Is China a meaningful market for Carraro India?

544335|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 61% YoY to INR820 crore and PAT rose 77.8% to INR44.92 crore; order book stood at about INR1,235 crore at 31 March 2026.

Management said the order book declined YoY to about INR1,235 crore, which it attributed to bidding for larger-ticket projects and faster execution. 544339|2026-03.headline: Laxmi Dental Q4 FY26 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to Rs 74 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.3%, and FY26 revenue grew 16.2% to Rs 277.9 crore.

EBITDA rose 41.8% YoY to Rs 13.5 crore and PAT reached Rs 10.1 crore, helped by a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit tied to a labour code gratuity item. FY26 closed with revenue of Rs 277.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 43.4 crore and PAT of Rs 28.9 crore, against a weak Q3. Management declined to give FY27 margin or growth guidance, and cited the company's Rs 99 crore cash balance and ongoing scanner deployment as strategic priorities.

Capex for FY27 will be set based on operational needs and revenue growth, funded from IPO proceeds still on hand.
US tariff is now about 10% (was about 50%). Management said this is not a deal breaker and expects US business to keep growing.

qa_highlights.question: Is Heartland Dental's contract under review, and are more US DSOs coming?

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering acquisitions with its cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate opportunities that add value and will disclose them only once completed. It gave no specifics.

544339|2026-06.headline: Laxmi Dental Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% y-o-y to about INR75 crore, a record, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and PAT up 23.8%.

544342|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.4% to INR 434.12 crore and PAT 35.61% to INR 43.84 crore; management reiterates 30-35% CAGR target.
544342|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 total revenue of INR 434.12 crore (+14.4% YoY), EBITDA of INR 61.35 crore (+23.34%) and PAT of INR 43.84 crore (+35.61%), against an internal target of INR 430 crore revenue and INR 40 crore PAT. Management reiterated 30-35% revenue CAGR guidance but cut the FY27 contribution expectation from the R32 plant and opened the door to dilution or debt for expansion.

The company remains debt-free with about INR171.3 crore of cash and investments, and announced a proposed acquisition of Epitome Cloud Inc. for about INR40 crore.

Two-wheelers grew ~19-20%, passenger cars ~11%, CV and tractor ~7-8%, and other segments ~4-5% (per management). Exports were hit by the West Asia situation.

segments.name: Automotive interiors and lighting (Antolin)
segments.commentary: Margins improved from 7-8% to early-to-mid teens after synergies and fixed-cost cuts. Management said the segment won several new customer programs post-acquisition. Ex-Antolin consolidated topline growth was said to be over 16%.

segments.name: Electric motors and controllers (EMFI)
segments.commentary: Management said the business doubled turnover in FY26 after Coimbatore capacity commissioned by end-December 2025, and expects full-year benefit in FY27. Management declined to disclose capacity or market share.

segments.name: High precision injection molded components / plastics (Takahata, TGPEL)
segments.commentary: Management said the injection-molded business saw very significant growth in Q1 and that plastics revenue grew about 2x last year. Takahata phase-four expansion has started, with new business revenue expected from early next year; TGPEL second Noida plant is filling up.

segments.name: Non-auto components
segments.commentary: Management said non-auto (compressors, marine, defense, railways, snowmobiles, lawn mowers, medical, music keyboards) has grown 15-20% a year over four years, but did not disclose its share of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Management expects volume momentum after GST 2.0 to continue through FY27 across two-wheeler, passenger car, CV and tractor segments.
Commodity cost increases are passed to customers with a one-quarter lag; management hopes the gap normalises in the current quarter (Q2 FY27).
Finance costs are expected to be temporary and normalise as acquisition-related debt is repaid.
Management said export markets (US, Europe, Middle East, Turkey, Egypt) have not yet recovered and expects normalisation to take more time.
Management expects to recover the lost margin from commodity inflation and said it will not lose margin.
Management said it targets consolidated EBITDA margins in the high teens and aims for Antolin margins closer to mid-teens.
capex_capacity: Acquired the piston manufacturing plant and machinery from Sunbeam Lightweighting Solutions Ltd; completed in Q1 FY27, adding piston capacity.
Capacity expansion underway across plastics, EV motors and controllers, interiors and legacy pistons; management did not disclose capacity figures.
Takahata phase-four expansion started, building a new plant adjacent to the existing facility on five acres of additional land; new business revenue expected from early next year.
TGPEL: second Noida plant has full capacity available and is filling up.
EMFI: Coimbatore capacity commissioned around end-December 2025.
Legacy CAFE-compliant piston and ring coating technologies already available at Ghaziabad and Pathredi plants; management said products are under customer testing and validation.
Management said all the tested flex-fuel products up to E85 are ready, requiring different plating with capacity already available.
demand_pricing: Management said realisation may rise to some extent with newer CAFE-compliant technologies, which cost more; management said it is leading the competition on these.
Mix shift toward smaller vehicles post GST 2.0 lowered value realisation per piece, per management.
Management said commodity prices have started to fall from unprecedented levels, and it expects normalisation within the next quarter.
Standalone gross margin was around 56-57% in the past two quarters versus 59-61% historically; management attributed this to product mix and commodity impact.
Management said it has back-to-back pass-through arrangements with customers across legacy, plastics, motors and interiors, with a one-quarter lag.
Management said the Q1 wage hike, effective 1 April, had a small impact on employee cost percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone legacy growth (~12%) trail the industry growth of ~20% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing growth was 12-14% versus company growth over 16%, and that exports were hit by the war situation, so manufacturing shifted toward OE customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin hold while EBITDA margin fell ~200 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of product, market, and volume effects, plus aftermarket lag in Q1 and the commodity pass-through lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is any price increase needed from OEMs to recover the commodity impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said back-to-back contracts exist with a one-quarter lag, so the increase for the prior quarter's average commodity price is recovered the following quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and what are the leverage thresholds?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated net debt was about INR 550 crore as of June; net debt to equity is 0.2x, and management said it will not cross 1x.

qa_highlights.question: How is the fundraise going to be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funds are fungible and will be split across acquisitions, debt repayment and ongoing investments; no split was given. It said the fundraise is progressing as per target.

risks_watch: Commodity-cost pass-through lag: management expects normalisation in Q2 FY27, so the Q2 margin is a key check.
Export weakness in the US, Europe and Middle East, with no clear recovery timeline per management.
Finance cost burden from acquisition debt, which management said will normalise over time; watch the repayment schedule.
Standalone legacy growth trailing industry manufacturing growth in Q1.
Undisclosed segment breakup: management declined to give plastics, Antolin and EMFI revenue and EBITDA for the quarter.
544344|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, integration and margin recovery, but evasive on specifics: management declined to give segment splits, EMFI capacity, market share, non-auto revenue share and the wage-cost impact. On exports, it was candid that recovery is slow.
key_quotes: As far as fundraise is concerned, I think we are progressing as per target.
We are not going to lose on our margins.
So, we have outgrown the industry even as we speak.
At present it is only 0.2x. So, we don't see any reason why we have to even go up to 1x.
I'd really request all of you to reach out to our secretarial department for the questions so that we can answer back one on one.

544345|2026-03.headline: Denta FY26 revenue rose over 23% to Rs 2,503.8 mn with order book of Rs 7,278 mn, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 19%, and management gave no firm order-inflow guidance.
544345|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 2,503.8 mn (over 23% growth), EBITDA of Rs 834.9 mn and PAT of Rs 609 mn, with an order book of about Rs 7,278 mn across 38 ongoing projects as of March 31, 2026. Analysts pressed on a sharp Q3/Q4 run-rate slowdown and a Q4 EBITDA margin of about 19% versus roughly 33% in the first three quarters, which management attributed to the Iran-US war, petroleum-linked raw material costs and a mix shift to smaller projects. Order-book inflow was described as pending new tenders under the new Karnataka government, with no order value committed. Working capital of about Rs 295 crore (inventory, receivables and other assets) is expected to convert largely in December-January, and management guided to about 20% FY27 revenue growth with an EBITDA margin of around 25%.

segments.name: Water management (core)
segments.commentary: Management says about 90% of the water order book sits in the water sector, covering drinking water, STP, irrigation and tank regeneration. The company has bagged 3-4 FTP projects covering about 15-16 cities in Karnataka.

segments.name: Amrut 2 and Jal Jivan Mission
segments.commentary: One Amrut 2 order of Rs 232 crore (Kuknuru and Yelburga, Koppal) and four Jal Jivan Mission projects in Karnataka. Management says about 70% of these projects is complete, with the balance 30% targeted this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% stated as the minimum projection; closing remarks cited a 20-25% target.
EBITDA margin guided at about 25% (confirmed in Q&A), down from about 33% run-rate in Q1-Q3 FY26.
No firm order-inflow number given; management expects to announce new orders shortly and aims for a healthy order-book increase by end-March 2027.
Management declined to give an absolute FY27 profit figure, saying it depends on project execution and raw material investment.
Government payments expected to accelerate from July-August 2026, with many payments in Q2-Q3 FY27, per management.
Possible price-escalation relief for HDPE/PVC items expected in July or Q2 FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: Inventory, receivables and other assets of about Rs 295 crore are tied up in working capital; management expects about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) to be realised in FY27, mainly by December-January.
Payment on supply is roughly 55% after material is laid, with the balance 35% on laying and the remainder on completion, per management.
Company is adopting NEBR and CAMUS-based STP technologies, claiming about 95% purity, largely through subcontracting to patent holders.
Bidding pipeline of about 5-6 projects worth about Rs 600 crore; management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and 2-3 major tenders.
Four to five projects identified in Madhya Pradesh under the National Water Management Programme (NWMP); a Mahanadi barrage tender in Odisha is yet to be floated.
demand_pricing: Karnataka's new government (formed late May/early June 2026) is expected to push infrastructure tenders after a roughly six-month slowdown.
Raw material risk: 20-30% of raw material is UPVC and HDPE pipe, with prices up in Q4 FY26, April and May 2026 after the Iran-US war; some suppliers seeking higher prices.
Price escalation clauses exist on projects above Rs 100 crore but not on smaller projects, per management.
Management said the company is taking smaller-value projects (Rs 10-50 crore) alongside larger ones (up to Rs 300 crore), which dilutes margin.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 execution slowdown was attributed to war-related disruption and irregular payments.

qa_highlights.question: Trajectory of order flow and government payment status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and expects to announce new orders in the coming quarter; payments are expected to pick up from July-August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said margin would be maintained around 30%, then confirmed a 25% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 after repeated questioning; it said smaller projects will dilute margin.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital liquidation timeline (Rs 295 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects cash in December-January, with about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) targeted in FY27, after laying and completion of projects by October.

qa_highlights.question: Order book fall from Rs 841 crore (Dec 2025) to Rs 727 crore (Mar 2026)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the reduction to revenue conversion and investment in completing old projects, and said the audit team would provide the exact reconciliation; it did not confirm any cancellation.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue and profit outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to a minimum of 20% revenue growth but declined to give an absolute profit number, saying it depends on project implementation and raw material investment.

qa_highlights.question: Diversification beyond Karnataka and into private industrial segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited NWMP projects in Madhya Pradesh and a biogas project with a partner holding GAIL and BPCL contracts; no firm private industrial wins were disclosed.

risks_watch: Margin dilution: Q4 EBITDA margin about 19% versus about 33% in Q1-Q3; FY27 guidance of 25% implies lower profit growth against a 20% revenue rise.
Working-capital conversion: about Rs 295 crore in inventory, receivables and other assets; collection timing rests on government payments.
Order book fell from about Rs 841 crore (Dec 2025) to Rs 727 crore (Mar 2026), with no reconciliation provided on the call.
Government dependence and political transition in Karnataka; payment timing is uncertain.
Raw material inflation from petroleum-linked pipes (UPVC and HDPE), with suppliers seeking higher prices.
Management answers on key numbers were vague or deferred to later written follow-up, including order-book reconciliation, margin split by project size and profit guidance.
544345|2026-03.management_tone: Management was upbeat and forward-looking on the new government's infrastructure push and order prospects, but evasive on specifics: it deferred the order-book reconciliation, margin split, and absolute profit figures to a later written follow-up. Its margin and payment answers shifted between statements, and it only confirmed the 25% EBITDA guidance after repeated questioning.
key_quotes: There will be 20% growth in revenue, that is the minimum revenue projections which we are having.
Manish Jayasheel Shetty: We will try to maintain roughly about 30%.
Without getting the order, it is not correct on my part to indicate the exact amount.

544350|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue crossed INR 2,000 crore (up 21.6% to INR 2,080 crore) with PAT up 52.4% to INR 168 crore; FY27 plans 60 new facilities.
544350|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations up 22.6% YoY to INR 564-565 crore, with Ind AS EBITDA of INR 174 crore (30.2% margin, the highest quarterly margin of the year) despite 19 facility openings. Full-year FY26 revenue from operations reached INR 2,080 crore, EBITDA INR 614 crore (28.9% margin) and PAT INR 168 crore (7.9% margin). Same-store sales growth was about 14%, split roughly equally between volume and value. Management guided to FY27 growth at a similar pace to FY26, EBITDA margins stable, 60 new facilities (40 surgical, 20 clinics), and a merger timeline of roughly Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Growth in FY27 expected to sustain at a similar pace to FY26, driven by micro-market penetration, new geographies and premium procedures.
EBITDA margins expected to stay stable in FY27 while greenfield expansion continues.
FY27 capex of INR 380-400 crore, including the new Chennai CMS facility.
FY27 acquisition-related deferred payments of about INR 60-65 crore; FY28-30 payments together about INR 60 crore.
Merger of Dr. Agarwal's Healthcare and Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital: shareholder/creditor meetings on July 2, 2026; NCLT sanction expected to conclude in about 5-6 months, i.e. by Q3 FY27.
Chennai CMS facility launch targeted by October 1, 2026, subject to approvals; 12-18 months needed to stabilise.
capex_capacity: FY26 surgery mix: 30 surgical centres opened; FY27 plan of 40 surgical centres (+33%) and 20 clinics, 60 in total, split 30 in H1 and 30 in H2.
Regional FY27 additions: South 24, North 16 (highest ever), West about 15; West and North to more than double additions versus FY26.
Eleven new facilities already launched in FY27 to date (including Faridabad, Ludhiana, Bikaner, Kollam, Mulshi, Nellore).
Delhi NCR: 7-8 more centres planned over 12-18 months; 30 letters of intent in hand for properties.
FY26 network: 269 facilities in India plus 19 in Africa; 19 greenfield openings in Q4 and 148 greenfield facilities added since FY23.
demand_pricing: SSSG of about 14% in FY26: volume about 7% (OPD growth about 5.5%, rest from surgical conversions) and value about 7% (premiumisation about 5.5%, price hikes 1-1.5%).
Average cataract revenue per eye is about INR 41,000-45,000; high-end cataract share rose to 26.3% of 62,800 cataract procedures (FY25: 22.5%).
Femto cataract procedures grew 87% YoY to over 5,900; lenticular (SMILE) refractive procedures grew 19%; retinal surgeries over 12,800 (+23%).
Refractive volumes grew more slowly than cataract; management is in talks with insurers for refractive coverage.
Walk-ins rose to about 10,000 patients a day from about 8,000 (+25%).
Payor mix FY26: 62.4% cash, 28.5% insurance/TPA, 9% government; domestic mix 72% cash.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex breakdown and the acquisition-related cash outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR 380-400 crore including the CMS facility; acquisition payments are about INR 60-65 crore, versus about INR 85 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What losses do new greenfield facilities carry, and will they recur?
qa_highlights.answer: New FY26 branches had unit-level operating losses of about INR 30 crore (FY25 cohort about INR 21 crore). Management expects a similar drag in FY27, with per-branch losses falling from FY27 onwards, mainly in Delhi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise in the listed subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 one-off merger costs of about INR 80 lakh; corporate office rent of about INR 1 crore for the year; about INR 3.3 crore extra Facebook marketing spend. Merger costs are one-off, rent recurs.

qa_highlights.question: Are the FY27 facility additions all organic, and how many facilities closed in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: All 60 planned centres are organic; partner deals are not in the pipeline. Five eye clinics were closed in FY26, and AEHL's rental outflow for FY27 is about INR 32 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What limits the pace of openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Real estate at the right cost and compliance with state clinical licences, which can delay openings. Management will ramp up only if the new centres perform.

risks_watch: New-facility drag of about INR 30-40 crore per year could weigh on margins if FY27 openings are weighted to Delhi NCR and the North.
Chennai CMS facility approvals; launch targeted by October 1, 2026, and the timeline already slipped due to election code-of-conduct delays.
Refractive softness relative to cataract; insurance coverage for refractive is still under negotiation.
Paramedical attrition of 21-25% and fixed increments of about 9.5-10%.
Merger completion depends on the July 2, 2026 meetings and final NCLT sanction, expected around Q3 FY27.
Cash-to-insurance mix and the sustainability of about 1.5% price hikes alongside premiumisation.
544350|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and the FY27 pipeline, with specific numbers given readily. Management was more cautious on the timing of approvals (Chennai CMS, merger) and on new-facility losses, and deferred some questions (FY27 new-market count, FY25 subsidiary Q4 cost detail) for later follow-up.
key_quotes: For the first time in our company's history, we crossed over INR 2,000 crores of revenue, a milestone made possible by the trust of over 30 lakh patients and the dedication of every doctor and team member across our network.
On the margin front, we expect our EBITDA margins to stay stable even as we continue to invest aggressively in greenfield expansion, reflecting the underlying operating leverage in our model.
The biggest bottleneck for us, obviously, will be getting the right real estate because one is you want to ensure that you get the right real estate at the right cost.

544350|2026-06.headline: Dr. Agarwal's Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 26% YoY to INR614 crores, with Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores (28.5% margin) and PAT margin at 8.9%.
544350|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered revenue from operations of INR614 crores (+26% YoY, +8.8% QoQ) and Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores (+25.2% YoY), with EBITDA margin up 30 bps to 28.5%. PAT margin expanded 127 bps to 8.9% despite greenfield losses of about INR20 crores at corporate EBITDA level. The company commissioned 18 new facilities (16 surgical), a record for a single quarter, and reiterated a FY27 plan of 60 additions including 40 surgical centres. Same-store growth for the oldest cohort (pre-FY23) was 16.3%, driven roughly equally by volume and value.

segments.name: Spares and services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR39 crores, up 6.2% YoY; management is prioritising a higher AMC share from the installed base, but gave no quantified target.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share about 9% of Q1 revenue on first slip-form paver shipment. Algeria, Morocco and Nigeria about 38% of shipments; management targets about 30% CAGR over next three years, if not more.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 expected to be seasonally soft and a fairly challenging quarter for EBITDA; 12.5% margin looks challenging in Q2.
Margins expected to return to about 12.5% corridor from Q3 FY27 if volumes improve.
Full-year EBITDA margin of 12% described as challenging; management said too early to call full-year numbers.
Non-SLCM growth target of about 10-15% YoY on a lower base; H2 expected to be better than H1.
Long-term EBITDA margin corridor of 13-15% reiterated; Q4 FY26 cited as about 15%.
Another calibrated price increase under evaluation, with some action targeted within Q2 FY27; about 60% of revenue typically comes in H2.
capex_capacity: ARGO 4000 launch planned in Q2 FY27 to fill a portfolio gap.
Manufacturing consolidated under one leader; Obadenahalli plant head now oversees procurement and supply chain.
Strategic inventory built in first few months for products with imported components; no large strategic steel purchase made at current prices.
Cash above INR1,100 crores; management actively pursuing inorganic opportunities with guardrails, no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Industry SLCM registrations down 27% YoY in Q1; AJAX down 21%. Second-ranked player lost about 0.7% share; Conmat and Venus gained share.

State-wise: Maharashtra and MP volumes declined (MP about 50%) but share rose; Gujarat volumes up about 40% with share 71% to 82%; Rajasthan volumes down 21% with share 66% to 86%; Odisha share 61% to 88% with volume up 13%; UP down about 7%.
Application mix: roads about 40-43%, urban infra 15-20% and buildings 10-15% (now about 35-40% combined per management, up from 15-20%).
Contractors facing payment delays from some state governments; government infrastructure spending below budget.
Steel E250 and E350 prices have risen; fuel prices also up. Price increase of about 2% taken in Q4 FY26.
Management said it is not playing the price game and prefers installation over discounting.

qa_highlights.question: Is non-SLCM growth targeted at 20-30% for the year given the low base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would be happy with 10-15% growth in non-SLCM on a lower base, with H2 expected better than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 17% on flat revenue?

qa_highlights.question: Why did a peer grow volume about 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the peer grows in pick-and-carry cranes, not SLCM; AJAX's SLCM decline was in line with industry registrations being down 27%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for Q2, Q3 and full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 12.5% margin looks challenging; margins to return to about 12.5% from Q3 if volumes improve; 12% for full year also looks challenging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steel and pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel prices rose; management hopes for softening after US primaries in September-November; a calibrated price increase is planned, likely starting within Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Are inorganic opportunities being pursued aggressively given the cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is aggressively pursuing inorganic opportunities within guardrails and will update when clear.

risks_watch: Continued SLCM volume decline (industry -27%, AJAX -21%) and weak Maharashtra and MP volumes.
Steel and fuel cost inflation with unclear timing of price increases and possible competitive pushback.
Government payment delays to contractors and under-spending on infrastructure.
Recovery of deferred non-SLCM volumes expected August-September; need to verify.
Export revenue recognition timing and country/currency risk.
Investor-call audio quality issues reported by several participants during the call.

544367|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore (INR 1,007 cr, +157% YoY) with 23.5% EBITDA margin, despite a INR 25.7 crore non-cash Ind AS 29 charge.
544367|2026-03.overview: Management reported first-ever INR 1,000 crore+ annual consolidated revenue, FY26 EBITDA of INR 236 crore (up 98%) and PAT of INR 185 crore (up 85%), above the revised guidance of about INR 900 crore revenue and 22% margin. Q4 was the highest-ever quarter at about INR 310 crore total revenue, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 19.1% from 27.9% in Q3 because of a INR 25.7 crore Ind AS 29 net monetary loss at Turkish subsidiary Endoks and one-time Labour Code provisions. Order book exiting FY26 was above INR 1,400 crore. FY27 guidance is muted at about 15-20% growth as new capacity ramps, with management expecting above 50% growth in FY28.

segments.name: Quality Power (standalone, incl. projects)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 246 crore per management; EBIT margin about 33% for Quality Power and 21% for QP projects. Order book above INR 520 crore, with data-centre order book about INR 520 crore cited in Q&A.

segments.name: Mehru Electrical and Mechanical Engineers
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 318 crore; margin about 20% in Q4 and 15% for the year; annualised EBIT margin about 15%. Order book about INR 430 crore; management sees only 30-35% further capacity headroom at current plant.

segments.name: Endoks Energy (Turkey)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 468 crore; reported EBIT margin 23% including Ind AS 29 effect, about 29-30% without it; management cites about 32% EBITDA on stable-currency basis. Order book about INR 450 crore; Q4 cash flow about INR 136 crore.

segments.name: Sukrut (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Turnaround underway; losses halved versus last year and management targets 70-75% growth this year without losses.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 15-20% growth in revenue and margin band of 15-20%, reflecting an S-curve stabilisation year; growth to resume above 50% in FY28 (management said this is 'correct' when asked).
Order book target of INR 1,500-1,800 crore before start of FY27 per management.
Expect some near-term gross margin pressure in Q1-Q2 FY27 from raw material and commodity price increases; pass-through to customers is with a lag.

Targeted BESS converter orders of USD 60-80 million this year against USD 31 million current BESS order book; PCS factory in Turkey (about USD 2 million investment) expected to start billing by Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27.
Dividend: final dividend of INR 1 per share recommended; promoters waived their entitlement.
capex_capacity: New Sangli factory (global coil, HVDC, PCS, CTC, magnet wire) expected to commence operations around July-August 2026; management also said trial production by end-2026 and project managers stick to Dec-Jan start; commissioning on track for Q3 FY27 per CFO.
New high-voltage test laboratory to be commissioned alongside the new factory.

Mehru: additional oven capacity post-September 2026; GIS manufacturing and testing infrastructure with first prototypes around July-August 2026; INR 17.2 crore capex for GIS and HV testing equipment. Current plant saturation at about 30-35% above FY26 output of about INR 320 crore.
Endoks: new PCS facility at Nigde targeted for December 2026; new BESS manufacturing facility on in-house technology; 1,725 kW PCS inverter expected to launch within next two quarters.
Capital WIP of INR 73 crore; management says Sangli peak revenue potential of about INR 1,500 crore subject to CTC cable expansion and insulator supply.
demand_pricing: Order book exiting FY26 above INR 1,400 crore (about 1.4x FY26 revenue); Q4 order intake about INR 870 crore per corrected figure, with INR 300 crore executed in the quarter.
Pipeline of opportunities above INR 1,100 crore for QP alone across FACTS, renewables and data centres; demand cited across Middle East, Europe, US and Australia.
BESS: management sees BESS PCS as 40-50% of project cost; converter margins about 10-12% at bid level, targeted to reach 17-18% at volume; battery pass-through about 2-3%.

Data centres: first US data-centre order of about INR 49 crore won; management expects a couple more projects in coming quarters; US reactor market for data centres sized at about INR 1,500 crore per year by management.

Supply chain constraints: insulator deliveries running 18-24 months; cable constraints mitigated by vertical integration. Order intake in Sangli and Delhi largely closed for next quarter; only strategic orders being taken.
Transformer bids in US (USD 80-100 million) were largely lost; management is not prioritising transformers at lower margins.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the BESS and data-centre opportunity and what products will be supplied?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS order book about USD 31 million with a further USD 30-50 million expected by year-end; management targets USD 60-80 million of orders this year and sees a billion-dollar opportunity. Data-centre orders are booked out with 6-7 month delivery timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the BESS competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Chinese players are seen as the largest competition; GE is at a high price level and not yet competed with directly. Company says it competes on software/EMS and service in Europe, US and Australia.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of about 15-20% growth in FY27; traditional HV margins are steady with a couple of points of pressure from conflict-related price increases; BESS converter margins are in an investment phase.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 revenue flat QoQ and what is the Endoks seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mehru's Q4 is its highest-profit quarter and Endoks' Q1 is seasonally muted; it reports Endoks on a Jan-Dec basis so QoQ comparison is not like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fundraising plan given about INR 250 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: The USD 75 million enabling resolution is a dry-powder authorisation, not an immediate raise; company says it will draw much lower than the cap, cash is needed for organic growth and acquisitions, and it prefers zero debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other expenses increase in Q4 beyond the Ind AS 29 charge?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said freight outward of about INR 12 crore and liquidated damages of about INR 5 crore (pre-acquisition Mehru item, since curtailed) also rose other expenses; net monetary loss was INR 25 crore.

risks_watch: Ind AS 29 treatment at Endoks creates quarter-to-quarter swings in other expenses and reported margins (Q3 net monetary gain vs Q4 loss of INR 25.7 crore); management states it is non-cash and symmetric, but reported margins will fluctuate with index movements.
Supply chain: insulator lead times of 18-24 months and winding conductor shortages are delaying projects; management said the board is considering an insulator solution without details.
Raw material and commodity price inflation with a lag in pass-through; management flagged possible Q1-Q2 FY27 margin dip, with no price-variation clauses noted by analysts.
Commissioning timelines slipping: Sangli plant guided to July-August 2026 with trial production by end-2026; Endoks Nigde PCS facility targeted December 2026.
Turkey geopolitical exposure: management says operations are stable after 16 years, but analysts flagged India-Turkey tensions; Turkey also hosts BESS PCS ramp.

Governance and dilution: promoters and management waived incremental salary (second year) and dividend entitlement tied to the fundraise; enabling resolution for USD 75 million; BDNA committee evaluating acquisitions larger than cash on hand.
Disclosure inconsistencies to verify: order inflow quoted as INR 600 crore then corrected to INR 870 crore; Mehru and Endoks EBIT and EBITDA margin figures were given on differing bases.

544367|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue INR256.4 crore with reported PAT INR46.7 crore; gross margin rose to 47.2% and order book stood at INR1,945 crore.
544367|2026-06.overview: Revenue was INR256.4 crore and reported EBITDA INR64.7 crore (25.2% margin). Excluding a INR7.82 crore non-cash Ind AS 29 hyperinflation loss on Turkish operations, management cited adjusted EBITDA of INR72.5 crore (28.3%) and PAT of INR54.5 crore. The order book closed at INR1,945 crore, about 1.9x last year's revenue. Sangli machinery installation is under way with trial production targeted this month, but customer audits mean meaningful volume is guided for Q3-Q4. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20% and standalone EBITDA of around 20% or high teens, and flagged likely temporary margin moderation in Q3 from new capacity fixed costs and aluminium pass-through.

financial_highlights.change: Year-on-year growth not stated for group; Quality Power standalone rose from INR37 crore to INR69 crore per management
Increased; to rise as Sangli and Endoks capacity is capitalised

financial_highlights.value: INR1,945 crore (Endoks INR801 crore, Mehru INR585 crore, Quality Power standalone INR553 crore)

segments.name: Quality Power standalone
segments.commentary: Order book INR553 crore; standalone revenue INR69 crore per management, up from INR37 crore. Management expects standalone EBITDA of around 20% and flagged Q3 margin moderation from Sangli fixed costs and aluminium cost lag.

segments.name: Mehru
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR83 crore, up from about INR60 crore. Q1 EBITDA about 18% versus internal target of 22-23%, hit by copper and oil price spikes in April; revised guidance to around 18%. Order book INR585 crore; capacity near 100% utilisation.

segments.name: Endoks (Turkey, power electronics / BESS)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR107 crore revenue; Turkish revenue dipped slightly due to Eid holidays. Order book INR801 crore. Power conversion system facility civil works complete, operations expected Q3 FY27. Pipeline about USD60 million BESS PCS orders, with USD40 million more expected in 12 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20%; management declined to raise it before Q3, saying revision may come then.
Margin guidance: model around 20% or high-teens EBITDA; coil products stable guidance about 20%, with most recent orders booked above 25%.
Q3 FY27 standalone margin moderation expected from new Sangli fixed costs and aluminium cost pass-through; margins expected to normalise as utilisation rises over the next 15 months.
Sangli coil facility: trial production targeted this month; commercial revenue to trickle in from Q3, meaningful from Q4. Peak revenue potential about INR1,500-1,800 crore.
HVDC magnet wire facility: full production targeted by Q4 FY27 after three to five months of stabilisation.

WS Insulators acquisition: consolidation expected from Q4 FY27 after SEZ approvals; EV about INR315 crore. Insulator order target of about INR200 crore over next nine months; standalone potential INR250-300 crore without capex, INR450-500 crore with capex.
Management indicated FY28 growth guidance of 50%, pending order book and delivery timelines.
Order book slated for completion in about 15 months.
Interim dividend of INR0.25 per share declared.
capex_capacity: Sangli new facility: machinery installation in progress; last-mile issues around sequencing, utilities and statutory approvals; building completion certificate pending. Approvals and about 60 global customer audits expected to take about six months; initial ISO/OHSAS audits about one month.
HVDC CTC magnet wire facility at Sangli: machinery installation commencing; full production targeted Q4 FY27.

Endoks PCS facility: civil complete; interiors and power electronics fit-out in progress; facility estimated at about USD70-80 million revenue capacity for about USD2 million capex plus about USD1 million further spend.
Winwin Speciality (Vizag, SEZ): about 40 acres of land; planned INR50 crore capex for capacity; about 120 people on site.
Possible second facility decision (Turkey or Vizag for European and export markets) in 6-7 months.
Fundraise of less than INR500 crore planned, including Winwin acquisition funding, INR50 crore capex and US sales entry; roadshows from 20 August and raise targeted before AGM.
demand_pricing: Demand strong across businesses; energy storage at Endoks has inquiry levels ahead of expectations. Data-centre bids of about USD100 million seen, but 12-month delivery periods limit participation for now.
Two large HVDC programmes expected: one partly awarded (expected Q3-Q4) and Barmer tender close to award. About half a dozen STATCOM projects in talks across US, Europe and Australia.
Management said order acceptance is not the constraint; capacity ramp is. Factories sit on close to two years of order book at current capacity.
Every executable order in the book was booked above the margin guidance communicated to the market; pricing discipline maintained.
Group procurement consolidation (CPO appointed) expected to lower aluminium casting and other input costs; about INR3 crore of volume discounts benefited Q1.
Chinese HVDC bidders: management views the four Chinese entities allowed to bid as non-operational with limited near-term threat; local content norms unchanged at 60-70%.

qa_highlights.question: Break up YoY revenue growth between Endoks, Mehru and Quality Power, and re-explain the Q3 margin pressure.
qa_highlights.answer: Quality Power standalone went from INR37 crore to INR69 crore, Mehru from about INR60 crore to about INR83 crore, and Endoks contributed about INR107 crore; Turkish revenue dipped slightly due to Eid holidays. Margin caution for Q3 relates to aluminium spikes that flow through about four to five months later, while coil products stable guidance is about 20% with recent orders above 25%.

qa_highlights.question: When will the order book reflect the enlarged capacity, and when can order book to billing be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to two large HVDC programmes (one partly awarded, expected Q3-Q4; Barmer near award) and about half a dozen STATCOM projects; order intake is not the constraint, and orders will be taken more actively once Sangli is stabilised around Q3. Order book is slated for completion in about 15 months; management would not commit to a book-to-bill ratio.

qa_highlights.question: Sangli coil and HVDC magnet wire commissioning timelines and peak asset turns?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production is targeted this month pending building completion certificate; ISO/OHSAS initial audits take about one month and about 60 customer audits take about six months. HVDC magnet wire needs three to five months of stabilisation with full production targeted by Q4 FY27. Peak revenue potential for Sangli is about INR1,500-1,800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: BESS scalability at Endoks and execution cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Pipeline is about USD60 million of PCS orders, with another USD40 million expected in the next 12 months, against earlier guidance of at least USD80 million. BESS orders execute in about six to nine months, faster than the core business; IGBT supply is the bottleneck and BESS in India is targeted by end of next year.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue guidance, margin guidance and FY28 growth; can revenue reach INR1,400 crore this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 20% FY27 growth and asked investors to model 20% or high-teens EBITDA, with a possible revision at Q3. On FY28, management pointed to the order book and delivery timelines; an analyst's 50% figure was confirmed as the FY28 growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Endoks and Mehru margins, debt position and fundraise purpose and size?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehru delivered about 18% EBITDA versus an internal 22-23% target, and revised Mehru guidance to around 18%. Endoks' existing lines run around 25%, but blended margins will be clearer in Q3. Group debt was about INR23 crore; the raise, under INR500 crore with no number set, funds the WS acquisition, a INR50 crore capex and US sales entry, with roadshows from 20 August.

qa_highlights.question: Winwin (WS Insulators) rationale, margins, timing and capex.
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation expected from Q4 after SEZ approvals; purchase consideration about INR50-60 crore per management, and the EV was cited at about INR315 crore. Standalone potential is INR250-300 crore without capex and INR450-500 crore with capex; margins are currently 15-25% and should stabilise within about four quarters. Internal demand is about INR40-45 crore a year, and the insulator order target is at least INR200 crore over nine months.

Fundraise of under INR500 crore (roadshows from 20 August, raise before AGM) and US sales entry; size and use still not finalised.
Endoks PCS facility operational timing (Q3 FY27), no contribution guidance yet; Endoks margin not yet disclosed by segment; IGBT supply constraints.
Chinese HVDC bidder entry: management sees limited near-term threat, but local content norms at 60-70% and the policy remain watch items.

rows.why: Fundraise under INR500 crore (roadshows from 20 August, raise before AGM) with INR50 crore Winwin capex planned, and management said factories sit on close to two years of order book at current capacity, with a possible second facility decision in 6-7 months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to raise FY27 20% revenue growth before Q3, saying revision may come then, while the INR1,945 crore order book is about 1.9x last year's revenue and FY28 growth guidance is 50%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 standalone margin moderation guided from Sangli fixed costs and aluminium pass-through, and Mehru EBITDA was about 18% versus internal 22-23% target and already revised down to around 18%; FY27 20% revenue guidance held with revision deferred to Q3.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Endoks PCS facility operations expected Q3 FY27 with about USD70-80 million revenue capacity, HVDC CTC magnet wire full production by Q4 FY27, and BESS in India targeted by end of next year.

rows.label: Two large HVDC programmes and STATCOM pipeline
rows.why: One HVDC programme expected partly awarded in Q3-Q4 and Barmer tender near award, plus about half a dozen STATCOM projects in talks; BESS pipeline about USD60 million with another USD40 million expected in 12 months.

rows.label: Winwin / WS Insulators consolidation
rows.why: Consolidation expected from Q4 FY27 after SEZ approvals, with EV about INR315 crore and standalone insulator potential INR250-300 crore without capex and INR450-500 crore with capex; margins currently 15-25%.

rows.label: Sub-INR500 crore fundraise
rows.why: Raise under INR500 crore targeted before AGM to fund WS acquisition, INR50 crore capex and US sales entry, with group debt only about INR23 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, order intake and pricing discipline but cautious on numbers, declining to raise FY27 guidance and deferring Sangli and Endoks margin targets to Q3; analysts pushed on the YoY revenue split, Q3 margin pressure, Mehru's miss, and the path to a 50% FY28.

544370|2026-03.headline: Nukleus FY26 total income rose 25.49% YoY to INR 36.19 crore, with PAT of INR 213.53 lakh and EBITDA of INR 917.34 lakh.
544370|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong growth in income and EBITDA, with management attributing margin expansion mainly to technology-led sales and operating productivity. Operational footprint is about 25 centres (17 co-working, 8 managed office) across Delhi NCR and Bengaluru, with roughly 7.3 lakh sq ft under management, about 3.06 lakh sq ft operational (figures differ across answers), and occupancy near 85%. Management is shifting the mix toward managed office and back-to-back deals, guiding to about 10 lakh sq ft operational by end FY27, but declined to give revenue numbers for that capacity. Several slides had revenue-mix errors that management said would be corrected later.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 92.75 lakh earlier; management stated about 8% increase, which conflicts with the figures quoted

segments.name: Co-working
segments.commentary: Management said co-working grows about 10% a year and carries the highest margin (illustratively about 30%). Its share of the portfolio is falling, from about 70% at IPO to roughly 50% now.

segments.name: Managed office
segments.commentary: Growing about 30-40% a year per management. Targeted to reach about 70% of portfolio in the expansion phase and about 90% over 3-4 years. Illustrative margin about 25%.

segments.name: Back-to-back / enterprise deals
segments.commentary: Illustrative margin about 20%. Landlord-funded fit-outs and revenue-sharing deals are increasing, reducing Nukleus's capex needs.

guidance_outlook: Operational area is expected to reach more than 10 lakh sq ft by end FY27, up from about 3.5 lakh sq ft now; management said this is a 10x rise from the IPO's about 1 lakh sq ft.
Management declined to give a revenue estimate for the current 3.5 lakh sq ft, saying it was too early to quantify.
Management said it intends to sustain the pace of square-footage addition for at least five years, without giving a percentage target.
Plans to expand beyond Delhi NCR and Bengaluru into Pune and Hyderabad, and eventually be a national brand in major cities.
Management said it will be among the biggest operators in three years, without quantifying this.
Management said accounts will move to Ind AS in FY27.
capex_capacity: Centre set-up takes about 3 months; bookings start around month 2; occupancy typically reaches a good level within about 6 months of opening.
Around 7 lakh sq ft under management; about 3.06 lakh sq ft operational per the presentation, while the call cited 3.5-3.6 lakh sq ft operational; the rest is CWIP or under development.
Committed area of about 7.5 lakh sq ft against about 2.5 lakh sq ft expected at IPO; RHP commitment was 1.04 lakh sq ft and the company said it delivered 1.24 lakh sq ft.
Flagship centres include Noida Sector 142 (about 1.5-2 lakh sq ft inventory), Logic Cyber Park, Skymark, IFCO Tower Gurugram and Prestige Blue Chip Bengaluru (Dairy Circle).
demand_pricing: Management cited office leasing of 82.6 million sq ft in CY2025, with GCCs taking about 44% of Q1 2026 absorption (9.1 million sq ft, 48% in Bengaluru).
Management said it is equipped to serve current GCC requirements and has started participating in RFPs; no GCC client signed yet, though it expects to sign its first one soon.
Pricing is set manually per centre to target 85-95% occupancy; dynamic pricing is not used and management said it is four to five years away for the sector.
Management said managed-office clients sign 4-9 year agreements, with revenue starting from day one and no vacancy gap for back-to-back deals.
Management said the client base has moved from startups and SMEs toward Fortune 500 and blue-chip companies, without naming clients.

qa_highlights.question: How will finance costs and leverage evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said finance cost rose to about INR 11.5 lakh from INR 92.75 lakh, described as an 8% increase, while long-term borrowings grew materially. The figures quoted do not reconcile, so the change needs checking against the filed accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What ROCE is targeted on new fixed-asset investment, and when do new centres stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: No ROCE target was given. Management said centres take about 3 months to build, reach a good occupancy level in about 6 months, and that revenue impact from the 10 lakh sq ft pipeline will fall mainly in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain came from operations versus accounting adjustments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed most of the gain to productivity. An AI call-filter reportedly cut calls handled per salesperson by 60-70%. No capitalisation adjustment was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand-based dynamic pricing used, and how does Nukleus compete with larger players?
qa_highlights.answer: Dynamic pricing is not used. Management said the largest operator holds about 1.5 crore sq ft and nobody in the sector is large yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current operational area, and how much will be managed office vs co-working?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 7 lakh sq ft under management, about 3.5 lakh sq ft operational, and over 10 lakh sq ft operational by end FY27, with a mix moving toward 70% managed office and 30% co-working.

qa_highlights.question: Why focus on managed office, and what are the margins and contract terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said managed office and back-to-back deals deliver scale and longer contracts, while co-working has higher per-sq-ft profit but is slow to grow. Contracts run 4-9 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will Nukleus adopt Ind AS and use NDS-based EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Nipun Gupta said the accounts will be converted to Ind AS in this financial year (FY27).

risks_watch: Inconsistent figures: the operational area was stated as 3.06 lakh, 3.5 lakh and 3.6 lakh sq ft in different parts of the call; the revenue-mix slide was flagged for correction; and the finance-cost numbers do not reconcile.
Execution risk on the pipeline of more than 10 lakh sq ft operational by end FY27, given a 3-6 month occupancy ramp and the need to fill newly added space.
Rising debt to fund expansion, with management not giving a leverage target and ROCE falling as capital employed grew.
No GCC client signed yet despite RFP participation; GCC conversion is a key watch item.
Related-party and governance questions: a management board member (Pooja Gupta) handles finance, and the company is only about a year post-SME listing.
544370|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, technology and national ambitions, but cautious and evasive on numbers: it declined to quantify revenue potential, ROCE targets and client names, and admitted errors in its slides.
key_quotes: So, during the financial year, all the money that we took from the market has been deployed effectively.
We will be one of the biggest in next three years. That is what I can assure you today.
I think there will be a significant growth is better put, putting a number to this is something I don't think is a good idea at this kind of a stage.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H2 FY26 EBITDA rose 35.16% YoY to INR 507.85 lakh on income of INR 1,888.35 lakh (about 27% margin), but management attributed gains to productivity without quantifying the margin, and the mix shift to managed office (about 25% illustrative margin) is below co-working (about 30%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Operational area is guided to more than 10 lakh sq ft by end FY27 from about 3.06-3.5 lakh sq ft now, with centres already under construction (about 7 lakh sq ft under management and committed area of 7.5 lakh sq ft), though the figures are inconsistent across the call.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Managed office is growing 30-40% a year and co-working about 10% a year, with occupancy about 85% (target 85-95%) and H2 FY26 total income up 30.12% YoY to INR 1,888.35 lakh.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 85% and fixed assets rose 160.71% YoY to INR 3,525.36 lakh, while the company is expanding into Pune and Hyderabad, so further capacity commitments are likely; landlord-funded and revenue-share deals are reducing Nukleus's own capex needs, which tempers this.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no revenue figure for the 10 lakh sq ft pipeline and declined to quantify revenue potential, so there is no numeric guidance to raise; revenue impact is expected mainly in FY27-FY28.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Execution risk on the 10 lakh sq ft pipeline given a 3-6 month occupancy ramp, rising debt, and figures that do not reconcile (operational area stated as 3.06, 3.5 and 3.6 lakh sq ft; finance cost INR 11.5 lakh vs INR 92.75 lakh).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Expansion into Pune and Hyderabad and a national brand ambition are stated, but no timing or unit count was given; no GCC client has been signed yet despite RFP participation.

rows.label: First GCC client signing
rows.why: Management is participating in RFPs and expects to sign its first GCC client soon, with GCCs taking about 44% of Q1 2026 absorption (9.1 million sq ft), but no client is signed yet.

rows.label: Rising debt and ROCE dilution
rows.why: Long-term borrowings grew materially and ROCE fell as capital employed rose, with no leverage target given, so balance sheet pressure is more likely to persist than ease.

rows.label: Ind AS conversion in FY27
rows.why: Management confirmed accounts will move to Ind AS in FY27, which could change reported EBITDA and PAT comparability against the current figures.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 10 lakh sq ft expansion, technology-led productivity and national ambitions, but cautious and evasive on revenue potential, ROCE, client names and finance-cost figures, and admitted slide errors; analysts pushed on the inconsistent numbers and finance costs.

544387|2026-03.headline: Desco Infratech H2 FY26 revenue rose 99.28% YoY to INR 118.79 crore, with PAT of INR 16.38 crore, though margins were squeezed by new power distribution and solar EPC work.
544387|2026-03.overview: Management reported half-year/full-year FY26 revenue of INR 118.79 crore (up 99.28% YoY), EBIT of INR 23.43 crore (up 76.30%) and PAT of INR 16.38 crore (up 80.87%). CGD EPC contributed INR 83.24 crore and power distribution plus solar EPC INR 35.37 crore. Management attributed margin compression to the H2 entry into power distribution and solar EPC, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 70-80% YoY. Operating cash flow stayed negative at roughly INR 18-19 crore, which management called growth-driven, with a promise of improvement. Management also outlined a CBG build-out (2 TPD commissioning in Q1 FY27, plus 15-18 TPD of planned expansion) and new subsidiaries in the UAE and India.

financial_highlights.change: Improved to roughly 3-4.5% of revenue per management, from approx INR 12 crore negative last year

financial_highlights.metric: Power distribution and solar EPC revenue

segments.name: City gas distribution (CGD) EPC
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 83.24 crore of FY26 revenue with management citing PAT margin of about 15.3%. Management guides CGD at 60-65% of revenue in FY27 and beyond; the order book has about INR 330-332 crore in CGD, with EPC timelines of 18-24 months and O&M of 24 months.

segments.name: Power distribution and solar EPC
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 35.37 crore, started in H2 FY26, with management citing EBITDA margins of about 9.5-10% (on a PAT basis in one answer) and 20% EBITDA margin on a later answer, which was not reconciled. Working capital days are 10-15 versus 30-35 for CGD; order book is about INR 1 year execution timeline.

segments.name: CBG (compressed biogas) via SGAEPL and Desco Biogreen
segments.commentary: First 2 TPD plant to commission in Q1 FY27 (delayed 15-25 days, targeting end-May, June at latest). Capex about INR 3.5-4 crore, opex about INR 60-65 lakh, revenue about INR 1.4-1.5 lakh per day, PAT margin 22-23% claimed, payback 3.5-4 years. Management expects CBG revenue of about INR 170 crore by FY30.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 70-80% YoY, described by management as conservative.
Management targets INR 1,000 crore revenue by 2030 (may slip about 1 year), citing PNG penetration of only 6.5% and a government mandate of 12-15% by 2030 and 25-30% by 2040.
Operating cash flow expected to be at par or slightly positive next year, and positive within about two years, per management.
Debt-to-equity may rise to a maximum of 0.3x over about 1.5 years as structured debt is raised.
CBG breakeven (EBITDA and PAT) expected within 18-20 months.
Expansion of 15-18 TPD CBG capacity (12 TPD Gujarat and 4-5 TPD Madhya Pradesh) with about INR 25 crore capex, funded via bank debt, not equity; cost of debt expected to fall to 8.5-9.5% from 16-17%.
capex_capacity: CBG 2 TPD plant in SGAEPL to be commissioned in Q1 FY27, capex about INR 3.5-4 crore, with one PSU LOA for 5 TPD capacity cited.

Planned additional 15-20 TPD CBG capacity over about 18 months: MOU signed in South Gujarat (capex INR 12-15 crore) and talks with farmers in Dhar, Madhya Pradesh (capex about INR 9 crore), MOU expected within about 30 days.
Desco Global FZ-LLC (Ras Al Khaimah) incorporated; EPC work there delayed due to the Middle East crisis, with no investment made so far.
Desco Biogreen Private Limited incorporated for sustainability-oriented segments; management said SGAEPL may later merge into it.
demand_pricing: CGD order book about INR 330-332 crore out of total INR 345 crore order book; power distribution and solar make up the rest. Pipeline of about INR 650 crore, of which about INR 470-480 crore is CGD and about INR 100 crore is solar and power distribution, with tenders delayed by the Middle East crisis.
Customer mix in CGD order book: about 70-72% PSU/semi-government (BPCL, GAIL, IOCL, IGL) and 25-28% private (Torrent, Adani, and others). KP Group cited as a key power and solar client.
Management said it is declining low-margin orders in CGD amid crisis-driven demand, and is now providing surety bonds rather than bank guarantees.
Likhitha Infra named as a direct competitor that management described as stronger; management plans to take share from it, though it does not regard it as a rival.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cash flow and the INR 1,000 crore revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said negative cash flow is growth-led, from working capital in project ramp-ups; operating cash outflow improved to about INR 18-19 crore on INR 118 crore revenue, and it expects at-par or slightly positive operating cash flow next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin contraction and the revenue mix going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the squeeze to H2 entry into power distribution and solar EPC, and said CGD will remain 60-65% of revenue in FY27 with the rest from power distribution and solar.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost and timeline of the unsecured NBFC borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NBFC loans at about 16-17% per annum fund 90-120 day solar EPC projects; it plans to restructure debt after H1 and repay from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book mix and execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Of INR 345 crore, about INR 330-332 crore is CGD (EPC 18-24 months, O&M about INR 35-40 crore over 24 months); power distribution averages a 1-year timeline.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors view the margin sustainability in solar and power distribution given tender-based bidding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable and it will avoid aggressive bidding, accepting only selected work; it quoted about 20% EBITDA margin for this business versus 23% last year, as stated by the analyst.

qa_highlights.question: What are the CBG economics and expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 2 TPD capex of INR 3.5-4 crore, revenue of INR 1.4-1.5 lakh per day, 22-23% PAT margin, and a 3.5-4 year payback, with 15-18 TPD expansion requiring about INR 25 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital profile and why are receivables high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CGD working capital days are about 30-35 versus 10-15 for power and solar; high receivables reflect unbilled work-in-progress from O&M jobs started on January 1, 2026, and retention amounts released after a 36-48 month defect liability period.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow remains negative at about INR 18-19 crore; receivables and work-in-progress are rising with revenue, and collections depend on certification.
Margin dilution from the shift to power distribution and solar EPC, with management citing 9.5-10% margin and also 20% EBITDA for the same business; the two figures are not reconciled in the call.
Dependence on high-cost NBFC unsecured borrowings at 16-17%; refinancing to 8.5-9.5% is not yet secured.
Middle East crisis is delaying tenders (about INR 100 crore solar and power pipeline) and the UAE subsidiary's EPC work.
Ambitious FY27 growth of 70-80% and INR 1,000 crore by 2030 target against a current order book of about INR 345 crore.
Promoter stake increase and any equity raise remain unclear; management declined to comment on equity.
544387|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, with frequent forward-looking claims (for example, 70-80% growth and INR 1,000 crore by 2030) that are not backed by detailed quantified bridges. Answers on margins, cash flow and working capital were often hedged or repetitive, and several figures were restated inconsistently during the call.
key_quotes: The negative cash flow is primarily due to the growth led and not because of the stress led.
So yes, what I foresee is INR 1,000 crores we will be able to achieve easily by 2030.
We are consciously about not chasing low margin growths.

We will definitely look out for the greatest of the margins where we basically improve our margins in gas because this crisis times in the times of crisis are the time where you can be like where the opportunity arises.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Margins were squeezed by H2 entry into power distribution and solar EPC, with management citing EBITDA of about 9.5-10% and 20% in different answers, unreconciled, and the mix shifting toward these lower-margin lines while CGD stays at 60-65% of FY27 revenue.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 for the 2 TPD CBG plant; 15-20 TPD expansion over ab
rows.why: The 2 TPD SGAEPL CBG plant is set to commission in Q1 FY27 (delayed 15-25 days, targeting end-May/June) on INR 3.5-4 crore capex, and 15-20 TPD more is planned over about 18 months on INR 25 crore capex with an MOU signed in South Gujarat.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 70-80% YoY, backed by a INR 345 crore order book (INR 330-332 crore CGD) against FY26 revenue of INR 118.79 crore, though the INR 650 crore pipeline is partly delayed by the Middle East crisis.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management guided a 15-18 TPD CBG expansion (12 TPD Gujarat, 4-5 TPD Madhya Pradesh) for about INR 25 crore, with the MOU expected within about 30 days and debt funding planned, so further announcements are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: The 70-80% FY27 growth guide is already described as conservative by management, but the order book of INR 345 crore and the Middle East tender delays give no visible basis for raising it yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Operating cash flow is negative at about INR 18-19 crore, the Middle East crisis is delaying about INR 100 crore of solar and power tenders and the UAE EPC work, and the INR 1,000 crore 2030 target may slip about 1 year.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The 2 TPD CBG plant commissioning in Q1 FY27 and the Desco Biogreen sustainability segment are the new lines, but no specific product launches were discussed beyond these.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turns positive
rows.why: Operating cash flow was about INR 18-19 crore negative on INR 118.79 crore revenue, and management expects it at par or slightly positive next year and positive within about two years, but collections depend on certification and retention of 36-48 months.

rows.label: Refinance NBFC debt at lower cost
rows.why: NBFC borrowings cost 16-17% and management plans to restructure after H1 and repay from accruals, with bank debt at 8.5-9.5% targeted, but neither is secured yet; debt-to-equity may rise to 0.3x over about 1.5 years.

rows.label: UAE subsidiary EPC work
rows.why: Desco Global FZ-LLC in Ras Al Khaimah has no investment made so far and its EPC work is delayed by the Middle East crisis.

tone.note: Management was confident on 70-80% FY27 growth, the INR 1,000 crore 2030 target and CBG economics, but hedged on margins, cash flow and working capital, while analysts pushed on the unreconciled 9.5-10% versus 20% margin figures and the negative operating cash flow.

544396|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 2.4x YoY to INR 68.46 crore; FY26 revenue about INR 209 crore with EBITDA near INR 65 crore, with management guiding ~70% CAGR to INR 850-900 crore by FY29.
544396|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a transformation year, shifting mix away from PPaaS toward TSP, with international, SaaS and RegTech as the planned growth drivers. Q4 revenue was about INR 68.46 crore, EBITDA INR 19.26 crore and net profit INR 12.24 crore, and the call noted Q4 as the lowest EBITDA margin quarter. FY26 operating cash flow was negative, which management attributed to longer TSP credit periods. Management guided to ~70% revenue CAGR over three years, with the first-year (FY27) run-rate on the order of INR 340-350 crore, and said the mix shift would lift margins over time.

financial_highlights.change: full-year EBITDA margin cited at 31% vs 37% prior year (analyst figure)
net profit fell 9.7% per analyst question; PAT margin about 20% vs 25%
reason: longer credit period in TSP business

financial_highlights.value: about 180 days expected going forward (analyst interpretation, not confirmed by management)
financial_highlights.change: expected to decline gradually as mix changes

segments.name: TSP (Technology Service Provider)
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 90% of FY26 business per management; slide 17 shows TSP tapering to 30-40% of business contribution by FY29, with absolute value expected to rise. Carries longer credit periods and low-to-medium margins.

segments.name: PPaaS (Payment Platform as a Service)
segments.commentary: Management said more than a year of effort has not delivered desired results; engine being pivoted to domestic merchant orchestration and global PPaaS. Guided at 5-8% contribution in FY27-FY29 per analyst reading of slides; about 40+ accounts in funnel.

segments.name: RegTech
segments.commentary: AI-led RegTech product bought by one large public sector bank; close talks with multiple public and private banks. Purely SaaS; management expects revenue contribution from FY27 and guided 10-15% contribution range per analyst reading.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Zero base in FY26; guided to about 25% of business in FY27, 40% in FY28 and about 50% in FY29 per analyst reading. Management said about 40% of FY27 international business is already in hand, and bagged a large RegTech order including a central payment body abroad. Mix of license and SaaS.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of about 70% over three years; FY29 revenue INR 850-900 crore per management (analyst cited ~INR 950 crore), from FY26 base of about INR 209 crore.
FY27 growth of about 70% targeted; analyst-proposed FY27 range INR 340-350 crore accepted as 'anything around that range'.

EBITDA margin expected to rise over time to a range of roughly 40-50% at the end of the period, with the timing tied to Slide 17 blocks; management said FY26 margin pressure would reverse in FY27 and FY28, and that PAT margin returns to 25% by this financial year.
Operating cash flow conversion expected to improve as TSP credit periods shorten; no specific conversion figure given.
AI targets: 30% efficiency in support functions, 50% faster development, 1.5x capacity from existing business; RegTech AI revenue from FY27; revenue per employee up 300% in three years.
Market growth cited: payment processing 22% CAGR, RegTech ~32%, digital lending and orchestration above 40%.
capex_capacity: Investment in SaaS-based hosted engine targeted to reach at least 200 tenants in TSP verticals by FY29.
Pipeline of about 40+ PPaaS accounts and about 10 countries under international evaluation.
About 9 accounts added in Bank-in-a-Box and payment devices in Q4; about 2 PAC orders received recently; entered IoT-based payment solution with a new fintech.
Project expenses reportedly up about 60% in the presentation, attributed to new product line capacity and the PPaaS-to-TSP shift; management said new development is not charged to P&L.

Unallocated Tata Mutual Fund funds (INR 300 crore referenced by analyst): management said no inorganic deal has been signed; some deals rejected after due diligence; deployment expected in global assets and beyond-payments areas (RegTech, lending).
demand_pricing: Management said 8 of 10 RegTech pitches go into POC or sales pitch; described demand as a pseudo-mandate from bank CRO and CISO functions.
Competition in AI RegTech described as limited for now; management expects competition in about two years, citing three years of build effort.

International pricing: management said margins could run 25-50% higher than India-level margins, with some engagements at 50-60% higher; the company declined some licence deals with unfavourable payment terms.
Large OPEX deal signed in which revenue is triggered on each milestone; management expects lumpy quarters before a steadier base from FY28-FY29.
Management said credit period reflects TSP mix and will reduce with mix shift; analyst-cited receivable days of about 180 are not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 operating cash flow negative and what EBITDA-to-OCF conversion is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Aggarwal attributed it to the shift from PPaaS to TSP, which carries longer credit periods; expects conversion to improve gradually as international and other mix rises. No numeric conversion target given.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the 70% CAGR and when will EBITDA reach 33-35%?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Thakur said confidence is high given the funnel: about 200 SaaS tenants, about 10 international countries, and 40+ PPaaS accounts. Said full-year FY26 margin impact came from TSP mix, and balancing the year should bring EBITDA back to prior levels; no quarter given for 33-35%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the absolute revenue numbers for FY27-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 850-900 crore by end FY29 off the INR 209 crore FY26 base; the 70% CAGR is not uniform, with heavier triggers from large projects; FY27 about 70% growth targeted.

qa_highlights.question: How much of FY27 international revenue is already secured?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% is in hand at the start of the year, with the balance dependent on advanced discussions expected to convert in Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management defined high margin as above 70% over India margin, with international margins of 30-40% or more on a 15-20% India base; the gap is due to the product being roughly 5-6 years ahead of the target markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for PPaaS given weak results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pivoting PPaaS to merchant orchestration domestically and to global markets; two advanced discussions expected to close by end Q1 or early Q2; will not over-invest until results show.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profitability decline and what is the status of the Tata Mutual Fund funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin decline attributed to the mix shift from high-margin PPaaS to low-margin TSP. Some inorganic deals were rejected after due diligence; the company is looking for a deal that gives instant global presence and execution, or moves into RegTech and lending; no deployment made yet.

risks_watch: Negative FY26 operating cash flow and high TSP receivable days; watch for FY27 cash conversion and receivable day reduction.
FY27 revenue heavily dependent on international and large OPEX deal triggers, with about 60% of international FY27 business not yet secured.
Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin the lowest in the year; full-year margin fell to about 31% vs 37% prior; PAT margin down from 25% to about 20%.
