544397|2026-09.headline: Ather Energy Q2 FY27: wholesale volume up 42% YoY to 93,000 units, first positive PAT, and gross margin at 24% (H1 FY27: 23%).
544397|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong demand with preorders up about 108% and inquiries up about 109% YoY, supporting wholesale volume of 93,000 units (up 42% YoY) and registrations of about 92,500 (up nearly 60%). Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, and adjusted gross margin reached 24% in Q2 FY27 versus 25.4% in Q4 FY26 after commodity headwinds. EBITDA turned positive at 4.9% (from -9.6% a year earlier) and the company reported its first positive PAT. Management is raising installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units per year by Q2 FY28 because demand exceeds supply, and Konarc launched in phases from late August.

guidance_outlook: Installed capacity to rise from 9.2 lakh units/year to 11.4 lakh units/year by Q2 FY28, through Hosur (+6,000 units/month, live later this quarter) and AURIC Phase 1 (base 42,000 units/month, plus 12,000 units/month incremental).

demand_pricing: Preorders rose about 108% YoY to about 1.8 lakh; inquiries rose about 109% YoY to over 10 lakh; Ather searches rose about 94% vs about 34% for EV searches industry-wide.

Rodney Hunt USD target: USD75 million in five years, from about USD30 million today.
Q4 gross margin gain attributed to forex (billing at about INR92/USD against INR82 estimate); management says it lasts while the dollar stays high.
FY27 capex planned at about INR15-16 crore for the five Indian plants; US and Saudi capex not yet quantified.
Singapore sea-level projects: offers of about USD800-900 million submitted; first orders possibly from 2029, awards from 2028.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR67 crore: INR37 crore plant and machinery and INR30 crore acquisitions.

Saudi Arabia plant: company set up, land not yet acquired; site visit planned end-June/July 2026; commissioning target December 2027 (earlier December 2026).
Rodney Hunt Orange (Massachusetts) constrained by production staff shortage; new capacity chosen in Houston.
demand_pricing: US tariff: management says stability matters more than level; 25% to 50% increase mid-year led to under-estimated costs on January-June orders. Section 232 shift cited as continuing uncertainty.

Hong Kong Yuen Long Barrage project about INR40 crore (including small gates and valves); Chennai desalination project (VA Tech) over INR35 crore; Saudi Al Haer sewage treatment project in progress.
Middle East deliveries still blocked; order intake continues in Southeast Asia, Middle East, Far East and Europe.
Raw material prices rising: about 20% rise in India raw material cost per CFO; US steel also more expensive.

qa_highlights.question: Is domestic revenue flat in FY27 given INR327 crore FY26 base versus INR320 crore projected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the mix is balanced by choice; domestic margins are higher because low-margin domestic jobs are not taken. Domestic may rise if exports fall short.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 gross margin improvement only forex or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex-driven: orders quoted at INR82/USD and billed at about INR92 gain INR10 per dollar. Gross margin guided at 50-55% for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative given WestTech and carry-over?
qa_highlights.answer: Management calls it conservative given WestTech integration and the US tariff history; it expects growth of 13-17% and margin of at least 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt capacity and growth after Houston and Saudi plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Target USD75 million in five years; USD100 million not planned. Plant costs rose sharply, and US hiring constraints shaped the Houston decision.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is open to opportunities that are small and scalable; it is merging subsidiaries of similar businesses to reduce their number.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Singapore sea-level opportunity size INR5,000-6,000 crore and when does it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Clarified as offers of USD800-900 million, not an order; awards start 2028, first orders 2029, spread over 20-25 years; market share targeted 20-40%.

risks_watch: US tariff regime changes (Section 232 shift) and steel input cost inflation affecting project margins.
Middle East war delaying dispatches; Saudi plant land acquisition and commissioning timeline (December 2027) at risk.
Rodney Hunt Houston plant cost overrun (USD4.2 million to USD7-8.5 million) and hiring constraints in Orange, Massachusetts.
Other expenses inflated by one-off bank charge; overheads growing 7-10% against low revenue growth.
Forex-driven margin gain may reverse if the dollar falls; order book conversion and Q1 billing (INR36 crore overflow from March).
WestTech and Penstocks integration; margin outlook at WestTech not yet guided.

544402|2026-06.headline: Jash Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 17% YoY to Rs156 crore and PAT turned positive at about Rs5 crore; FY27 target Rs875 crore reiterated.
544402|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs156 crore, up about 17% YoY, with PAT moving from about minus Rs5 crore to plus Rs5 crore and gross and EBITDA margins both higher YoY. Management said shipments to Qatar, Singapore and other Middle East customers were held back (about Rs15 crore in total), so the quarter was below what management expected. Consolidated order book stands at Rs932 crore (India Rs293 crore, outside India Rs639 crore). Management reiterated FY27 revenue of Rs875 crore and PAT of about Rs100-105 crore, and said Rs1,500 crore revenue is targeted by 2031.

About 70% of US orders are to be made in America and 30% in India; management is cautious on new US order booking. A few large orders above $7 million each are under negotiation but not being pushed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was product-wise and region-wise breakup dropped from the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IR team concluded order mix changes too much quarter to quarter, so data will be shown year-on-year going forward; a Q1 split of Rs70 crore India and Rs80 crore outside India was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 margin gain is from tariff refund versus manufacturing benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination; the Rs5.6 crore tariff refund was booked in consumption. Dharmendra Jain also said the revenue reversal for deferred March recognition (Rs27-28 crore) was offset in June, leaving about Rs10 crore positive.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt margin profile and path to 10% PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 40% of revenue is from old orders and 60% from new orders; expected PAT margin is 8-9%; 10% may be reached by FY28 if things go well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Russia-sanctions/tariff risk and bidding in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bidding continues but aggressive order-chasing has slowed; it will review after the next US visit, and a US Senate bill was cited as a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Saudi and US plant timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi: approvals received, land application submitted, plant ready by December 2027 and operational by March 2028. US: land acquired, contractor to be finalised; both targeted in operation by March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs875 crore FY27 target expected to be exceeded and what is executable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book of Rs932 crore is not all executable this year because some orders are deferred to FY28; there is scope to exceed Rs875 crore but it is too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Jash Process Equipment (WesTech) underperform?

544403|2026-03.headline: ABLBL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 2,174 crores, with consolidated EBITDA up 14% to INR 375 crores and margin at 17.2%.
544403|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered double-digit revenue growth of 12% YoY, led by Lifestyle Brands (+11%) and Emerging Businesses (+18%), with retail like-to-like at 6%. Consolidated EBITDA rose 14% to INR 375 crores and margin expanded about 20 bps to 17.2%, helped by a one-time PLI benefit of about INR 20 crores in the quarter. Reported PAT was INR 55 crores after a one-time labour code exceptional item; normalized PAT was INR 60 crores (+58%). Management flagged softer wedding demand and moderating sentiment late in the quarter from geopolitical uncertainty and volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Others channel jump and PLI benefit: what drives it and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by contract manufacturing from the new Pulivendula factory plus institutional business. About INR 20 crores of PLI benefit landed in Q4 as a one-time item; management said Lifestyle margins expanded about 20 bps for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Van Heusen Innerwear: when does it turn profitable?

544403|2026-06.headline: ABLBL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore and EBITDA 14% to Rs 327 crore, with margin up 50 bps to 16%.
544403|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore, the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with EBITDA up 14% to Rs 327 crore and PAT up 21% to Rs 29 crore. Lifestyle Brands grew 10% to Rs 1,725 crore at an 18.5% EBITDA margin, while Emerging Brands grew 19% to Rs 332 crore at a 4.3% margin. Management attributed a modest demand moderation to adhik maas during the peak wedding period and a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2 that depressed wholesale growth to 5%. Gross margin contracted about 150 bps, which management attributed to channel mix and provisioning rather than raw material costs.

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 332 crore (+19% YoY), with retail LFL of 11% and e-commerce growth above 30%. Retail network crossed 400 stores; EBITDA margin 4.3%, up 240 bps.

segments.commentary: Retail grew 10% with 8% LFL, the seventh straight quarter of LFL growth. Wholesale grew 5% on primary billing, though underlying secondary growth was early double-digit.

guidance_outlook: Gross store additions of more than 300 in FY27, with net additions of 150-200 after closures of about 120-140 stores.
Cost inflation of 3-4% expected for Q2-Q3 FY27 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages; mostly to be offset by productivity and cost rationalisation, plus small price hikes.
Management expects Q1+Q2 wholesale primary billing to even out, with the Q1 shortfall moving into Q2.
Small-town retail (about 500 stores) is about 15-16% of retail revenue and is expected to exceed 20% of portfolio over the next three to four years.
Management aims for sustained double-digit growth and margin expansion; it expects retail to grow in early double digits.
Reebok revenue is about Rs 500 crore (from about Rs 250 crore at acquisition); management sees close to 20% long-term growth possible.
capex_capacity: Retail footprint of 3,362 stores (about 5 million sq ft) across more than 800 cities and towns at quarter end; more than 65 gross openings in Q1 (Aditya Bansal's question: 68 gross).
Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha; Karnataka concentration is limited.
Reebok has about 200 stores versus 500-700 for other premium brands, indicating a long retail runway.
Van Heusen Innerwear distribution is about 38,000-40,000 outlets; management expects roughly 20% network addition over the next couple of years.
Two Reebok factories still operate outside India pending BIS annual renewal; domestic sourcing is being built up.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand was broadly consistent with the prior-year trend; adhik maas caused modest moderation in the peak wedding period.
Wholesale grew 5%, with a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2; management says secondary was early double-digit.
Small-town stores grew over 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros; small-town growth has been double-digit for five consecutive quarters.
Price hikes were small and varied by brand and category, taken to offset input-cost increases; management says no meaningful apparel inflation is visible.
Marketing spend was about 3.5% of sales in Q1, down from last year because of IPL spend in the base quarter.
E-commerce profitability is said to be close to retail profitability, with growth now coming without deep discounting.
Quick commerce is small for the company; innerwear is the largest category there.
Casual wear share is rising by 2-3 percentage points a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why the divergence between primary and secondary sales in Lifestyle wholesale, and how will it evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: A 10-15 day festive timing shift moved primary billing into Q2; management expects Q1 and Q2 combined to be as strong as other channels.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation is expected and will prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 saw marginal to no cost pressure. Management expects 3-4% cost increase in Q2-Q3 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages, offset mainly by productivity and some price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 150 bps gross margin contraction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited channel mix and slightly higher inventory-age provisioning, not raw material costs, and said the effect is not material and will even out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to Karnataka minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Garmenting was never part of the notified hike, which is under High Court challenge. Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

qa_highlights.question: How are the net store adds and LFL growth reconciled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to more than 300 gross and 150-200 net additions in FY27 after 120-140 closures; network growth of 5-6% plus 7-8% LFL supports early double-digit retail growth.

qa_highlights.question: How do small-town and Tier 1 growth compare, and how is Gen-Z targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Tier 3-4 is growing above 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros. Gen-Z is served through sub-brands and collections (for example Peter England's Vybe), with no share figures disclosed.

risks_watch: Wholesale growth of 5% and gross margin contraction of about 150 bps in Q1; watch whether the festive shift reverses in Q2.
3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3 and the wage-regulation outcome in Karnataka at the High Court.
Consumer wallet pressure from inflation; management says it has seen no meaningful demand shift so far but is cautious about H2.
Reebok BIS certification risk on imports from factories outside India, renewed annually.
Net store additions of 150-200 against a gross plan above 300; watch LFL sustainability through closures.
key_quotes: So, when you look at Quarter 2, you will find the Quarter 1 plus Quarter 2 in as strong a place as rest of the channels.
We expect a major part of it comes through productivity and the rest through cost rationalization.
But we are cautious that this may play out in the second half of the year.
Over the years, we have managed to bring this channel profitability very close to our retail profitability.

rows.why: Two Reebok factories outside India still operate pending BIS annual renewal, and Reebok revenue of about Rs 500 crore relies on imports while domestic sourcing is being built up.

544405|2026-03.headline: Belrise Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn with EBITDA margin at 11.4%; FY26 adjusted PAT up 41% to INR5,020 mn.
544405|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total revenue grew 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn and manufacturing revenue grew 21% to INR21,763 mn, while EBITDA rose only 5% to INR2,901 mn, with margin at 11.4%. Adjusted PAT rose 17% to INR1,290 mn, with a one-time INR94.7 mn operational loss at the aerospace and defence subsidiary absorbed in the quarter. For FY26, total revenue grew 15% to INR95,091 mn and adjusted PAT grew 41% to INR5,020 mn. Management reported new two-wheeler and exhaust/fuel-tank orders, the Chester Hall acquisition in the UK, and guidance of mid-teens growth with broadly stable margins for FY27.

segments.name: Two-wheeler and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed 83.2% of Q4 manufacturing revenue and 82.0% in FY26. Content per vehicle rose 65-70% during FY26 (management also cited 60-65% on another basis), with two-wheeler content per vehicle moving from about INR12,000 to INR20,000 including the Badve Auto Comps and Eximius merger.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.2% of Q4 and 5.2% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. Suspension business currently serves two- and three-wheeler OEMs only, not PV OEMs.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.4% of Q4 and 8.3% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. CV segment grew 32% in Q4 and 35% in FY26.

segments.name: Four-wheeler
segments.commentary: Four-wheeler business grew 71% in Q4 and 37% in FY26 (transcript initially said 31%, corrected to 37% in footnote). Content per vehicle rose from about INR25,000 to INR40,000-45,000 with the H-One acquisition.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence (Belrise Aerospace and Defense)
segments.commentary: Acquired SDM (France) in Q3 FY26 and Chester Hall (UK) in Q4 FY26. Q4 carried a one-time operational loss of INR94.7 mn from startup costs, legal and professional fees and personnel costs; management expects SDM to be EBITDA positive in 2027.

guidance_outlook: Mid-teens revenue growth expected to continue, supported by the order book.
EBITDA margins expected to remain broadly stable versus FY26 levels (FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 12.1%); cost pressures seen as short-term and not expected to affect medium-to-long-term margins.
Capex expected at 6% to 6.5% of manufacturing revenue, with R&D included within this range.
Doubling four-wheeler and CV revenue versus FY25 within the current fiscal year requires about 40% to 45% growth, per management endeavour.
Final dividend of INR0.55 per share declared.
SDM expected to turn EBITDA positive in 2027 after the one-time Q4 loss.
capex_capacity: Bangalore brownfield expansion to supply exhaust systems and fuel tanks to a fast-growing two- and three-wheeler OEM; production slated to begin Q2 FY27 with peak annual revenue of INR90 crore.
Large order from a Japanese two-wheeler OEM for exhaust systems and metal components; peak annual revenue about INR220 crore, production starting Q4 FY26-27 (transcript says 'this fiscal year').
Haridwar plant ramp-up: trial parts dispatched to a large two-wheeler OEM; peak production targeted within FY27, sourcing from Greater Noida and Pantnagar.
Chassis, battery trays and metal components for an emerging EV player; supplies expected to start Q3 of the fiscal year.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation or break-even timelines for new plants (Chennai, Pune, Bhiwandi).
Over 850 robots deployed across the company; medium-term vision is a large integrated aerospace and defence facility in India.
demand_pricing: Sector saw strong Q4 growth, helped by the GST rate cut late last year; management hopes for structural rather than pull-forward demand.
Back-to-back raw material pricing model passes steel and plastic cost changes to customers with a lag, limiting margin impact.

Q4 headwinds: oil-crisis-related supply chain disruption, higher raw material, energy and logistics costs, and Haryana minimum wage increase. Fuel and labour costs expected to be passed on over time; transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs.
Two-wheeler segment only recently returned to pre-COVID peak; management sees long-term headroom.
Aerospace demand described as very strong, with OEM order backlogs of 8-10+ years; qualification cycles of 12-24 months cited as the main barrier.
Chester Hall: rejection rate 0.5%-1%; advanced discussions to transfer part of its subcontracted work to India.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend through the quarters, and how will the company absorb commodity, fuel and labour cost pressures to hold full-year margins stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 was hit by the INR94.7 mn one-time aerospace loss and acquisition fees, both called one-time. Fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time; transport costs still under discussion. Full-year guidance maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the two new two-wheeler OEM customers become over two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both to become very large over 2-3 years, with content per vehicle rising sharply and cross-model penetration. The Japanese OEM order is about INR200 crore annually, and the Bangalore program is one of the sharpest ramp-ups in three years.

qa_highlights.question: How much can aerospace contribute in four to five years, and can manufacturing move to India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets aerospace above 10% of revenue and sees India as a best-cost base. It is in talks with OEMs to shift Chester Hall subcontracted work and new orders from Europe to India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QIP of INR2,000 crore for?
qa_highlights.answer: Only an enabling resolution has been approved; no specific use was given, and management will update when there is progress.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive edge in exhaust systems, and what margin is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Edge comes from automation (850+ robots), high verticalisation, NVH engineering and stainless-steel plating capability. Management corrected the INR400 crore figure: the orders are INR220 crore and INR90 crore, about INR310 crore peak combined. No margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will R&D spend scale with aerospace and steering/high-tensile products?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is included within the 6%-6.5% capex range. The R&D team has more than 163 people. Management directionally agreed on hiring and partnerships but gave no specific target.

qa_highlights.question: Will the trading business be localised, spun off or hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not commented on hiving off the trading business and will update later.

qa_highlights.question: Does suspension have passenger vehicle customers, and what are suspension and H-One revenue and PAT figures?
qa_highlights.answer: No PV customers yet; the suspension business serves only two- and three-wheeler OEMs, with four marquee customers, three onboarded in the last 18 months. Management did not have suspension, polymer or H-One revenue and PAT figures and will follow up offline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inorganic strategy for FY27, and what are the content per vehicle and plant utilisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are chosen on customers, capabilities and verticalisation at mild valuations (book value to mid-single-digit EV/EBITDA); all four acquisitions are EPS and ROCE accretive. Content per vehicle has risen 60-65% in two-wheelers and is 40-45% in four-wheelers and CVs. Plant utilisation and break-even were not disclosed.

risks_watch: Margin trajectory: management guides FY26-level EBITDA margins (12.1%) but Q4 EBITDA margin was 11.4%; watch whether the one-time INR94.7 mn aerospace loss and acquisition fees recur or fade in Q1 FY27.
Oil-crisis cost pass-through: fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time, transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs; a lag in recovery could compress margins.

Execution of new programmes: Bangalore brownfield (production from Q2 FY27), Japanese OEM exhaust/metal order (production from Q4 FY26-27), Haridwar ramp to peak within FY27, and EV-player chassis supplies from Q3; monitor ramp timing.
Aerospace: SDM expected EBITDA positive in 2027; Chester Hall transfer of subcontracted work to India is in advanced talks but not yet signed; qualification cycles of 12-24 months.

Capital and disclosure gaps: QIP of INR2,000 mn-equivalent (INR2,000 crore) approved only as an enabling resolution with no use specified; plant-level utilisation and break-even not disclosed; suspension, polymer and H-One standalone revenue and PAT to follow offline; trading business hive-off undecided.
key_quotes: Our first commitment was to deliver mid -teens revenue growth while keeping our EBITDA margins stable. And I am glad to share that we achieved this.
We expect this loss to be one -time and expect SDM to be EBITDA positive in the year 2027.
At this point of time, it's only an enabling resolution.
We are unable to comment on plant-specific questions on utilization and break-even.
544405|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the headline commitments (mid-teens growth, stable margins, 4W/CV doubling, content-per-vehicle gains), with management repeatedly calling Q4 hits one-time. Evasive on specifics: declined plant utilisation and break-even, QIP use, trading business hive-off, H-One and suspension figures, and R&D hiring targets, deferring these to later updates.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin broadly stable vs FY26's 12.1%, but Q4 printed 11.4% after the INR94.7 mn one-time aerospace loss, and fuel/labour costs pass through only with a lag, so expansion is not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bangalore brownfield (peak INR90 crore revenue) starts Q2 FY27, EV-player chassis supplies start Q3 FY27, and Haridwar peak production is targeted within FY27; plant-level utilisation was not disclosed, so the size of the uplift is unverified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides mid-teens revenue growth (FY26 manufacturing revenue +17%, Q4 +21%), backed by the order book and new two-wheeler programmes (Japanese OEM ~INR220 crore peak, Bangalore INR90 crore).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex guided at 6-6.5% of manufacturing revenue (about INR5,000-5,000 crore-equivalent on FY26 base is not stated, so no number is given), and the INR2,000 crore QIP was approved only as an enabling resolution with no use specified, so a new project announcement is conditional on use of proceeds.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only held (mid-teens growth, stable margins, capex 6-6.5%), and management gave no sign of raising it, with Q4 margin at 11.4% below the 12.1% FY26 level.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA rose only 5% against revenue +12%, margin fell to 11.4%, and oil-crisis supply, energy and logistics costs plus the Haryana minimum wage increase are not yet recovered from OEMs, with transport recovery still under discussion.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New two-wheeler exhaust/fuel-tank programmes start production: Bangalore in Q2 FY27, Japanese OEM order from Q4 FY26-27, and EV-player chassis, battery trays and metal components from Q3.

rows.label: Two new two-wheeler OEM customers scale over 2-3 years
rows.why: Management expects both new two-wheeler OEMs to become very large, with the Japanese order about INR200 crore annually and content per vehicle rising sharply (two-wheeler CPV about INR12,000 to INR20,000).

rows.label: Aerospace above 10% of revenue and India as best-cost base
rows.why: Management targets aerospace above 10% of revenue and is in talks to move Chester Hall subcontracted work to India, but the transfer is not signed and qualification cycles run 12-24 months.

rows.label: SDM turns EBITDA positive
rows.why: Management expects SDM (France, acquired Q3 FY26) to be EBITDA positive in 2027 after the one-time INR94.7 mn Q4 loss, but no quarterly figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on mid-teens growth, stable margins, the 4W/CV doubling and content-per-vehicle gains, and called Q4 hits one-time; it was evasive on plant utilisation, break-even, QIP use, trading hive-off and H-One/suspension figures, which analysts pushed on.

544405|2026-06.headline: Belrise Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR25,465 million, EBITDA margin 11.5%, PAT up 9% to INR1,217 million.
544405|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY, led by manufacturing revenue up 20% to INR21,979 million, while trading revenue fell about 19% on Middle East disruption. EBITDA rose 5% to INR2,933 million, with margin down to 11.5%, and manufacturing EBITDA margin at 12.7%. Management reported a INR17,000 million QIP and the Hyva India tipper acquisition (completion expected Q3 FY27), and a run of new order wins across two-wheeler, renewable energy, and commercial vehicles. Management said cost pressures from steel, polymer, staff and energy have peaked and FY27 EBITDA margins should stay broadly stable versus FY26.

segments.name: Two- and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed about 81.4% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; management said segment revenue grew about 18% YoY, below industry growth of roughly 20-25%, attributed to customer mix.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 4.6% of manufacturing revenue in Q1 FY27; H-One high-tensile steel capability up to 1470 MPa cited as a differentiator.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.5% of manufacturing revenue; four-wheeler and CV revenue grew about 18% YoY per management opening remarks; Hyva India tipper acquisition announced 4 August 2026.

segments.name: Others (incl. aerospace, defence, renewables, trading)
segments.commentary: About 5.5% of manufacturing revenue. Trading business fell about 19% YoY due to Middle East crisis and logistics; management expects mid-teens group revenue growth. Aerospace and defence target is at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margins broadly stable versus FY26, with no material margin impact from input costs given back-to-back pricing.
Group revenue growth guided at mid-teens with stable EBITDA margins.
Majority of INR17,000 million QIP proceeds to be deployed within FY27, mainly for inorganic opportunities in aerospace and four-wheeler/CV, plus some organic growth.
Hyva India tipper business acquisition expected to complete in Q3 FY27; deal to be EPS and ROCE accretive from day one per management's stated threshold.
Aerospace and defence to reach at least 10% of consolidated revenue in the medium term.

New programs (chassis for fast-growing 2W OEM, US solar tracker assemblies, Sambhajinagar 2W chassis, brake assemblies) to start production in Q4 FY27; margin pressure expected to ease in coming quarters as pass-through takes effect.
capex_capacity: Four new facilities coming up, including brownfield facilities; fixed costs ramping ahead of revenue, per management.
Bangalore brownfield facility to host new 2W chassis program (annual revenue above INR650 million), SOP expected Q4 FY27.
US solar tracker sheet-metal assembly setup to support about 2.5 GW annual supplies; peak annual revenue above INR1,500 million; production from Q4 FY27.
Expansion at existing Maharashtra facilities to support a 59-assembly EV localisation program for a large Indian CV OEM.
Hyva acquisition includes three manufacturing facilities in Pune, Jamshedpur and Bangalore.
Management declined to disclose utilisation or ramp-up details for specific facilities such as Bangalore and Haridwar.
demand_pricing: Order wins: 2W/3W chassis for fast-growing OEM (above INR650 million annual revenue, on top of about INR900 million fuel tank and exhaust win last quarter); cumulative about INR1,550 million with that OEM, about INR2,000 million including suspension and braking wins.
Suspension systems now supplied to five 2W/3W OEMs, including a new Vietnamese 2W entrant in India, with suspension and braking.
Two-wheeler chassis order for an existing model at a large 2W OEM's Sambhajinagar plant, potential annual revenue of about INR500 million.
Management attributed slower 2W/3W growth to a customer mix gap with faster-growing OEMs, with new OEM ramps expected in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Trading business decline was due to Middle East crisis hitting African, Asian and Middle Eastern demand and logistics; management says the worst is behind it.
Input cost pressure (steel, polymer, energy, logistics, minimum wage hike) persisted in Q1; management expects pass-through in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new chassis order additional to earlier two-wheeler wins from South India?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it is over and above the exhaust and fuel tank win from last quarter (about INR900 million), making about INR1,550 million cumulative annual run-rate with that one OEM.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure remains from commodities, staff costs and energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity, staff and energy/transport cost pressures have largely peaked, with staff cost rise tied to the annual increment cycle and pre-hiring for four new facilities; pass-through expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Can management quantify the benefit from raw-material pass-through and the trading decline's margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify either on the call and offered to respond offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did 2W/3W growth (about 18%) lag industry growth (about 20-25%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a customer mix issue, as some faster-growing OEMs it does not work with closely gained share; newly penetrated OEMs should add volumes in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aerospace and defence revenue outlook and the Plasan Sasa defence opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least 10% of manufacturing revenue from aerospace and defence in the short-to-medium term; Belrise already exports parts to Plasan Sasa in Israel, with progress described as gradual given geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: Can H-One and Mag Filters revenue be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said it manages the business as one group and will not disclose segment-level numbers for H-One or Mag Filters.

risks_watch: Margin recovery hinges on pass-through of steel, polymer and energy costs to OEMs in Q2-Q3 FY27; management did not quantify the benefit or the trading-decline effect on margin

rows.why: Trading revenue fell ~19% YoY in Q1 on Middle East and logistics disruption; management says the worst is behind it but gave no numbers or guidance for the segment.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost peaking, order momentum and the mid-teens growth guide, but evasive on quantifying pass-through, trading margin drag, facility utilisation and H-One/Mag Filters numbers; analysts pushed on the 2W/3W growth gap and margin recovery.

544407|2026-03.headline: Aegis Vopak FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR923.1 crores and net profit 52.1% to INR341.9 crores; Q4 revenue up 22.2% to INR243.5 crores.
544407|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the company's first full year as a listed entity, with revenue from operations up 17% YoY to INR923.1 crores and operating EBITDA up 19.4% to INR686.5 crores. Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22.2% YoY to INR243.5 crores, with Q4 operating EBITDA up 24.2% to INR179.2 crores and net profit up 15.3% to INR73.9 crores. Management said FY25 and FY26 figures were restated to consolidate Hindustan Aegis LPG Limited, which was acquired as a 75% stake in Haldia. Management reiterated a 30-40% YoY throughput growth target for FY27 and a long-term capex roadmap of about USD5 billion by 2030.

financial_highlights.value: INR0.2 per share (about 2.0% on INR10 face value)

segments.name: Liquid terminaling
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR440.5 crores (+27.8% YoY); Q4 INR121.1 crores (+31% YoY) on volumes, capacity additions and product mix. Management cites about INR3,000 per CBM as a good blended earning.

segments.name: Gas terminaling (LPG)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR482.6 crores (+8.6% YoY); Q4 INR122.4 crores (+14.6% YoY). Gas throughput rose to 3.9 million tons in FY26 from 3.3 million tons in FY25.

segments.name: Ammonia (emerging)
segments.commentary: Pipavav ammonia terminal of 36,000 metric tons static capacity, backed by a 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc; commissioning expected next month per management. Not yet a reported revenue line.

guidance_outlook: FY27 throughput growth of 30-40% YoY, which management says is its standing target (not formal guidance).
FY27 capex of USD1.2 billion, cumulative aggregate capex reaching about USD1.2 billion by end of next year.
FY28 capex expected to be close to INR5,000 crores; numbers to be finalised.
JNPT liquid expansion (318,100 CBM) mostly operational in H1 FY27, with full completion targeted by around October; contributes from Q2 FY27.
Long-term capex pipeline of about USD5 billion by 2030, with a gearing target of about 0.6x and a planned second-phase QIP (equity).
capex_capacity: JNPT: liquid storage of 106,900 CBM today; expansion adds about 318,100 CBM liquid, 77,236 MT LPG and a 35,000 MT LPG bottling plant, total capex about INR1,675 crores; phase 1 targeted for Q1 FY27.

Kandla: about 952,000 CBM liquid and 48,000 MT LPG; CRL4 liquid terminal adds 94,148 CBM, on track for commissioning next year (FY27). Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline connection expected in H1 FY27. VLGC-compliant after first VLGC received in December 2025.

Pipavav: cryogenic LPG terminal of 48,000 MT commissioned June 2025 (total LPG 70,800 MT); new VLGC-compliant jetty expected to complete within calendar 2026; 15-year take-or-pay for 0.5 million MT per year of petroleum products with operations expected by year-end; ammonia terminal of 36,000 MT.

Mangalore: cryogenic LPG terminal of 82,000 MT commissioned June 2025; 75,000 CBM liquid added and operational, total liquid 193,000 CBM; LPG rail gantry under construction; land secured for a further 60,000 CBM.

Haldia: 226,890 CBM liquid storage; about 25,000 MT LPG added via 75% stake in Hindustan Aegis LPG under a HPCL exclusive terminaling agreement through 2038; 3 acres of land acquired for expansion. Kochi: about 82,545 CBM, with up to 60,000 CBM planned on newly allotted land.
demand_pricing: Management says the company operates as an open-access terminal and does not track revenue split between long-term and spot contracts; long-term contracts exist but are not the norm. Operates close to 25 units across India.

LPG imports were hit after Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption from March; volumes were down about 50% in March, improving to a 30-35% shortfall in May. Parent's distribution volumes grew strongly in Q4, supporting terminal utilisation.
Management expects the JNPT expansion to earn full realisations from commissioning, as JNPT has more demand, rather than ramping up gradually.
Liquid terminals are paid on capacity hired, so management measures earnings per CBM rather than physical occupancy.
Business mix expected to shift toward gas, at about 55:45 or 60:40 gas to liquid over the next three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity being built by Aegis Vopak directly or by Aegis Logistics?
qa_highlights.answer: Land is leased to Aegis Vopak, but the parent Aegis Logistics builds the infrastructure under its supervision, for cost and in-house capability reasons; Aegis Vopak then owns and operates the terminals.

qa_highlights.question: What supports a USD5 billion capex plan when only USD1.2 billion has been spent so far?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex grew from USD200 million to USD600 million to USD1.2 billion, and is now running at INR4,000-5,000 crores a year, rising later. Spending follows demand, with larger projects in the last two years of the period, funded by EBITDA growth and a second-phase QIP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix by customer and contract term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not track these statistics; it runs as an open-access terminal with no product or customer dependence, and long-term contracts exist but are not the norm.

qa_highlights.question: Lease expiries and business mix over the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Most leases are not near expiry; the only near-term one is Pipavav's concessionaire lease in 2029. Gas is expected to be more dominant, at about 55:45 or 60:40 gas to liquid.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 guidance and FY27/FY28 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance, but throughput growth of 30-40% YoY is the usual target. FY27 capex is USD1.2 billion and FY28 is about INR5,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: JNPT expansion timing and realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning starts around next month, with most capacity running by H1 and completion around October; realisations are expected to be strong from the start.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kandla-Gorakhpur, Mangalore-Hassan and Uran-Chakan pipeline timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Kandla-Gorakhpur connects in H1 FY27; Uran-Chakan is about a million tons; Mangalore-Hassan-Cherlapalli is expected in FY28, with the Mangalore LPG rail gantry earlier.

risks_watch: Capex execution at scale: USD5 billion by 2030, with 12 ports targeted from seven, and funding that relies on a second-phase QIP and debt at about 0.6x gearing.
LPG import disruption from the Strait of Hormuz conflict; management expects normalisation from Q2 FY27.
Timing of JNPT Phase 1 (Q1 FY27), CRL4 at Kandla (FY27), Pipavav VLGC jetty and ammonia terminal commissioning, and the Pipavav petroleum product operations by year-end.

Ammonia business is early-stage; Pipavav ammonia terminal is about one-third contracted to Hindustan Zinc, with ITOCHU holding 10% of the ammonia subsidiary and planning to raise it to 25% over three years.
Vadhvan port project (about INR20,000 crores outlay) is only a non-binding MoU, subject to approvals and land allocation.
544407|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and capex, with a clear long-term plan. Management was more hedged on specifics: no formal guidance, FY28 capex still to be finalised, and several timelines (Kochi, Mangalore, Vadhvan, Bangalore-Hassan-Cherlapalli) left open.
key_quotes: We always follow demand, we are not somebody who will do flag planting and do anything prematurely.
Now we are doing it at a pace of, let's say, INR4,000 crores or INR5,000 crores a year.
So, being vertically integrated in LPG business helps Aegis Vopak as well as Aegis Logistics and the Group as a whole to get over this situation.

544407|2026-06.headline: Aegis Vopak Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, with liquid terminaling up 31% and operating EBITDA up 15.6% to INR179.4 crore.
544407|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, led by liquid terminaling (INR126.5 crore, +31% YoY) while gas terminaling fell 3.5% YoY to INR107.2 crore. Operating EBITDA rose 15.6% YoY to INR179.4 crore (about 76.7% margin) and cash PAT was INR124.9 crore. Management said the board approved a 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA and 49,577 cbm of liquid capacity at Kochi, and that the Pipavav ammonia terminal (36,000 MT static) was commissioned. Management framed a $5 billion capex plan through FY2030-31, of which about INR10,000 crore is to be commissioned by March/June 2027.

segments.name: Liquid terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR126.5 crore, up 31% YoY, driven by higher volumes, new capacity and product mix; management cited JNPA plot 1 maturing (about INR6,000 realization per unit vs blended INR3,000) and better-located capacity commissioned last year.

segments.name: Gas terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR107.2 crore, down 3.5% YoY on LPG import disruption from the Middle East; management said volumes held up via diversified sourcing and multi-location distribution. Standard throughput rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow volumes at least 25% YoY every year; management said AVTL delivered 3.9 million MT in the last year and expects more than 25% growth.
Liquid capacity to rise from about 1.7 million cbm to about 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end.
About INR10,000 crore of expansion (JNPA, ammonia, liquid) expected to be commissioned by March 2027 or June 2027 at the latest.
Kochi 49,577 cbm expected by early next financial year; CRL4 at Kandla (about 94,148 cbm) targeted for later next year.

Funding: debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x; about $3 billion of the $5 billion capex to come from debt, with about $2 billion equity net worth target and mandatory dilution to 25% of equity by 2 June 2028.
capex_capacity: JNPA expansion: 318,100 cbm liquid storage, 77,236 MT LPG capacity and a 35,000 MT LPG bottling plant, total outlay INR1,675 crore; first phase of about 100,000 cbm expected in Q3 FY27.
JNPA: board approved a 52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank; existing liquid capacity about 101,900 cbm.
Kochi: board sanctioned 49,577 cbm; total liquid capacity to reach 132,122 cbm from 82,545 cbm.

Pipavav: 36,000 MT ammonia storage commissioned; 0.5 million MT/yr 15-year take-or-pay petroleum product agreement to start by year-end via additional liquid rail gantry; VLGC-compliant jetty by APM Terminals expected this year; Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline connection expected in the first half of FY27 (per Q&A, 2-3 months).

Mangalore: 75,000 cbm added last year, total 193,000 cbm; evaluating 60,000 cbm more; LPG rail gantry and bottling investment INR52.5 crore. Haldia: 226,890 cbm liquid storage plus 3 acres of land acquired; Haldia-Panagarh pipeline (HPCL, 60 km) expected October-November 2026.
demand_pricing: LPG throughput is priced per metric ton, not per storage day, and management said there is no escalation; the focus is on volume growth.
Liquid terminaling is charged per cbm capacity, not occupancy, so revenue is not driven by utilization.

Management attributed gas volume resilience to diversified sourcing (ITOCHU partnership, non-Middle East cargoes) and ullage availability; it said domestic LPG shortfall had recovered to about 80-85% of normal by July.
Ammonia realizations described as 2.5-3x LPG realizations; first-year utilization projected at 20-25% of the 36,000 MT static capacity (prorated for an August start).
Pipavav: 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc for part of ammonia capacity for its DAP plant.

qa_highlights.question: Are LPG throughput charges fixed by counterparty and term, and why haven't terminal charges risen while distribution margins did?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals; charges are per MT with no escalation. Management said terminaling is infrastructure usage, while distribution margins reflect sourcing and inventory risk during the geopolitical disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AVTL gain share versus national LPG imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited non-Middle East sourcing (none of its ships were stuck), a partner in ITOCHU, and wider distribution using freed-up ullage across more locations than Mumbai and Kandla.

qa_highlights.question: Is 25% volume growth sustainable, and what is the Haldia pipeline impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for at least 25% YoY growth; four pipelines are due this year (Jamnagar-Loni done; Kandla-Gorakhpur at Kandla and Pipavav in 2-3 months; Haldia-Panagarh in 2-3 months). Haldia-Panagarh is HPCL's 60 km line; the Panagarh bottling plant is 0.5 million MT/yr and currently about 0.25 million MT is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and liquid capacity path to FY28, and what is the Pipavav take-or-pay economics?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10,000 crore to be commissioned by March/June 2027; liquid capacity 1.7 to 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end. The Pipavav 0.5 million MT is higher utilization of existing capacity via rail gantry, not new tankage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth plans beyond the INR10,000 crore phase and the $5 billion program?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing organic and inorganic options, inland depots, strategic storage and industrial terminals, and said binding agreements will be announced as signed. The $5 billion plan through FY2030-31 is reaffirmed, with timing expected to be lumpy.

qa_highlights.question: Why did liquid revenue jump when capacity did not change?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity added last year was only partly in the base year and has now matured, JNPA plot 1 is fully running, and product mix has changed, which takes time.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a mix of debt and equity, with debt gearing capped at 0.6x and debt/EBITDA at 3.5x, about $3 billion of debt, a $2 billion equity net worth target, and mandatory dilution to 25% by 2 June 2028.

Gas segment EBIT pressure: gas revenue fell 3.5% YoY and management did not give gas EBITDA when asked; ammonia first-year utilization of 20-25% is a projection, not a result
key_quotes: So, as you can see, across our businesses, we continue to see multiple growth drivers taking shape.
We like to at least grow in our volumes 25% year-on-year every year. That's our hope.
Occupancy is not what liquid works on. So the rate is on CBM basis.
But these all you cannot time it. It happens, then you just get on with it.
It may be lumpy, it may be simultaneous, time will tell.

Cautious on the gas side, attributing the decline to geopolitics while saying volumes held up.

544408|2026-03.headline: Leela Palaces Q4 FY26: operating revenue up 12% to INR 484 crores and EBITDA up 13% to INR 266 crores, with ADR up 15% offsetting a March occupancy hit.
544408|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 484 crores and operating EBITDA rose 13% to INR 266 crores, at a 55% margin, while PAT increased to INR 172 crores from INR 117 crores. Growth was driven by ADR, which rose about 15% to around INR 32,000, while RevPAR grew only 6% as occupancy fell from 78% to 72% after the West Asia conflict disrupted international travel in March. For FY26, operating revenue grew 15% to INR 1,527 crores, EBITDA grew 19% to INR 743 crores at a 49% margin, and PAT reached a record INR 403 crores. Management said April occupancy had recovered to last year's level, with high single-digit to early double-digit RevPAR growth expected for April.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 117 crores in Q4 FY25

segments.name: City hotels
segments.commentary: Occupancy fell in March on the international, US and UK source-market disruption; management expects city occupancy in mid-70s in FY27. Non-resident covers at city hotels were 54% of the cover mix.

segments.name: Resorts
segments.commentary: Described as insulated from the war; management expects a strong rebound in May and June. Resort occupancy guided to mid-60s to late-60s for FY27.

segments.name: F&B
segments.commentary: F&B revenue grew 15% in FY26 and close to double digits in Q4; banqueting grew more than 10%. Non-resident covers rose about 9-10% in Q4 and about 12% for FY26.

segments.name: Managed hotels / HMA fees
segments.commentary: HMA fees grew double digits in Q4, helped by Hyderabad ramp-up to about 62% occupancy and ADR about 1.24x peer set, plus additional HMA fees from contract terms. FY27 management fees guided to grow double digits.

segments.name: ARQ by The Leela
segments.commentary: Invite-only ultra-luxury club; first club in Bengaluru in FY26, with New Delhi in Q1 FY27, Chennai in Q2 FY27 and Mumbai later in FY27. Initiation fee is INR 45 lakh plus GST; stabilised target is 2,000 members.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 RevPAR growth of high single digit to early double digit in April, and May and June to be very strong; Q1 revenue and EBITDA guided to grow double digit.
FY27 occupancy: city hotels mid-70s, resorts mid-60s to late-60s, blended early 70s.
Net debt to EBITDA to stay around 1.6x in FY27, then fall toward 1.4x and near 1x as new assets ramp; acquisitions could push it slightly higher.
Depreciation to stay around INR 100 crores for the next two to three years, rising only when new hotels open.

Coorg (The Leela Forest Sanctuary): first-year revenue of INR 65-70 crores at about 40% occupancy, with stabilised EBITDA margin of 50-55%; stabilised revenue of INR 165-175 crores in year four including 19 additional villas (capex about INR 38 crores). Rebrand expected end-Q1 or early Q2 FY27.

Jaisalmer and The Leela Luxury Residences Mumbai to open in FY27. Ayodhya, Agra and Ranthambore now slated for CY28 (previously FY28), with approvals and funding in place and capex unchanged; Dubai refurbishment to start by end of CY26, handover 1 January 2027 and rebrand 1 January 2028.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio is over 5,200 luxury keys across 24 properties: 15 operational hotels and nine in the pipeline. FY26 keys grew 23% with 966 keys added across Mumbai BKC, Dubai, Jaisalmer and Coorg.
Coorg acquired on 18 March 2026: 71-key all-villa resort on 76 acres, with 25 rooms having heated pools; only about 20 of the 76 acres used so far.
Greenfield projects under construction: Bandhavgarh, Srinagar, Sikkim, Agra, Ayodhya and Ranthambore (design, demolition, excavation, piling and structural work underway).
Asset enhancement initiatives (F&B refurbishments, retail, spa, kids club, villa conversions) targeted at about 25% projected yield on cost.
Solar capacity of 2.25 MW commissioned at The Leela Palace Chennai; green energy now 67% of consumption, and power and fuel cost fell to 3% of operating revenue from 3.3% in FY25.
demand_pricing: West Asia conflict cut international inbound and outbound travel in March; the international business is roughly 50:50 with domestic in FY26 and has shifted to about 40:60 international to domestic in Q4.
Domestic demand was unaffected; management said April occupancy recovered to last year's levels.
MICE cancellations in March were given credit notes and deferred over six to nine months; management expects a high share to return in coming quarters.
Three weddings originally planned in the Middle East were moved to Leela hotels in March, with more enquiries for April and May.
Expedia and Agoda moved to charging on a gross basis rather than net, which raised sales and marketing and commission costs.
Dubai: asset is 25% owned, with Brookfield holding 75%; management said there is no change in plans and it is focused on operational break-even.

qa_highlights.question: Were March trends sharply weaker and what are April and May trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy fell on US and UK source markets while ADR held; April occupancy returned to last year's level, with high single-digit to early double-digit RevPAR growth expected, and May and June strong.

qa_highlights.question: Were there MICE cancellations, and are they deferred or lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Cancellations occurred in March; they were converted to credit notes and deferred over six to nine months, with a high share expected back in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Did Ayodhya, Agra and Ranthambore slip, and has capex changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Timing moved from FY28 to CY28 because of approval-linked construction risk; approvals and funding are in place, and capex is unchanged with no cost escalation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Dubai write-off risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see a write-off possibility, that the asset was underwritten on conservative real estate pricing, and that it is evaluating daily.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other costs rise as a percentage of revenue in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise mainly to a one-time accrual for new labour code leave encashment and gratuity, plus hiring of value-driver staff; excluding this, payroll rose 8-8.5%, and management expects the ratio to decline.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt to EBITDA trend in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 1.6x in FY27, falling toward 1.4x and then near 1x as new assets generate EBITDA; acquisitions could push it higher temporarily.

risks_watch: Recovery of international inbound demand from US and UK source markets, which is the segment hit by the West Asia conflict.
Q1 FY27 delivery against the guided high single-digit to early double-digit April RevPAR growth and double-digit May-June performance.
Dubai: a possible impairment if the market stays weak, plus the refurbishment and handover timeline (1 January 2027 handover; 1 January 2028 rebrand).
Q4 cost ratios (employee cost 16.6% of revenue vs 15.9%; other costs up 70 bps), with management expecting them to fall; management did not give exact room, F&B and HMA revenue figures for Q4.
Coorg ramp-up and rebranding, plus ARQ club openings in New Delhi, Chennai and Mumbai.
Depreciation guided flat at about INR 100 crores until new hotels open.
544408|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on domestic demand, pricing power and the medium-term outlook, while candid that March international occupancy was hit. Management was less specific on Q4 line-item detail (room, F&B and HMA revenue) and on city-level data, deferring those to follow-up calls.
key_quotes: Our domestic business has not been impacted at all, and whilst some part of our international business has been impacted from a key source market.
The only sub -segment of demand that got impacted because of the war was our international business from our key source markets.

We are looking at an overall stabilized number of 2,000 members, because at that number we feel is the right fit where we can serve them, take care of them, and give them that kind of a luxury experience they have paid for.

544408|2026-06.headline: Leela Palaces Q1 FY27: operating revenue up 28% to INR3,520 mn and operating EBITDA up 41% to INR1,434 mn, margin 41%.
544408|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was driven by domestic demand, which offset a weak international start to the quarter caused by West Asia travel disruption. Six owned hotels (including Coorg) posted occupancy of 67.5% (vs 63.6%), RevPAR up 17% and ADR up 10%, with same-store RevPAR up 15%. Operating EBITDA margin expanded 383 bps to 41%, and consolidated PAT rose five-fold to INR488 mn despite a INR156 mn share-of-loss from the Dubai JV. Management reiterated double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: ~5x YoY; after INR156 mn share of JV loss (Dubai)

financial_highlights.value: 1.6x (gross debt ~INR1,600 crore, net debt INR1,332 crore)

segments.name: City hotels
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 14% YoY. Bengaluru and Chennai are GDS and corporate heavy; Delhi and Jaipur called out as strong performers.

segments.name: Resorts
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 24% YoY, with high double-digit occupancy and ADR growth at the two Rajasthan resorts; Coorg acquired and rebranded as The Leela Coorg Forest Sanctuary on 8 July, reached EBITDA break-even in the quarter.

segments.name: Dubai JV (25% stake, Brookfield sponsor)
segments.commentary: Operationally break-even but recorded an accounting loss at SPV level (interest and depreciation), flowing through as INR156 mn share of JV loss. Leela takes over operations in CY27, followed by about a year of renovation.

segments.name: HMA / managed portfolio
segments.commentary: HMA fees INR262 mn (+86%); other operational service revenue +26%. Management said fees are partly performance-linked and key-money-linked, so quarterly growth may vary.

guidance_outlook: FY27: reiterated double-digit RevPAR growth and mid-to-high teens operating EBITDA growth.
Second half expected to be strong as international arrivals, incentives and conferences return; Oct-Mar cited as the peak international months.
Operating EBITDA margin expected to hold near Q1 levels (~41%) or grow marginally QoQ; management cites ~50% annual margin.
Srinagar and Bandhavgarh resorts expected Oct-Dec 2027; Jaisalmer and Leela Residences Mumbai on track for FY27 year-end; Agra, Ayodhya, Sikkim and Ranthambore in CY28; Tadoba in CY30.
FY30 target of INR20 bn EBITDA reiterated; ROCE to move from double-digit to mid-to-high teens over the coming years as new hotels stabilise.
Leverage comfort level of around 2.5x average net debt/EBITDA, with variation across quarters.
capex_capacity: Portfolio at 25 properties, 5,257 keys: 15 operational hotels and 10 in pipeline; roughly half of keys owned and half managed.
Tadoba (Maharashtra) concession signed with MTDC: 30 luxury keys on 62 acres, INR1,200 mn project, 60-year concession extendable by 30 years, targeted CY30; management cites 15-17% yield on cost.
Ranthambore: 400-year-old fortress wall stabilisation has delayed the project by about two quarters; management expects to catch up once complete.
Mumbai Residences: 63 keys; show-arounds from end-CY26, residents expected early CY27.

Bandhavgarh villa construction started; Srinagar walling and landscaping in progress; Agra piling under way; Ayodhya main piling to start mid-to-late August after test piling; Sikkim main block civil work started.
Coorg 19-key brownfield expansion to follow stabilisation of the operating asset.
Renewable energy share about 67%, targeted at 75%; renewable project planned at Coorg and Chennai to reduce fixed costs.
demand_pricing: International room revenue at the five owned palace hotels moved from a 10% YoY decline in March to a 1% YoY increase in June.
Domestic room revenue up 25% YoY at the five palace hotels; retail segment up more than 20%.
Leela website share of bookings is 16% (about 64% direct overall); management says direct acquisition costs about one-third of OTA cost.
Management said the international/domestic mix is roughly 50:50 and expects international to recover further in H2 FY27.
Occupancy of existing five palace hotels close to 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Are occupancies on track for mid-70s in FY27, given Q1 occupancy of 67%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an FY occupancy target. It pointed to balanced growth across city hotels (+14%) and resorts (+24%), and expects H2 international demand to add compression.

qa_highlights.question: Tadoba: underwritten ARR, occupancy and IRR? Could it open before CY30? Leverage cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tadoba is a value-accretive deal with 15-17% yield on cost, and the timeline reflects approvals and design for a wildlife trail. Net debt/LTM EBITDA is 1.6x, with an average comfort level of 2.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion timelines: have Bandhavgarh, Srinagar, Ayodhya and Agra slipped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slippage is about one quarter. Srinagar and Bandhavgarh are for CY27 (Oct-Dec for the latter), Jaisalmer and Leela Residences by year-end, and Ranthambore is delayed by about two quarters due to wall stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the HMA fee growth sustainable (run-rate around INR100 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HMA fees depend on performance, key-money-linked structures and ramp-up of new hotels, so quarterly growth will vary, but the trajectory is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 24% resort RevPAR growth beyond base effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to FIT share gains, repositioning (kids clubs, F&B, spa, Amber Terrace), and multi-generational and drive-to demand, with high double-digit growth in both Rajasthan resorts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainability of the EBITDA margin, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited renegotiated AMC and central procurement rates, revenue growth and renewable energy share. It guided to around 41% for the summer quarter, with about 50% for the full year.

risks_watch: International demand recovery: international room revenue at five palace hotels moved from -10% YoY in March to +1% in June; management expects H2 (Oct-Mar) to add compression, but West Asia conflict is not fully normalised.

Dubai JV: SPV accounting loss (asset-level interest and depreciation) drove a INR156 mn share-of-loss; Leela takes over operations in CY27 followed by about a year of renovation; residence sale plan assumes 2-3 years.

Margin durability: Q1 41% is a summer-quarter margin versus about 50% for the full year per management; guided to hold near 41% or grow marginally QoQ. Coorg is still ramping.
Leverage: net debt/LTM EBITDA 1.6x; management comfort level averages 2.5x, with variation across quarters, and debt-funded capex and acquisitions are contemplated.

So HMA is an ongoing business for us. The HMA contracts have various fee structures, incentive linked to performance and past key money commitments.

544408|2026-09.headline: Leela Palaces Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 36% to INR 1,877 million on 33% revenue growth; FY27 guidance kept at mid-to-high teens for H2.
544408|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose 33% YoY to INR 4,119 million, with every revenue stream growing above 20%. Operating EBITDA grew 36% to INR 1,877 million at a 46% margin (up 118 bps), and PAT rose 27% to INR 946 million. RevPAR grew 30% and the company said it outperformed the India luxury market (17% vs 13% for April to August). Management reiterated mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for H2 despite H1 running well ahead of guidance, and said the Mumbai BKC project needs incremental equity to buy the full FSI.

financial_highlights.change: from 1.6x in Mar 2026 and 3.7x in Mar 2025

segments.name: City hotels (H1)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 26% in H1 FY27; record H1 city occupancy of 74% vs 69% last year. Bengaluru, Chennai, Jaipur and Udaipur each grew at high double digits.

segments.name: Resorts (H1)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 18% in H1 FY27; same-store resort occupancy near 60%, with mid-50s blended including Coorg. Jaipur H1 occupancy above 60%.

segments.name: Owned domestic hotels (Q2)
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 30% with ADR up 30% to INR 25,046 and India headline occupancy of 69%. Domestic revenue at owned hotels grew more than 30%, and growth excluding Coorg was similar.

segments.name: Management fees
segments.commentary: Fees up 76% to INR 289 million; share of revenue rising from about 5% to 7%. Management said 85-90% of new managed-fee revenue flows to EBITDA.

segments.name: Dubai Palm Jumeirah JV (25% stake)
segments.commentary: Share of loss narrowed QoQ. The asset is EBITDA breakeven to positive; interest and depreciation keep it loss-making at PAT. Third-party operator runs it; renovation planned from around April 2027 for about 12 months.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 EBITDA growth guided at mid-to-high teens; management said H1 far exceeded the original mid-teens FY27 EBITDA guidance and the FY27 outcome should be much better than initially guided.
Management said Q3 is tracking ahead of pace with double-digit RevPAR growth expected; festive and long weekends in Oct-Nov support demand.
Corporate rate ask for CY27 is mid-to-high double digit; 60-70% of corporate static rates have moved to dynamic pricing.
Effective tax rate expected in the 20s% for FY27 after H1 at 16% of PBT (pre-JV share) due to Coorg deferred tax asset.
Target of over 5,200 keys by FY30 (about 2,600 owned, roughly 50:50 owned vs managed); FY30 EBITDA aspiration of INR 2,000 crore-odd cited on the call.
BKC Mumbai hotel commissioning reiterated for CY30; lease executed September 2026; Leela plans to seek shareholder approval for FSI purchase.
capex_capacity: Five contracted owned pipeline projects (Agra, Srinagar, Ayodhya, Ranthambore, Bandhavgarh) capex about INR 1,432 crore; INR 150 crore spent to date, about INR 450 crore by end FY27 and about INR 600 crore next year.

Openings: Jaisalmer and Leela Luxury Residences Mumbai in FY27 (residences first set of residents targeted in the last quarter of FY27); Arq Chennai to open this quarter; Srinagar and Bandhavgarh toward end of CY27; Agra, Ayodhya, Ranthambore and Sikkim in CY28; Tadoba around CY30.
More than 1,000 keys under development; 10 new openings across eight locations are contracted.

BKC Mumbai: 250-key Leela Palace plus 700k sq ft office, 50:50 JV with Brookfield; INR 800 crore committed capex (INR 400 crore equity, INR 400 crore debt) unchanged, though the FSI purchase could raise Leela's share above that.
Coorg (71 keys) rebranded as The Leela on 8 July 2026; EBITDA breakeven reached. Wellness itineraries launched recently.
demand_pricing: Suite occupancy up over 700 bps to mid-40s on paid basis; blended occupancy late 60s.
BRICS Summit boosted The Leela Palace New Delhi; management said the event was confined to Delhi and the ADR growth excluding it would still be high-teens.
Net Promoter Score 87 for H1 (about 13 points above the Asia-Pacific luxury average). RevPAR index rose to 1.46x from 1.41x; RevPAR premium about INR 4,500 over the luxury market.
Direct booking channel (brand website) rose to 15.1% of room revenue in H1 from 10.5% a year earlier.
International business low double-digit growth in Q2 excluding BRICS; management aims to return to a 50:50 India-to-international mix over time.
Dubai residences: 260-270 high-value transactions on Palm Jumeirah in recent months; sales timeline of 2-3 years unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the RevPAR outperformance sustainable, and when would occupancy be prioritised over ADR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited iconic, supply-constrained assets, NPS of 87, and broad-based growth with all segments up high double digits in rate and RevPAR. It said it has become more mindful on pricing but sees a long runway on ADR.

qa_highlights.question: Were FY27 EBITDA guidance and H2 growth rates being revised, given H1 EBITDA growth of about 38%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for H2 and said the full year would be well above the original mid-teens guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP impact on costs and the flow-through?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP expense started being booked from Q2, alongside headcount for new value drivers (Arq clubs, Azulian House) and the Coorg ramp-up. Excluding these, flow-through is about 60%. ESOP impact is slightly below INR 8 crore, though no exact figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the BKC capex rise from the INR 800 crore committed figure?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 800 crore committed capex is unchanged. Leela's share will rise to fund the FSI purchase, and this will be trued up when shareholder approval for the demerger/divestment is obtained.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ADR growth came from BRICS and other events?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BRICS impacted only the Delhi asset and that ADR growth excluding it would have been high-teens. It expects a major compression event each year (G20, India Energy Week, AI Impact Summit, BRICS).

qa_highlights.question: What are Coorg's revenue and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Coorg's ADR has roughly doubled versus the pre-branding period. The asset has reached EBITDA breakeven but no revenue or EBITDA figure was disclosed.

risks_watch: Dubai JV: ADRs still lagging on weak international demand; the asset goes into renovation around April 2027 for about 12 months, with EBITDA visibility only after rebranding.
BKC: material related-party transaction needing shareholder approval; office-stake divestment terms undetermined; funding may rise above the INR 800 crore committed capex.
Coorg still ramping; EBITDA at breakeven only.
Mid-to-high teens H2 guidance implies a sharp slowdown from the 36% Q2 EBITDA growth, against a high H2 base.
Dependence on compression events for ADR; the company says the BRICS effect was confined to Delhi.
Corporate rate renewals for CY27 are still under negotiation.
Effective tax rate guided to the 20s% in FY27, up from 16% in H1.

We delivered 30% RevPAR growth, 33% growth in operating revenue, and 36% growth in operating EBITDA; a second consecutive quarter of 35% plus EBITDA growth.
Excluding ESOP and excluding Coorg because Coorg is also stabilizing and it's not giving the EBITDA numbers as Jaipur and Udaipur, flow-through would be around 60% for the quarter.
We are very much on track for double-digit growth in terms of RevPAR in Q3 as well.

rows.why: Arq Chennai opening this quarter, Jaisalmer in FY27, Leela Luxury Residences Mumbai first residents targeted Q4 FY27, and Coorg rebranded as The Leela on 8 July 2026 with wellness itineraries recently launched.

rows.why: Corporate rate ask is mid-to-high double digit and 60-70% of corporate static rates have moved to dynamic pricing, but renewals are still under negotiation.

rows.why: Coorg (71 keys) rebranded as The Leela on 8 July 2026 and reached EBITDA breakeven with ADR roughly doubled, but no revenue or EBITDA figure disclosed.

544410|2026-03.headline: Prostarm Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 27% YoY to INR105 crore but fell 35% QoQ, with FY26 revenue at INR386 crore (+10%) as March billings slipped into Q1 FY27.
544410|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue of about INR105 crore grew 27% YoY but fell 35% QoQ, as project executions scheduled for March were deferred to Q1 FY27 due to West Asia-linked supply chain and gas-availability disruptions. EBITDA was about INR11 crore (down ~3% YoY) at a 10.43% margin, and PAT was about INR8 crore (up ~16% YoY) at a 7.56% margin. For FY26, revenue was INR386 crore (+10%), EBITDA margin fell 98 bps to 12%, and PAT was about INR33 crore (+14%). Working capital days rose to 185 from 68 as receivables reached about INR254 crore, mostly from one large project, and management guided to FY27 operating cash flow turning positive and FY27 revenue growth of at least 25%.

from INR64 crore and 68 days in FY25

segments.commentary: Core product made in two Pune facilities; Gujarat plant (1 kVA to 600 kVA UPS) now expected operational by Q2 FY27, delayed from Q1 FY27 by supply chain issues. Management expects UPS growth above 30-40% over the next two years.

segments.commentary: Navi Mumbai lithium battery pack facility is commercial; 1.20 GWh Jhajjar (Haryana) BESS plant is near commissioning, expected operational by end Q1 FY27, with a capex of about INR25 crore. segments.commentary: Management cites channel business of about INR100 crore per year (FY26: about INR107 crore). Services include installation, AMCs and rentals; EPC is executed for solar and BESS projects.

rows.why: FY27 capex of about INR100 crore is already planned, no new seamless capex is planned, and further capex is deferred to FY29-FY30 based on market conditions; seamless utilisation is guided ~70% in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called the 25% FY27 revenue guide conservative and will revisit it in H1 FY27, with upside from a BHEL win and data-centre welded demand.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Gas and raw-material cost pass-through

rows.label: BHEL tender for power-sector seamless tubes
