tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term growth story, normalisation and the 25% FY27 guide (called conservative), but withheld pricing, volumes, realisation, order-book split and peer comparison; analysts pushed on Q4 weakness, the delayed welded capex, the withdrawn acquisition and finance cost

544413|2026-03.headline: Digitide Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9.2% YoY to INR 800 crores, but adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores on wage code and accounting charges.
544413|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue reached INR 800 crores, up 2.5% QoQ and 9.2% YoY, with Tech and Digital at 31.1% of mix and international at 38.1%. EBITDA was INR 88 crores (11% margin), absorbing about INR 4 crores of one-time wage code impact. Adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores from INR 24 crores in Q3, mainly due to lease-accounting finance cost and a residual value policy change raising depreciation; reported PAT was INR (-5) crores after a INR 16 crores exceptional wage code charge. Management guided to 100 bps operating EBITDA margin expansion by exit FY27 and double-digit revenue growth, with early-to-mid teens cited.

segments.name: BPM
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 551 crores (+1.1% QoQ, +2.6% YoY); FY26 INR 2,170 crores, about 70% of revenue. EBITDA margin 16.3%, up 187 bps YoY.

segments.name: Tech and Digital
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 249 crores (+27.2% YoY); FY26 INR 910 crores, 29.6% of revenue (up 280 bps from 26.8%). EBITDA margin 12.1%, up 289 bps YoY.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 304 crores (+16.4% YoY), 38.1% of mix; FY26 mix 37.3%, up 180 bps. Healthcare (US) revenue crossed about USD 25 million in FY26.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit revenue growth in FY27-28; management quantified as early to mid-teens.
100 bps operating EBITDA margin expansion by exit of FY27 (Q4 FY27); mix (Tech and Digital and international) expected to contribute about 40% each, with operational efficiencies the rest.
FY31 target of INR 8,400 crores (USD 1 billion), of which about INR 1,700 crores inorganic; implies about 14-15% organic CAGR.
Healthcare expected at 12-15% of revenue by FY31 (USD 120-150 million); Tech and Digital at 40% and international at 50% of revenue by FY31.

Cash conversion baseline of about 70% of EBITDA; steady-state lease depreciation about INR 38-40 crores and PPE depreciation about INR 20 crores per year; management said at least one acquisition likely this year, with six targets evaluated and two at advanced stage.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 105 crores, mainly technology platforms, AI capabilities and IT and leasehold infrastructure.

Annual cash deployment roughly INR 100 crores: maintenance capex INR 70-80 crores, plus INR 15-20 crores for two large leasehold premises moving in FY26-27; balance accrues for internal growth and inorganic deals.
AI centres of excellence set up in Bengaluru and Coimbatore for a global P&C insurance client, with the deal running on Azure.
Management stated no plans to monetise physical assets; premises are largely leased, with one owned premises.
demand_pricing: Q4 TCV INR 620 crores, second consecutive quarter above INR 600 crores; FY26 TCV INR 2,355 crores.
About 15% of pipeline is hyperscaler-led (AWS, GCP, Microsoft); management linked part of the 27% Tech and Digital growth to hyperscaler deal conversion.
Top-10 customer revenue concentration fell about 200 bps; of FY26 incremental revenue of about INR 205 crores, about 45% came from new customers.
Healthcare: two new US provider-side deals won in Q1 FY27 (per management); positioned as revenue cycle management, revenue enablement and CX partner; compared with Sagility as not like-for-like.
Revenue per FTE up 11.4% YoY to INR 584k, supported by AI-led delivery and pyramid optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 growth in USD terms, and how much came from existing versus new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency growth was 5.2%. About INR 205 crores of incremental revenue was added, with roughly 45% from new customers and the rest from existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is the standalone Digitide business loss-making once Alldigi profits are excluded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; corporate costs sit in Digitide, including US and Canada sales leadership, and cost transfer pricing is applied, so standalone-versus-consolidated comparison is not like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: What is sustainable OCF conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 70% of EBITDA is the baseline; FY26's 77% was boosted by novation catch-up after the demerger, with Q1 FY26 at -36%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pipeline is hyperscaler-led and is it converting?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% of the pipeline is hyperscaler-led and contributions are now flowing through partners, with the Azure-based AI CoE deal cited.

qa_highlights.question: Will PulseNerve become a recurring platform or IP revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: PulseNerve is an orchestration layer enabling large AI service deals rather than a standalone platform; DocuSense, SmartPay and DigiCollect were cited as IP assets with non-linear revenue potential.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation run-rate and what does EBIT look like after the Q4 changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-time PPE depreciation charge is about INR 4 crores; steady-state lease depreciation is about INR 38-40 crores, with total depreciation around INR 60-62 crores, and the 100 bps margin guidance was reiterated. Net margin guidance was declined, with management pointing to an FY26 adjusted PAT margin of 2.3% as baseline.

risks_watch: Adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 crores in Q4 from INR 24 crores in Q3; management attributes this to lease and depreciation accounting, but the step-up in depreciation (Q4 INR 66 crores vs INR 49 crores a year earlier) and finance cost weigh on earnings.
Q4 EBITDA margin was flat at 11%, and management has pushed margin expansion timeline out; 100 bps expansion is now targeted by exit of FY27.
FY31 USD 1 billion target needs about 14-15% organic CAGR plus about INR 1,700 crores inorganic; inorganic progress and acquisition timing remain open.
Management declined to give a steady-state net profit margin, so analysts must derive it; reported PAT was INR (-5) crores in Q4 and INR 6 crores for FY26.
Watch whether DSO stays near 75 days and OCF conversion holds near 70% of EBITDA; watch hyperscaler pipeline conversion and healthcare wins.
544413|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and the FY27 outlook, but defensive and evasive on profitability: management repeatedly deflected questions on net margin, standalone profitability and EBIT, and framed Q4 weakness as accounting-driven.
key_quotes: What these numbers demonstrate is the absorptive capacity of our operational model.
We are looking at a strong 100-basis point expansion by the time we exit FY27.
Our normal target baseline for this is 70% conversion.
So, the 14% to 15% CAGR growth over the period is, we are very, very confident of that.

vs INR 24 crores in Q3 FY26
After INR 16 crores exceptional past service cost from wage code
Adjusted PAT margin 2.3% after INR 65 crores exceptional items

BPM +187 bps YoY; Tech and Digital +289 bps YoY

rows.why: Management guided ~100 bps operating EBITDA margin expansion by Q4 FY27 exit from 11% Q4 FY26 margin, with mix shift to Tech and Digital (29.6% of FY26 revenue, segment margin 12.1%) and international (38.1% of Q4 mix) plus efficiencies; Q4 EBITDA was flat QoQ at 11% after ~INR 4 cr wage code hit.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants or large capacity sized beyond two leasehold premises (INR 15-20 cr cash deployment, moving FY26-27) and AI CoEs already commissioned; utilisation not disclosed and management stated no plans to monetise physical assets.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides early-to-mid-teens revenue growth; FY26 revenue grew 7.1% (5.2% constant currency) and Q4 TCV of INR 620 cr (FY26 INR 2,355 cr) is the backing, with Q4 revenue +9.2% YoY to INR 800 cr.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Annual cash deployment guided at ~INR 100 cr (maintenance INR 70-80 cr plus INR 15-20 cr leasehold); FY26 capex INR 105 cr, and balance is earmarked for internal growth and inorganic deals, but no sized new growth capex was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was set as new (early-to-mid-teens growth, +100 bps margin by Q4 FY27) and FY26 constant-currency growth was only 5.2%, leaving little room to raise guidance soon.

rows.why: Margin timeline already pushed out to exit FY27, Q4 EBITDA flat at 11%, adjusted PAT fell to INR 11 cr from INR 24 cr in Q3, and depreciation rose to INR 66 cr from INR 49 cr YoY; net margin guidance was declined.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PulseNerve orchestration layer and DocuSense, SmartPay, DigiCollect IP assets cited with non-linear revenue potential, but no launch dates given; healthcare (US) crossed ~USD 25 mn in FY26 with two new US provider deals won in Q1 FY27.

rows.label: At least one acquisition in FY27
rows.why: Management said it is hopeful of at least one acquisition this year; six targets evaluated, two at advanced stage, and FY31 target needs ~INR 1,700 cr inorganic.

rows.label: Net cash build and cash conversion
rows.why: Net cash rose to INR 182 cr from INR 125 cr in Q3 and DSO fell to 75 days; management baseline is ~70% OCF/EBITDA versus 76.5% in FY26 (boosted by novation catch-up).

rows.label: Healthcare (US) scale-up
rows.why: Healthcare revenue crossed ~USD 25 mn in FY26 and two new US provider-side deals were won in Q1 FY27, with 12-15% of revenue targeted by FY31.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth (TCV INR 620 cr, early-to-mid-teens guide) and the 100 bps FY27 margin target, but evasive on net profitability, standalone economics and EBIT, deflecting those questions and framing Q4 weakness as accounting-driven; analysts pushed on margins and depreciation.

544413|2026-06.headline: Digitide Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5.3% YoY to INR775 crore but fell 3.1% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 9.9% and TCV bookings of INR205 crore.
544413|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR775 crore, up 5.3% YoY and down 3.1% QoQ, as management deliberately walked away from low-margin work and book-to-bill slipped. Reported EBITDA was INR76.9 crore (9.9% margin), down about INR11 crore QoQ, of which INR9.9 crore was a one-off lease-related item in Q4 and about INR10 crore was new wage costs under labour codes and state minimum wage revisions. Reported PAT was INR2.9 crore with no exceptionals, the first positive group PAT after two quarters. Management called Q1 the margin trough and reiterated a 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion for FY27, while de-emphasising the revenue target.

financial_highlights.change: Down about INR11 crore QoQ; like-to-like operating decline about INR1 crore
Up INR1 crore QoQ from INR21 crore
Positive after two quarters; no exceptional items

financial_highlights.value: INR55 crore (about INR36 crore ROU, INR19 crore owned/intangible)
financial_highlights.change: Normalised guidance INR55-57 crore per quarter

financial_highlights.value: INR15 crore (about INR11 crore lease interest)

segments.name: Tech and Digital
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR237 crore, 31% of total, growing 20.3% YoY. Management reports AI-led revenue of about INR15 crore (roughly 2% of revenue) from new AI projects; AI work inside BPM/T&D is not reported separately.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR296 crore, 38% of total, growing 10.2% YoY.

segments.name: BPM (India and West)
segments.commentary: Management describes it as margin-dilutive and resource-intensive in parts; deliberately selective on pursuits and repricing legacy contracts. Sequential decline cited by analysts; no segment revenue figure given in the call.

segments.name: Alldigi (standalone exclusion)
segments.commentary: Analyst cited standalone margin of about 5% excluding Alldigi; management said Q4 included dividend income not repeated in Q1. Management says Digitide standalone optics understate group profitability due to centrally held costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 200 bps reiterated; management says Q1 is the margin trough.
Lease cash outflows for FY27 guided at INR175-180 crore, unchanged.
Normalised D&A guided at INR55-57 crore per quarter.
Double-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance not reaffirmed; management asked investors to measure on profitability growth rather than revenue.
USD 1 billion revenue ambition by FY31 retained as 'North Star' but not to be pursued at expense of profitability; no revised percentage growth path given yet.
Headcount (about 55,000) expected to decline over the next few quarters.
M&A to be pursued as 2-3 targeted acquisitions rather than one large deal; management says equity dilution is not an option being considered.
capex_capacity: About 55,000 employees mapped to business units; headcount on a declining trend as Tech and Digital grows and productivity improves.

Four-part operating model: business units, service lines, two go-to-market forces (West: US and Canada; India Plus), and consolidated corporate functions with a new COO office alongside the CFO office.
Platforms: payroll, insurance and collections; AI and cloud professional services (six new clients signed in the quarter); about 5.7 million AI interactions at 80-85% containment.
AI funnel of INR100-150 crore being chased; management open to a separate AI business unit with its own P&L at a future date.
No immediate plan to monetise land and buildings, which management says are held for operating use.
Lease renewal in March quarter capitalised as right-of-use asset.
demand_pricing: TCV bookings INR205 crore vs management ambition, with book-to-bill of about 11-13% in the quarter.
Customers deferring some planned bookings and billing into Q2 and Q3.
Wage cost step-up of about INR10 crore per quarter from new labour codes and state minimum wage revisions effective 1 April; active client repricing and cost-of-living adjustment talks underway.
Three large international deals being shaped with hyperscalers.
Verticals prioritised: BFS (India and West), insurance (US mid-market), healthcare; small presence in oil and gas and CMT in the US.
Management says competition in insurance is intense; approach is curated qualification of RFPs, not catch-all.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone margin ex-Alldigi around 5%; what is the forward margin and how much of the ~INR500 crore quarterly book has converted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 standalone included dividend income not repeated in Q1, so the comparison is not like-for-like. Book-to-bill was 11-13% and some bookings slipped to Q2/Q3; some legacy contracts are being renegotiated.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR9,000 crore FY30/31 revenue target, including INR1,800 crore inorganic, be funded, and will there be dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will pursue build-partner-acquire, with two or three acquisitions rather than one large deal. Equity dilution is not an option the management team is pursuing; no land monetisation is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why has performance deteriorated since demerger and what verticals offer good margin growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management framed the period as Chapter 3 of the company, with strategy unchanged but execution, accountability and walking away from weak accounts emphasised. Tech and Digital tracks are payroll, insurance and collections platforms, AI and cloud services, and AI within BPM.

qa_highlights.question: Should Alldigi be merged, and will margins return to pre-demerger levels?
qa_highlights.answer: The board will decide on any legal merger at an appropriate time with no timeline. Management said Digitide's central costs and capabilities are interlocked with Alldigi and that the group should be viewed on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI-led revenue incremental or cannibalised, and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: AI revenue of about INR15 crore is net new from new and existing clients; the pipeline is INR100-150 crore across stages. Management is building dedicated AI sales and solutioning teams.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not reaffirm it. Its priority is margin improvement, and it asked investors to track profitability and ROE rather than revenue.

risks_watch: Book-to-bill of about 11-13% and TCV of INR205 crore below ambition; watch whether the deferred bookings land in Q2 and Q3 as management expects.
DSO at 82 days (up 7 days QoQ) with higher receivables and unbilled balances; Q2 focus is converting these to cash.
Wage cost step-up of about INR10 crore per quarter from labour codes and state minimum wage revisions; client repricing and cost-of-living talks are not yet concluded.
Margin path depends on repricing and exits of low-margin accounts; FY27 200 bps EBITDA expansion reiterated but no quarterly margin path given.
Alldigi-related governance: standalone profitability is weak excluding Alldigi, legal merger has no timeline, and central costs are only partly cross-charged.
Revenue growth guidance was not reaffirmed and the FY31 USD 1 billion target has no revised growth path; headcount expected to decline over the next couple of quarters.
key_quotes: We are not going to chase top line for its own sake.
We believe Q1 is the trough on margins, and we are working towards EBITDA margin expansion in FY27.
Revenue is not the only metric we are managing for this year.
We will not go and do one big acquisition.
As a management team, we do not see that as one of the options that we will execute, Aditya.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given; management said there is no immediate plan to monetise land and buildings, and M&A is planned as 2-3 targeted acquisitions rather than capex.

rows.why: Management did not reaffirm double-digit FY27 revenue growth and asked investors to track profitability rather than revenue, so no upgrade signal exists.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI funnel of INR100-150 crore is being chased with about INR15 crore AI revenue in Q1 and six new AI and cloud clients signed, and management is open to a separate AI business unit at a future date, but no specific product launch date was given.

rows.why: Customers are deferring some planned bookings and billing into Q2 and Q3, and three large hyperscaler deals are being shaped, but TCV of INR205 crore was below ambition in Q1.

rows.label: Headcount reduction and productivity
rows.why: Headcount of about 55,000 is guided to a declining trend as Tech and Digital grows and productivity improves, which supports margin recovery against the INR10 crore per quarter wage step-up.

rows.label: DSO normalisation
rows.why: DSO rose to 82 days from 75 QoQ (down from 91 YoY), and management says Q2 focus is converting receivables and unbilled balances to cash, but this is not yet delivered.

544414|2026-03.headline: Bluspring FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR 3,304 crore and Q4 EBITDA margin hit 4.2%, with STEAG and LSG acquisitions set to push margins toward 5%.
544414|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 8% YoY to INR 846 crore (flat QoQ) and EBITDA rose 44% YoY to INR 35 crore, with margin up 35 bps QoQ to 4.2%. Adjusted PAT (excluding the Q3 Labour Code one-off) grew 26-27% to INR 67 crore for FY26, and the company reported a net cash position of INR 15 crore at March 2026. Management signed definitive agreements to acquire STEAG Energy Services (India) and LSG Sky Chefs' Bengaluru operations, and guided to 15-16% organic growth in FY27. foundit showed its highest quarterly sales in six quarters (INR 26 crore) and narrowed EBITDA losses to INR 9 crore from INR 12 crore in Q3.

financial_highlights.change: +26-27% YoY, excludes Q3 Labour Code one-off

segments.name: Facility and Food Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 2,031 crore (+12% YoY); Q4 INR 519 crore (+10% YoY, flat QoQ). Q4 EBITDA INR 24 crore (+56% YoY), driven mainly by collections rather than volume; 24 new contracts with INR 124 crore ACV added.

segments.name: Telecom and Industrials
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 615 crore (+7% YoY) with telecom muted by delayed telecom capex; industrial sub-vertical grew 7% QoQ. Q4 revenue INR 157 crore; Q4 EBITDA INR 18 crore (+13% YoY, +19% QoQ); FY26 EBITDA INR 57 crore (+11% YoY).

segments.name: Security Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 659 crore (+14% YoY); Q4 INR 169 crore (+15% YoY, flat QoQ). Headcount crossed 24,000 after about 2,900 guard additions in FY26; FY26 EBITDA INR 19 crore (+23% YoY), Q4 EBITDA INR 6 crore.

segments.name: foundit (investment, shown separately)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 19 crore and sales INR 26 crore (vs average INR 17 crore in Q1-Q3 FY26). EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 9 crore in Q4 from INR 12 crore in Q3; management targets EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue growth guided at 15-16%, with organic EBITDA margin around 4%; Q1 is seasonally soft in food and telecom, so margin may dip below 4% before recovering from Q2.
STEAG (about INR 700 crore revenue, high-single-digit EBITDA margin, expected INR 60-65 crore EBITDA) to be consolidated from around end-May 2026; management says closing is expected within the week.
LSG Bengaluru (about INR 110 crore revenue, 17-18% operating margin, about INR 20 crore EBITDA) expected to close in 30-60 days from the call; consolidation for 8-9 months in FY27.

Combined acquisitions expected to add about INR 800 crore annualised revenue and about INR 80 crore EBITDA, taking EBITDA margin toward 5%; management expects PAT above INR 100 crore annualised, excluding foundit.

foundit targeted to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27 (Q4); management says the cost base supports breakeven at INR 34-35 crore revenue run rate, and it will consider monetising part of the stake.
Operating cash flow guided at 55-60% of operating EBITDA. Acquisition debt to be repaid aggressively after integration; funding via debt and internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Management says both acquired businesses are capex-light and does not foresee a large depreciation impact.
STEAG manages about 7 GW of power assets and 2,200 tph of process steam capacity, with over 2,000 employees.
LSG India Bengaluru holds in-flight catering facilities at Bengaluru airport under a concession running to 2039.
Bluspring workforce is above 93,000, up 6,600 during FY26.
demand_pricing: Q4 saw about 42 new contracts with ACV of INR 181 crore; FY26 total was 164 contracts with ACV of INR 459 crore.
Top 30 clients contribute less than 50% of revenue.
Margin gains attributed to new contracts at better margins, better collections and exiting low-margin clients; management says no further low-margin contracts remain to be exited.
Telecom revenue held back by delayed capex from leading telecom operators; industrial metals business gained new contracts at better margins.
Management says bankers and advisers, including big four diligence, drove the Q4 acquisition-related exceptional cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin reach a sustained 5% after STEAG consolidation, and when will both deals close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said internal estimates put margin in touching distance of 5%. STEAG was expected to close within the week, with consolidation from Q1; LSG was expected in 30-45 days.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15% organic growth realistic given FY26 ACV of about INR 450 crore and contract losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organic growth was about 15-16% in FY26 before lost contracts, some lost to competition and some exited for low margins. It said no further deliberate exits are planned and the sales team is now fully built, supporting 15-16% guidance for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan and funding guardrail for foundit?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term goal is EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27; parent funds the shortfall within visible limits. Management will consider monetising part of the stake, and in the medium term may become a minority investor, once breakeven is reached.

qa_highlights.question: Is STEAG's valuation (INR 180 crore EV, about INR 140 crore cash) sustainable given INR 65 crore EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said STEAG grew from INR 530 crore in FY24 to INR 600 crore in FY25 and INR 700 crore in FY26, with 3-5 year contracts giving about three years of visibility. The seller, a German group, is exiting India to focus on Europe.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pre-Ind AS impact on EBITDA and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR 10 crore of the INR 121 crore EBITDA is from Ind AS. The only PAT adjustments are the INR 29 crore Labour Code one-off in Q3 and the INR 6.8 crore acquisition cost in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will foundit reach EBITDA neutral and PAT positive, and is the INR 100 crore PAT target ex-foundit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR 100 crore PAT target excludes foundit and that breakeven is expected by Q4 FY27. It said PAT-positive operation for foundit would need a run rate of about INR 34-35 crore, with no further people or product investment needed.

risks_watch: Acquisition integration of STEAG and LSG, and delivery of the stated synergies and cross-sell.
Acquisition-related debt repayment pace and funding mix (debt plus internal accruals).
Telecom segment recovery depends on the timing of telecom operators' capex.
foundit: quarter-one seasonality, AI-disruption risk to the talent platform, ongoing parent funding and the monetisation route.
Q1 FY27 margin seasonality in food and telecom may pull margin below 4%.
Management says organic FY27 revenue growth of 15-16% exceeds FY26 ACV-implied growth (about 10-13%), so the target needs to be tested.

qa_highlights.question: How will management run the three divisions over the next two years, and what is the addressable market for STEAG-type contracts?

Management cites vendor consolidation, outsourcing (about two-thirds of FM still in-house) and GST/Labour Code formalisation. STEAG's large contracts are end-to-end outcome-based O&M, combining STEAG, Hofincons and the FM team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the foundit path to breakeven and how much more funding is needed?

FY27 cash burn guided at INR35-40 crores in one answer, versus INR30-35 crores in the prepared remarks. Breakeven needs quarterly sales above INR35-40 crores, with revenue recognised from subscriptions over a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did foundit sales of about INR10 crores more over two quarters not show up in revenue?

qa_highlights.question: What are the STEAG contract economics: FY27 revenue, margin and five-year sustainability after the initial term?

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and are there deposits for large deals?

544416|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 48% to INR304.41 crore and PAT 64% to INR22.2 crore (7.59% margin); Melt N Mellow hit 7% EBITDA ahead of plan.
544416|2026-03.overview: Krishival Foods reported FY26 revenue of INR304.41 crore (up 48% YoY), EBITDA of INR41.95 crore (margin 13.78%, up 66%) and PAT of INR22.2 crore (margin 7.59%, up 89 bps). The ice cream arm Melt N Mellow reached about 7% EBITDA on roughly INR95 crore of revenue, a year ahead of its FY27 plan. Management guided FY27 to about 50% top-line growth and 50%+ bottom-line growth. Q4 EBITDA margin looked weaker on a reported basis, which management attributed to seasonal nuts B2B pressure and a INR2.88 crore ESOP charge booked in ice cream; it said the adjusted Q4 margin was 12.21% vs 12.03% in Q4 FY25.

guidance_outlook: FY27: about 50% top-line growth and 50%+ bottom-line growth (company-level).
Nuts: maintain about 15%+ EBITDA and 10%+ PAT in the next two years; PAT to stay above 10% even as depreciation rises.
Ice cream: EBITDA to stay above 7% and rise; target 14-15% EBITDA about three years out once capacity is fully used; FY27 PAT above 3% (stated conservatively).

Ice cream share of total sales to keep rising in FY27; management expects nuts and ice cream to be roughly equal by FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: Nuts capacity raised from 10 to 20 metric tons per day of finished product; the new 35,000 sq ft unit began production in April 2026. Plan is 30 MT/day next year and 40 MT/day after that, within a 2 lakh sq ft Halkarni MIDC factory under construction.

Nuts utilisation: existing 10 MT/day capacity expected near 90% in FY27; new 10 MT/day capacity expected about 25% utilised in FY27, with a further 25-50% of the enhanced capacity to be used the year after.
Ice cream: deep freezer network expanded from about 3,000 to over 15,000 in FY26 and will keep growing in FY27.
Ice cream capacity of 1 lakh litres per day; utilisation about 25% in FY26.
demand_pricing: Melt N Mellow footprint: 34,200 retail outlets (up from about 25,000 at acquisition, per management's comment that it had 37,000 retail touchpoints later in the call), 189+ ice cream SKUs.

Management said nuts pricing power comes from Tier 2-4 distribution and in-house sourcing; it sees competition from large FMCG players (e.g., Tata Consumer) as a sign of a growing category, and said sourcing depth is a barrier for them.
Management described near-term input cost volatility for imported commodities but said it sees no structural impact on growth.

qa_highlights.question: When will the expanded nuts capacity reach peak utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nuts capacity is 20 MT/day now (from 10), with 25% utilisation of the new capacity in FY27 and the existing unit near 90%, and further steps to 30 and 40 MT/day over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and PAT margins for nuts at steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15%+ EBITDA and 10%+ PAT for the next two years, with EBITDA possibly rising a couple of points but PAT held at 10%+ despite higher depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 EBITDA margin fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 is seasonally weak for nuts (B2B wedding demand) and that a INR2.88 crore ESOP charge sat in ice cream; excluding it, Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin was 12.21% vs 12.03% in Q4 FY25. Management said FY27 ESOP cost would be below the FY26 level.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the consolidated raw material cost increase in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher ice cream volumes in Q4, which need more raw material and packaging (RMPM), with ice cream sales of about INR43 crore in Q4 versus about INR47 crore in the first nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Where is ice cream demand coming from and how will sales promotion costs evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is over 50% from Maharashtra, with Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Andhra Pradesh the other focus states; management said branding spend will be set as a percentage of sales and funded from rising EBITDA, with no sharp unplanned jump.

qa_highlights.question: How were IPO, preferential and rights issue funds deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: IPO proceeds of about INR20 crore and a preferential issue of about INR65 crore went into nuts working capital. Of the INR100 crore rights issue, INR35 crore was received in January 2026 (INR25 crore for Halkarni plant and machinery, INR10 crore for nuts working capital); the remaining INR65 crore is due in two calls in calendar 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What synergy did the company get from acquiring Melt N Mellow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the existing milk and raw material sourcing, the distributor network, complementary working-capital cycles against nuts, and founders' R&D depth; it said the ice cream retail network can be used to sell nuts over time.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had no comment on the matter and that the investors were shareholders; it said it had no involvement in any wrongdoing by investors who are not part of management.

544420|2026-09.headline: Raymond Realty Q2 FY27 total income rose 7% YoY to INR757 crore, EBITDA margin 15%, booking value up 111% YoY in H1 to INR1,602 crore.

Quarterly pre-sales nearly doubled with no new launches, and H1 booking value reached INR1,602 crore (+111% YoY) while collections rose 67% to INR682 crore in Q2. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% pre-sales growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin, 20% ROCE and 9-10% PAT margin, and dropped explicit revenue growth guidance. An ICICI Prudential AIF subsidiary investment of INR210 crore for the Mahim project and a INR400 crore promoter equity infusion were announced, with debt held near INR1,200 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Structured via OCPRS with economics of 40% capital, 5% turnover fee plus 50% of residual profit; coupon virtually zero and treated as equity. Promoter equity ~INR410 crore cited; management says equity raising was part of the annual plan.

qa_highlights.answer: No revenue guidance this year due to percentage-of-completion complexity; management said revenue would be in a similar range to 20%, with EBITDA growth of 20% and pre-sales growth of 20%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full-year figure will be in line with H1 run-rate (H1 interest cited at INR91 crore).

544421|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA of ~260m (30% margin) included ~46m of one-offs; adjusted ~304m (35%), with gases segment margin 40% in Q4 and 38.4% for FY26.

Core gases segment revenue grew 9% QoQ in Q4, and FY26 core gases revenue grew 14.2% over FY25, with reported growth held back by the delayed start of Uluberia 2. Argon prices recovered from Q3 lows but remain below 1H FY26 levels. Management framed FY27 as an execution year with a stronger capacity base, but gave no numeric guidance beyond a 20% revenue CAGR target over the next 2-3 years.

544425|2026-06.headline: AJC Jewel Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 124.69% YoY to Rs 101.38 crore; EBITDA margin 4.58% and PAT margin 2.35%.
544425|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached Rs 101.38 crore versus Rs 45.12 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of Rs 4.64 crore (from Rs 1.58 crore) and PAT of Rs 2.38 crore (from Rs 0.57 crore). Margins expanded, with EBITDA margin at 4.58% (from 3.5%) and PAT margin at 2.35% (from 1.26%). Management announced a proposed 80% stake acquisition in AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC, Sharjah, via a non-cash share swap valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore, though the Sharjah entity is not consolidated in Q1. Management guided FY27 standalone India revenue of Rs 450 crore and 50% CAGR for three years, on a volume basis. Many answers on utilisation, Esthara economics and FY28 targets were deferred to H1 results.

segments.name: India gold jewellery (core B2B, casting)
segments.commentary: Capacity 5 kg/day; utilisation about 25% (about 1.2 kg/day). Kerala accounts for 90-95% of revenue. Top 10 customers are about 50% of revenue; about 200 other customers make up the rest.

segments.name: Sharjah UAE (AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC)
segments.commentary: Gold jewellery capacity 3 kg/day at about 800 g/day (about 27% utilisation). Management cited PAT margin of about 4% and EBITDA margin of about 5%, in a tax-exempt free zone. Not consolidated in Q1; expected consolidation from Q3.

segments.name: Esthara Jewels (silver DTC)
segments.commentary: Three stores operational in Kerala; two more under fit-out, expected to open by end of next month. Silver capacity 8 kg/day with about 1 kg/day production. Management targets about Rs 20 lakh revenue per store per month; first store reportedly about Rs 15 lakh per month. Capex about Rs 4,000 per sq ft; opex about Rs 5-6 lakh per store; breakeven targeted within one year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone India revenue target of Rs 450 crore (management reiterated it is standalone India only; Sharjah additional).
Revenue growth of about 50% CAGR for the next three years, stated as based on volume growth; management said price effects would be added only if gold prices rise.
Current PAT margin of about 2.5% cited for the year.
Sharjah full-year contribution to be updated after H1 results; acquisition completion expected in 3-6 months subject to BSE and regulatory approvals.
Dilution to existing shareholders from the share swap estimated at about 7-8%, per management (uncertain).
Store count and three-year store plans to be updated post H1 results.
Q1 and Q2 seasonally moderate; Q3 and Q4 stronger on festivals and weddings.

Silver jewellery production started in India; capacity up to 8 kg/day, currently about 1 kg/day.
Sharjah: 3 kg/day installed gold capacity at about 800 g/day.

Design and innovation centre set up; about 20 in-house design staff; library of about 2.5 lakh designs on B2B portal.
demand_pricing: Added 12 independent jewellers in Q1, mainly mid and small Kerala retailers; no new corporate clients after Kalyan.
Management is targeting expansion beyond Kerala, with a marketing team in Chennai; international orders to be served via Sharjah.
Management said gold price moves will not affect margins because it hedges with suppliers and on MCX.
Launched 9-karat and 18-karat products; 18-karat is served to some customers for higher margin at lower caratage. Early response described as encouraging.
Management said no gold metal loan or advance gold loan business; no bullion trading in consolidated revenue.
Receivables growth well ahead of sales (3-year receivables CAGR about 51% vs sales 16%), attributed to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total value and rationale of the Sharjah acquisition, and what margins does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: 80% stake via share swap, valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore; Sharjah earns about 4% PAT and about 5% EBITDA, aided by free-zone tax exemption. Completion expected in 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 50% growth guidance based on, volume or price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume only; price changes would be added only if gold prices rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected utilisation for FY27/FY28 and revenue at 100% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No utilisation guidance given. Indicative values at 100%: India about Rs 7 crore/day and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day. FY27 India target is Rs 450 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables growth far ahead of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods, and said it will try to reduce debtors.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow from operations has been negative for six years; when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to make it positive in coming years, without a specific timeline; focus is on sales volume and growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a demand impact from the duty change talk and what is the Q2/Q3 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said duty changes have not affected the business historically; Q1 and Q2 are moderate, Q3 and Q4 stronger. No specific Q3 numbers given.

Esthara store economics (Rs 15 lakh per month first store, breakeven within one year) and store count plans to be updated post H1; promoter remuneration about 10-15% of FY26 PAT to be aligned with PAT going forward.

544429|2026-03.headline: HDB Financial Q4 FY26: PAT rose 16.6% QoQ to ₹751 crore, NIM expanded to 8.23% and Gross Stage 3 fell to 2.44%.
544429|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sequential improvement on profitability, margins and asset quality. Disbursements hit a record ₹19,922 crore (up 11.2% QoQ), but gross loan book growth was only 3.4% QoQ and 10.9% YoY. NIM rose 16 bps QoQ to 8.23%, helped by lower borrowing costs, while yield dipped 7-8 bps on product mix. Management said March went well and it has not yet seen level 2/3 impact from the West Asia conflict, which it flagged as a key monitorable.

financial_highlights.change: vs 8.09% in Q3 FY26, 7.55% in Q4 FY25
vs 41.6% in Q3 FY26, 42.9% in Q4 FY25
vs 2.81% at Dec 31, 2025 and at Mar 31, 2025 per Q&A

segments.name: Enterprise lending
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements grew ~27.9% QoQ and ~15.4% YoY. LAP+EBL book grew 3.8% QoQ on ~36% disbursement growth. Enterprise lending Stage 3 fell to 1.58% from 1.82% in Q3 and 1.79% a year ago.

segments.name: Asset finance (CV/CE)
segments.commentary: Book showed moderate growth in Q4. Gross Stage 3 moved 3.14% (Q4 FY25) to 4.3% (Q3 FY26) to 3.79% (Q4 FY26). FY26 disbursements declined ~3% per analyst; management is pushing used vehicles, with a 50:50 new/used target over four years.

segments.name: Consumer finance
segments.commentary: Book grew 5.3% QoQ and 19.4% YoY, led by consumer durables then auto loans. Stage 3 rose to 2.44% from 2.26% a year ago, but improved from Q3.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book doubled in FY26; disbursements grew 58.7% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth target: nominal GDP + 6-7% CAGR, with the three-year agenda; management declined to give specific numbers.
Credit cost to moderate to around 2.3% (+/- ) and be sustainable at that level over the medium term.
NIM to be maintained at 8% or above, described as non-negotiable in 2/3/5-year plans; Q4 was 8.23%.
FY27 opex-to-gross loan book expected around 3.7% (FY26 was ~3.8%); cost-to-income guided to a similar range.
Cost of borrowings expected to hold for at least the current quarter; the CP mix is low and bank loans are below 50% of borrowings.
Expects Q1 to be seasonally slower; comparisons should be made Q1 vs Q1, not Q1 vs Q4. Ambition is YoY disbursement growth of 18-20%, described as hopeful, not committed.
capex_capacity: Branch count at 1,730 across 1,161 towns and cities; 20-30 branches may be added or relocated, with consolidation into larger formats (600-800 sq ft to up to 4,000 sq ft).
Management said no square footage has been reduced in the last three quarters as a listed company.
DIY digital sourcing grew ~2.2x in FY26; management expects it to grow further (2x to 5x cited).
App downloads at 1.41 crore; 4.76 lakh daily active users.
Five large AI-powered initiatives underway; bot-based collections nudging covered over 50% of early-bucket customers needing a nudge in Q4, improving early-bucket collection efficiency by ~25 bps.
demand_pricing: Management says all product yields were held in Q4; the 7-8 bps yield decline was from product mix, with unsecured disbursement growth lagging. Yield should return with unsecured growth, staying within the 14%+ range.
Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY26 disbursements were ₹15,599 crore, ₹17,917 crore and ₹19,922 crore respectively.
Secured share of gross loans is 74%, up from the 72% level management has held historically.
Borrowing costs have risen across the market over the past month, per management; the company has no low-cost borrowings left to reset after the last tranche in Oct-Nov 2025.
Average exposure per customer is ~₹1.66 lakh; the retail book is 100% of the portfolio.
AUM mix is 38:38:24 (enterprise lending : asset finance : consumer finance), expected to move to roughly 38:37:25 in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in March and early April on the West Asia conflict, supply chains and CV operators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March went well and is reflected in the results; no level 2/3 impact seen so far. It remains a key monitorable, with a 15-20 day watch period.

qa_highlights.question: Were contingency or buffer provisions considered for MSME/SME stress?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific level 2/3 impact seen yet. Management said LAP and MSME challenges were resolved by the March quarter and the focus is now growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 35 bps QoQ fall in cost of funds and can it be sustained given market rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it held lending rates and worked on borrowing strategies; no low-cost borrowings remain to reset. Cost of funds should hold for the current quarter, though market rates have risen.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 1 PCR rise by 30 bps, and why did enterprise lending PCR fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Provisioning is refreshed quarterly on an automated ECL basis (fully automated this quarter) using PD, LGD and product mix. Management said there is no one-time item.

qa_highlights.question: Why did asset finance Stage 3 recover so quickly?
qa_highlights.answer: Recovery has been K-shaped: accounts challenged in Q1 recovered slowly, while newer slippages are recovering faster. Management pushed recoveries and flow-forward reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM be sustained at 8%+ and what about branch additions?
qa_highlights.answer: 8%+ NIM is non-negotiable in internal plans; Q4 was 8.23%. Branch count will change by 20-30 sites through consolidation and upsizing, with digital channels driving growth.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict, supply chain disruption and El Nino impact on CV and MSME repayments; management says it is too early to call second- and third-order effects.
Rising market borrowing costs (CP mix low, bank loans below 50%), which could pressure the 8%+ NIM.
Disbursement-to-book conversion: book growth of 3.4% QoQ and 10.9% YoY is still below the nominal GDP + 6-7% aspiration.
Asset finance Stage 3 at 3.79% and consumer finance Stage 3 at 2.44%; sustainability of the recovery and the used-vehicle push.
Write-off quantum for FY26 and Q4 was not disclosed on the call; to be provided offline.
Yield dilution from product mix until unsecured business loans regain growth.

rows.why: Used-vehicle push in asset finance targeting a 50:50 new/used mix over four years and DIY digital sourcing growing ~2.2x in FY26 (expected 2x to 5x) are ongoing initiatives, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.why: Bot-based nudging covered over 50% of early-bucket customers needing a nudge in Q4 and improved early-bucket collection efficiency by ~25 bps, with five large AI initiatives underway.

544429|2026-06.headline: HDB Financial Q1 FY27 PAT rose 38.3% YoY to ₹785 crores, a record, with Stage 3 down to 2.34% and NIM at 8.35%.
544429|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly profit of ₹785 crores (up 38.3% YoY, 4.6% QoQ) with ROA of 2.5% and ROE of 15%. Gross Stage 3 improved to 2.34% from 2.44% in March 2026 and 2.56% a year earlier, and credit cost held at 2.32% versus 2.35% in Q4. Loan book grew 11.3% YoY to ₹1,21,846 crores but only 2.8% QoQ, with Asset Finance and Business Loans still lagging. Management pushed growth recovery into Q2–Q3 and kept the 2.3% steady-state credit cost and 8%+ NIM framing without formal annual guidance.

segments.name: Enterprise Lending
segments.commentary: Q1 disbursements grew 14% YoY; LAP (LAP+ EBL) book grew 13.2% YoY but LAP growth is steadying at about 3–4%. Gold loan book doubled YoY, with about 500 branches enabled; Unsecured Business Loans disbursements began accelerating late in the quarter, while the book shrank marginally QoQ.

segments.name: Asset Finance
segments.commentary: Commercial vehicle book grew 10% YoY and construction equipment 8% YoY; disbursements remain the laggard. Management reduced high-value, low-return products (tractor trailers, high-end HCVs), and says Stage 3 improved sequentially.

segments.name: Consumer Finance
segments.commentary: Book grew 7.5% QoQ and 21% YoY; consumer durables grew over 50% YoY on compressor season demand, and auto loans grew 21% YoY. Auto is flagged as the area needing more growth.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; steady-state credit cost viewed at about 2.3%, with a possible decline only if the economy improves.
NIM expected to hold at 8%+ and focus remains 2.5% ROA on a consistent basis.
Business Loans book expected to turn positive QoQ from Q2 and show YoY growth from Q3; Q2 expected to be positive in direction.
Cost of funds expected to be range-bound in Q2; Q3 view deferred. Current ratio about 1.3x and CP book under 2%.
Asset Finance growth expected to pick up over the next three to four quarters, with July run rate improving if the trend holds.
Viral Shah's 18% growth question was not answered; management said it would revert closer to dates.
capex_capacity: Gold loans: about 500+ branches enabled; management says the existing network could roughly double gold loans over time, with the timing still under internal work.
Distribution footprint of about 1.6 lakh+ retail touchpoints across about 1,200 cities; relationships with 150+ consumer durable manufacturers.
Rural micro-finance run through a couple of hundred branches as a small pilot; management declined to say whether it would be shut down.
Customer franchise 23.9 million, up 18.6% YoY and 4.1% QoQ.
demand_pricing: Q1 disbursements ₹17,629 crores, up 16.2% YoY; gross loan book ₹1,21,846 crores, up 11.3% YoY and 2.8% QoQ; secured loans 73.9% of book.
May 2026 was the highest-ever volume for a large number of Asset Finance products management wants to grow.
Yields described as fairly constant; Q1 yield uptick attributed to product mix (consumer durables seasonality), not to pricing.
Competition: management declined to name who is taking up the Asset Finance segments it is vacating.
Fuel price increases of about 8–9% reportedly passed on in small doses; freight rates described as stable for its customer base.
ECLGS uptake described as work in progress and modest; eligibility requires working capital end-use.
Top 20 customers are about 0.3% of AUM, so the book is retail-weighted.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Asset Finance disbursement lagging and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Used CV build-out and product reprioritisation are largely done, and growth should show over the next few quarters; July run rate improvement was expected but not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year credit cost guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not guide; 2.3% is the steady-state view, with a possible decline only if economic conditions improve. Current metrics are comfortable, and check bounce for June–July was described as fine.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Business Loans, MFI and two-wheeler books shrinking QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: MFI is a small pilot. Business Loans initiatives from late March are taking time to spread across the network; the book is expected to turn positive from Q2 and grow from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Asset Finance Stage 3 level and can it fall toward 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is on a flat book; Stage 3 should fall as the book grows and as the economy improves, and it was steady so far in June-July.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cost-of-funds outlook and liquidity strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds expected to be range-bound in Q2; liquidity is supported by a current ratio of about 1.3x and CP under 2%, and Q3 guidance is deferred.

qa_highlights.question: Is the yield uptick in Q1 seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: The uptick is purely product mix, driven by the consumer durables compressor season; yields are otherwise stable, and the next peak is Dussehra-Diwali.

risks_watch: Credit cost: Q2 and monsoon/El Niño impact on collections, with Stage 2 accretion (about 40 bps this quarter) and early-bucket behaviour to monitor.
Business Loans and LAP growth shortfalls and whether Business Loans turns positive QoQ from Q2.
Asset Finance disbursement recovery and CV/CE volumes against the stated four-quarter ramp.
Cost of funds and liquidity for Q3, with management deferring the Q3 view.
Fuel-price pass-through and fleet-operator stress; management says exposure to large fleets is minimal.

544429|2026-09.headline: HDB Financial Q2 FY27 PAT rose 34% YoY to ₹780 crore, NIM 8.23%, Stage 3 down to 2.43%, with management guiding to a near-term 8.2%+ NIM.
544429|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed disbursements up 18.7% YoY to ₹18,522 crore and PAT up 34% YoY to ₹780 crore, with Stage 3 improving YoY to 2.43%. Gross loan book grew 11.7% YoY to ₹1,24,469 crore, which management described as slow relative to disbursements because of high repayments. Sequentially, NIM was 8.23% versus 8.35% in Q1, and credit cost rose to 2.37%, with Stage 2 build-up in Asset Finance (mainly used/new CV) flagged as seasonal. The 25 bps repo hike on October 7, 2026 is the main near-term margin variable; management expects a minor impact in Q3 and aims to hold NIM at 8.2%+ in the near term.

financial_highlights.change: vs 7.95% in Q2FY26 and 8.35% in Q1FY27
vs 40.7% in Q2FY26 and 39.9% in Q1FY27

segments.name: Enterprise Lending
segments.commentary: Disbursements grew 25.5% YoY; LAP+EBL (mortgage) disbursements up 30% YoY, LAP growing about 3-3.5% QoQ. Gold loan disbursements up over 60% YoY, unsecured business loans turned slightly positive QoQ (+0.2%) after six quarters.

segments.name: Asset Finance
segments.commentary: Commercial vehicle book up 8% YoY and construction equipment up 12% YoY. New CV is hitting budget, while used CV growth is weak and is being addressed through internal actions; CV and CE drove the Stage 2 build-up.

segments.name: Consumer Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements up over 25% YoY and book up 22% YoY. Consumer durables book up 49% YoY, auto loans up 22%, relationship personal loans up 16%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects NIM to hold in a narrow range, targeting at least 8.2%+ in the near term and 8%+ over the long term; minor impact expected in Q3 from the 25 bps repo hike.
Disbursement trajectory expected to rise, with Q3 better than Q2 and Q4 better than Q3; management hopes Q4 shows growth in the 17-18% range, though it did not commit to a number.
Medium-term credit cost target of 2.3% +/- range; Q2 credit cost of 2.37% described as a 5 bps uptick expected to reverse.
ROA target of 2.5%+ on an annualised basis in the short to medium term.
Cost ratio expected to improve modestly while AI investments continue; management said it will not let costs balloon.
Borrowing cost of 7.04% in Q2; NCDs being raised at about 8.2-8.25%.
capex_capacity: Customer franchise at 24.8 million, up about 2 million in the last six months.
Retailer and dealer touchpoints up about 10% to 1.65 lakh+; management says it has not reduced towns served.
Headcount reduced, attributed mainly to productivity gains from automation and workflow simplification.
AI-led customer onboarding started in consumer finance; over 1 in 5 early-bucket collection calls now handled by an AI bot.
Average ticket size about ₹4.6 million for LAP and ₹1.4 million for enterprise business loans; EBL offered in more than 800 cities.
demand_pricing: LAP is primarily floating, reset monthly via a published floating reference rate (updated on the 16th of each month); ALCO reviews repricing monthly and reprices if the change is substantial.
About 55-60% of bank borrowings are linked to repo; MCLR-linked borrowings are minimal. NCD rates are about 8.2-8.25%.
Management is making calibrated repricing decisions on fixed-rate assets, with risk-adjusted returns (RAROC) guiding product pricing.
Drought declared in some Maharashtra districts; tractor exposure described as small and no crop loans held. Management is monitoring food inflation risk.
Insurance commission regulation: FY26 insurance-related fee income about ₹455 crore, roughly 0.3% of RoA; the consultation paper impact is still being assessed with FIDC and IRDAI.

qa_highlights.question: Why did asset yields moderate QoQ despite strong consumer finance growth, and how will cost of funds and NIM trend if repo rises 75-100 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is seasonally about 10-12 bps higher on NIM. Management said NIM came in 1-2 bps above plan, excluding an extra day in Q2, and expects only a minor Q3 impact, with LAP floating-rate pass-through and Q3 product mix as offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Asset Finance growth weak, is the problem in new or used CV?
qa_highlights.answer: New CV is hitting budget; used CV is the issue, with a combination of internal challenges and weak market demand. Delinquencies in the older book have not yet come off.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the Stage 2 build-up in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to CV, and slightly to CE, as seasonal and expected to revert in the coming quarter. Management said the rise was 9 bps QoQ and that faster book growth would have shown about 2 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will drought and macro conditions in key states affect Asset Finance and the credit cost guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is monitoring impacts, with a small tractor exposure in drought-declared areas. Credit cost is managed within 2.3% +/-, and it could fall about 5 bps next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Asset Finance growth and FY28 growth, and the risk to NIM plus fee income from the insurance commission proposal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes growth will return to the industry median, citing capacity and network readiness; FY26 disbursement growth was 3%. On fees, the company is still assessing the proposal, with ₹455 crore of insurance-related income at stake.

risks_watch: NIM sensitivity to the repo hike: about 55-60% of bank borrowings are repo-linked, and NCD rates are about 8.2%, so the cost of funds could rise if the cycle continues.
Used CV growth and the older delinquent book remain unresolved; Stage 2 build-up in CV/CE needs to reverse next quarter.
Insurance commission regulation could affect fee income (about ₹455 crore in FY26).
Drought and uneven monsoon could affect rural asset quality and food inflation.
Disbursement growth must accelerate in Q3 and Q4 for the 17-18% growth target, while high repayments are holding loan book growth back.
key_quotes: We would want to hold on to where we are as at Q2, and really come up to an 8.2 %+ at least in the near term.
On the Used piece, we ha ve had certain challenges, and that's where we have taken certain actions internally, and we expect to see a turnaround as we go through over the coming months.
So, of course, there is impact of macros. We live in the Indian heartland only, not outside.
I am very hopeful that in Q3, when we speak, we start to turn around the corner on the Asset Finance quality as well.

544430|2026-03.headline: Sambhv Steel Tubes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 38% to INR685 crores and EBITDA 91% to INR92 crores, with record quarterly profit.
544430|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT for Q4 FY26, with EBITDA per ton at INR9,500 excluding sponge iron sales, helped by raw-material lag and firm HR coil prices. For FY26, sales volume rose 37% to 3,96,000 tons, revenue 60% to INR2,413 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR143 crores. Capex was raised: the Kesda stainless steel Phase 1 (3,60,000 tpa) is on track for Q4 FY27, plus an additional INR200 crores of brownfield and power/DFT projects. Management guided Q1 FY27 EBITDA per ton to INR7,500-8,000 and FY27 average to INR7,000-8,000.

financial_highlights.change: more than doubled; PAT margin 6% vs 3.8%

segments.commentary: Capacity to rise from 58,000 to 1,16,000 tpa on debottlenecking, with consent to operate expected the week of the call. Management said 300 series is only about 10-20% of mix near term; FY26 SS sales were about 49,000 tons on 1,69,000 tons of total production including intermediates.

segments.name: Carbon steel (ERW pipes/tubes and GP/coated pipes)
segments.commentary: FY26 value-added volumes were 3,56,000 tons, up 51%. DFT line adds 1,50,000 tpa of ERW capacity for about INR50 crores, taking total ERW/tubes capacity to 0.5 million tpa by Q4 FY27.

Target of about 2 million tpa finished capacity by 2030 (10 lakh tons MS pipes/tubes, 3 lakh tons coated, 7 lakh tons SS).

Phase 2 and Phase 3 at Kesda not yet defined; management expects another INR300-400 crores of capex by FY28 once Phase 1 execution is clear.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR930 crore capex is spent, how will it be funded, and what are the debt limits?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR300 crores spent, balance about INR630 crores with INR675 crores term loan planned for Kesda; the INR200 crores add-on is partly debt (max INR150 crores). Long-term debt capped at 1.5x net worth and 1.5x forward EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA per ton so high, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement at lower raw-material prices in Q3 was consumed in Q4 while HR coil prices rose; Q1 FY27 guided at INR7,500-8,000 and FY27 average at INR7,000-8,000.

qa_highlights.question: Is the stainless steel production versus sales gap explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Production of 1,69,000 tons includes about 60,000 tons of slabs and 59,000 tons of HR coil that were captively consumed; saleable CR coil sales were about 49,000 tons. HR to CR recovery is about 98%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI 1.2 benefit and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Thin-gauge CR coil PLI available till about 2030-31, capped at about INR200 crores or installed-capacity tonnage, at 13-15% of revenue depending on thickness and grade.

qa_highlights.question: What are Kesda's Phase 2 and 3 timelines and the 2030 aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 and 3 product mix not finalised; to be announced after Phase 1 utilisation is seen. 2030 target of 2 million tpa with 10-12% share in MS coil and pipes and SS flat products, and about 60% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the monsoon and Q1 demand look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a below-normal El Nino monsoon forecast, which could lift demand; Q1 and Q4 typically strong for steel, Q2 and Q3 seasonally weaker.

risks_watch: Sustainability of INR7,000-8,000 EBITDA per ton once HR coil and raw material prices normalise, given Q4 benefited from inventory lag and price spike.

544430|2026-06.headline: Sambhv Q1 FY27 revenue INR732 crore (+31% YoY), EBITDA INR100 crore, PAT INR56 crore; FY27 EBITDA/ton guided INR7,500-8,500.
544430|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the highest-ever quarter for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with revenue up 31%, EBITDA up 31% and PAT up 70% YoY. Sales volume rose 16% YoY and value-added volume rose 27%, with EBITDA per ton of about INR10,000 excluding sponge iron. The Kuthrel stainless CR coil debottlenecking doubled capacity to 116,000 tpa, and the Kesda greenfield project is guided for Q4 FY27 commissioning. FY27 margin guided at about 12% with a 1-2% standard deviation; PAT margin guided at about 6% with a 1% standard deviation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kesda Q4 FY27 timeline achievable through monsoon?

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the INR100 crore warrant issue?

qa_highlights.question: Why co-branding for stainless pipes instead of direct sales?

qa_highlights.question: Working capital needs and capex schedule?

544439|2026-06.headline: Crizac Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% YoY to INR2,012 million on adverse university mix; management now guides FY27 flat versus FY26.
544439|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR2,012 million, down 4% YoY and below the INR3,917 million of Q4 FY26, consistent with Q1 being the seasonal trough. Management attributed the decline to a less favourable university mix (fewer high-fee top-ranked university bonuses and slabs), not lower platform activity, as enrolments rose 15% YoY. EBITDA fell 7.6% YoY to INR600 million, with margin at 29.8% versus 31%, while PAT grew 2.9% to INR471 million. Management moved from earlier growth expectations to a flat FY27 outlook, citing flight disruption and rupee volatility expected to hit Q2, with pent-up demand expected in Q3 and Q4. It also announced a leadership change: Chairman Christopher Nagle stepped down as UK CEO and became Non-Executive Chairman of the Indian holding company, with Eric Wijmenga taking UK and Europe operations.

544441|2026-03.headline: Meta Infotech FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR270 crore but PAT fell to INR11 crore; management targets 4x PAT by FY29 with no numeric guidance.
544441|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described as an investment year: revenue grew 23% YoY to INR270 crore and H2 revenue grew 72% YoY to INR60 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR18 crore (FY25: INR25 crore) and PAT fell to INR11 crore (FY25: INR14 crore). Management attributed the squeeze to new hires, geographic expansion, 12 new vendor onboardings, a Thales-owned Imperva transition that cut professional services revenue from about INR8.5 crore to INR2 crore, and a forex loss on a large contract. The company set an aspirational target of up to 4x PAT by FY29 from FY26 levels, without numeric revenue or margin guidance. Order book stood at INR506 crore as of May 2026, about 1.9x FY26 revenue.

rows.why: The INR moved from about INR80-85 to INR88-89 per USD on the large deal, causing a loss of a couple of crore; contracts will now be signed on a Spot+2 basis.

tone.note: Management was confident on the three-year PAT plan, services growth of at least 25% and the INR506 crore order book, but defensive on FY26 margins, H2 product losses and cash flow, repeatedly citing compliance limits; analysts pressed on the FY27 numbers and the low-margin Zscaler deal.

544443|2026-03.headline: Travel Food Services Q4 system-wide sales grew 27.7% YoY to INR9 billion, while FY26 adjusted consolidated PAT rose 21.5% to INR4.5 billion on about 1% traffic growth.
544443|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a disruption-heavy year (India-Pakistan conflict, aircraft crash-related schedule cuts, FDTL crew rest curbs, Middle East conflict from March 2026) in which TFS airport passenger traffic grew only 1.2%. Despite this, system-wide sales grew 25.4% to INR32.1 billion, driven by 9.4% like-for-like growth and 13.1% net contract gains. Q4 saw gross margin of 87.3% (85.6% after a one-time reclassification) and EBITDA up 38.3%, but PAT growth was held to about 15% by a INR212 million litigation provision and a weaker JV contribution. Trade receivables rose to about INR2.64 billion at year-end on EATS ramp-up, which management expects to normalise by H1 FY27.

segments.name: Travel QSR
segments.commentary: About 55% of FY26 consolidated revenue; growth driven by throughput, menu engineering and value combos.

segments.name: Lounges
segments.commentary: About 41% of FY26 consolidated revenue; growth from premiumisation and dwell time. Kyra Lounge opened at Hong Kong International Airport and a Cochin lounge opened in the year.

segments.name: Management and other services
segments.commentary: About 4% of FY26 consolidated revenue.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin expected in the 80% to 83% range for FY27 overall, with some inflationary pressure from LPG prices linked to the Middle East conflict.
Capex averaging INR50 crore to INR60 crore a year, including FY27, mainly for unit mobilisation at Delhi, Cochin and upcoming Noida.
Receivables (about INR264 crore at year-end vs INR100-110 crore average) expected to normalise to 40-45 days by H1 FY27.
Management expects FY27 passenger traffic growth of around 5%, per public reports, with Q1 FY27 still affected by the war-like situation.
Annual dividend of INR10.25 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
Bhogapuram (Vizag) contract under GHL expected to add about seven outlets; Noida airport operations expected to start in the coming months.
capex_capacity: Pipeline of more than 50 outlets, all committed per management.
Network now covers 20 airports and more than 550 travel QSR outlets and lounges; 76 travel QSR units mobilised in FY26 (including Delhi, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Cochin, Navi Mumbai).
Noida airport on track to start operations in the coming months; two more airports in the works in the coming months.
International: Malaysia lounges expanded to three airports; second Hong Kong lounge opened in Q4; subsidiaries in Dubai and Indonesia.
Delhi T3 concession expired in February 2026; a six-month short-term extension was granted, and the company plans to bid through its JV GHL when it comes up.
demand_pricing: Passenger traffic at TFS airports grew 1.2% in FY26; Q4 was broadly flat YoY, with January up, February flat and March/April weaker on international traffic.
Management said domestic traffic was robust while international traffic fell nearly double digits in March-April, especially at southern airports and Goa.
Food inflation was about 3% to 5% in April per management; price hikes taken in line with inflation; key supplier contracts are annual.
Management said the mass-market credit card lounge access curbs are offset by premium cards growing more than 50%, with premium cardholders being frequent flyers.
Management expects LFL to be driven by about 7% to 10% passenger traffic plus about 7% to 10% from price and initiatives (combined).

qa_highlights.question: How is Q1 FY27 trading, given last year's Q1 was hit by India-Pakistan conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said January was strong, February was muted, March and April were weak on international traffic, and early May shows improving trends versus March and April.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic growth in FY27 and risk from Kolkata airport privatisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not guide numbers; cited 11 airports in the privatisation pipeline and said Kolkata's inclusion or state changes are not expected to alter the schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Can airport F&B pricing and energy costs be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Electric equipment is a large part of the cost base, giving a natural hedge; food inflation has been manageable, and price hikes follow inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Are airport concession fees rising and what is long-term economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Rentals are a normal portfolio negotiation with some going up and some down; management said nothing dramatically different is happening.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structural versus temporary Q4 EBITDA margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-off reclassification of INR78 million cost reduced gross margin to 85.6% in Q4; full-year gross margin excluding it is about 84%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise, and what drove the receivables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost rose due to a INR212 million litigation provision booked in full; receivables rose on EATS bank billing ramp-up and should normalise by H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state LFL breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: LFL is roughly passenger traffic (7% to 10% historically) plus 7% to 10% from price and initiatives, averaged over a year.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and interest in duty-free or retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stressed cash discipline, zero debt and ROCE of about 45%, and prioritised international lounges and expressway wayside amenities; no duty-free plans were mentioned.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and international traffic recovery; Gulf-bound and NRI travel remains weak.
Input cost pressure: LPG prices and food inflation impact on gross margin against the 80% to 83% range.
Receivables of about INR264 crore at year-end must normalise to 40-45 days by H1 FY27 as EATS scales.
Credit card lounge access restrictions from banks, a structural lounge risk.
Litigation provision of INR212 million, with the outcome still open; Delhi T3 concession extension expires after six months.
544443|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and bullish on long-term aviation growth, but cautious on near-term traffic, citing the Middle East conflict and international traffic weakness. Management was evasive on specific FY27 inorganic growth and gave no numeric revenue guidance.
key_quotes: FY26 has been a defining year for us. Not only as our first full year as a listed company, but at the same time, being one that has been marked by multiple disruptions
we do see the international lounge opportunity or lounges, particularly going through a very interesting, as you say, a development globally.
the premium cardholder is your frequent flyer.
So, we've made our business model quite robust , in terms of how we deal with these year -on-year, irrespective whatever the underlying reason is.

rows.why: 76 travel QSR units mobilised in FY26, Noida airport operations due in coming months, and a 50+ outlet pipeline management calls fully committed; network now 20 airports and 550+ outlets.
